Beneath the comic clashes lie regrets about choices made, opportunities lost, and the lives each woman imagines the other was allowed to live. As the sisters reckon with jealousy and wounded pride, they also begin to recognise the common history that neither success nor disappointment has erased.

The musical explores sisterhood, rivalry, and the longing to be seen for who one truly is. It asks whether reconciliation is possible when love has long been tangled with envy, and whether a shared past can become the beginning of a different future.

schneekonigin.en:
Gerda and Kai are inseparable childhood friends, living an ordinary, happy life until a fierce winter storm descends on their city. On the stormy evening, Gerda’s mother tells them of the Snow Queen, the mysterious ruler of snow and ice. Soon afterward, a splinter from a shattered magic mirror pierces Kai’s eye and heart, turning everything he once loved cold and ugly; he grows distant before disappearing, lured away into the Queen’s frozen realm. Certain that Kai has been taken, Gerda refuses to abandon him and sets out alone to bring him home.

Her search leads her beyond the familiar streets of her city and into a strange, shifting world where enchantment and danger coexist. Along the way, Gerda encounters an assortment of unusual figures and is drawn into situations she never could have imagined: eccentric strangers offer guidance, unexpected companions come to her aid, and a peculiar gang threatens to turn her journey into captivity. Each encounter tests her determination, but also helps her discover resources of courage and trust that she did not know she possessed.

Meanwhile, Kai is held in the Snow Queen’s icy domain, cut off from the warmth and friendship that once defined his life. The closer Gerda comes to him, the more urgent her mission becomes. The Snow Queen’s world is beautiful but merciless, a place in which cold can silence memory, affection, and hope. Gerda must press forward despite fear and uncertainty, relying on the help she has earned and on her refusal to accept that Kai is lost forever.

At last, Gerda reaches the heart of the frozen world and confronts the force that has separated them. Her journey becomes not merely a rescue, but a struggle to restore Kai’s ability to feel, remember, and choose love over the Queen’s icy power. Through steadfastness and compassion, Gerda breaks the hold of the frozen realm and brings Kai back from its grip.

The musical centres on friendship, loyalty, and the courage to keep going when the path is frightening. It contrasts coldness, isolation, and fear with warmth, empathy, and the transforming power of love.

weihnachten mit bibi and tina.en:
As Christmas approaches, Bibi and Tina return to Martinshof for a winter adventure filled with snow, music and mishaps. Eager to make the festive season unforgettable, the two best friends throw themselves into the preparations, turning the farm into a lively place of anticipation. Tina brings her practical warmth and love of animals to the task, while Bibi’s impatient enthusiasm—and her magic—make every plan more unpredictable.

What begins as an attempt to create the perfect Christmas celebration soon becomes a fast-moving journey through the wintry world around Martinshof. Bibi and Tina encounter surprises that test their organisation, courage and ability to listen to one another. Whenever a problem seems impossible, Bibi is tempted to solve it with a quick spell; yet magic does not always produce the neat result she expects. Instead, unexpected consequences and comic confusion make the friends reconsider what truly matters as Christmas draws closer.

Along the way, the girls rely on the people and animals around them, sharing songs, laughter and moments of uncertainty. Their adventure invites them to look beyond decorations and grand gestures: helping someone who needs support, repairing misunderstandings, and making space for everyone to belong become more important than any flawless celebration. As the pressure of the season builds, Bibi and Tina must combine Bibi’s extraordinary abilities with Tina’s steadiness and their shared trust. The festive atmosphere is repeatedly threatened by disorder, but every setback offers the pair a chance to act with greater care and generosity.

By the time Christmas arrives at Martinshof, the friends have transformed a chaotic season into a celebration shaped by cooperation and affection. The joy of the occasion comes not from magic alone, but from the community that gathers around them and the choices Bibi and Tina make for one another.

爱因斯坦 时间相对论.en:
The musical opens in darkness on the deck of a ship at night, where an ageing man stands alone, gazing out at the sea. A page approaches and hands him a violin—the instrument that has been his faithful companion at every decisive station of his life. As Albert Einstein begins to play, the years fall away and his memories rise around him: the boy captivated by how the world works, the rebellious student, the celebrated scientist and the ageing exile. Throughout, a silent dancer known only as “the Light” returns again and again to give visible shape to his thoughts and theories, drawing the audience into the way he imagined time, space and the nature of the universe.

His memories trace Albert’s early fascination with the hidden order of the world and his resistance to conventional authority. At the Zurich Polytechnic he refuses to accept learning by rote, searches for intellectual freedom, and forms relationships that shape both his work and his private life. His unsettled beginnings lead to the Patent Office in Bern, where routine employment cannot contain his imagination. There, amid friendships, arguments and flashes of insight, Albert develops ideas that overturn established assumptions about time, space and light. Recognition slowly follows, transforming the ignored young thinker into an international scientific figure.

Yet the ascent carries a personal cost. Albert’s devotion to ideas, his restlessness and the pressure of public renown strain the people closest to him. The story moves through the upheavals of Europe, from the old imperial world through war and political extremism, as Albert confronts the moral implications of scientific progress and the dangers gathering around him. Forced to leave Nazi Germany, he makes a new life in the United States and takes up a professorship at Princeton, while fame turns him into a public symbol as much as a man.

By the end, the ageing Einstein on the ship weighs what his lifetime of thought has changed and what it has cost him—he has transformed how humanity understands the universe, yet time cannot be reversed and the bonds broken along the way cannot be fully repaired. Left alone with the violin that has accompanied him through every stage of his life, he confronts the responsibility that comes with knowledge before his story draws to a close.

路德维希二世 国王归来.en:
Crowned King of Bavaria after the death of his father, Ludwig II longs to rule through beauty, peace and imagination rather than military power. Yet his ministers press him to accept the harsh logic of European politics, while his brother Otto is increasingly consumed by fearful visions. Ludwig finds fleeting happiness with his cousin, Empress Elisabeth of Austria—Sissi—whose affection offers him a glimpse of the freedom and tenderness he cannot claim openly. His devotion to art deepens when he becomes the patron and friend of Richard Wagner, seeing in the composer’s music the heroic, ideal world he wants to create.

But Ludwig’s dreams collide with public duty. War and political pressure leave Bavaria dependent on Prussia, while the King’s spending on Wagner, elaborate performances and increasingly ambitious castles alarms the court. A politically useful engagement to Sissi’s sister, Sophie, cannot solve his isolation: Sophie loves the photographer Edgar Hanfstaengl, and Ludwig himself cannot give her the devotion expected of a future husband. Wagner, too, proves unable to live up to Ludwig’s idealised image of artistic purity, leaving the King still more disillusioned.

Retreating from Munich and its intrigues, Ludwig creates private kingdoms of the imagination at Neuschwanstein and in his fantastical architectural projects. He surrounds himself with night journeys, theatrical spectacles and dreamlike visions in which mythic figures such as Lohengrin and Siegfried seem more real than his ministers. As debts mount, his advisers turn his solitude and eccentricity into evidence against him. Declared unfit to rule, Ludwig is stripped of his crown and taken toward Lake Starnberg, where his final passage remains shadowed by mystery.

The musical explores the conflict between artistic idealism and political reality, and the personal cost of refusing to live by society’s rules. It portrays Ludwig as a man seeking love, beauty and freedom while the world around him demands power, conformity and compromise.

le roi soleil.en:
Amid the Fronde rebellion, France is ruled in practice by Cardinal Mazarin and Queen Anne of Austria while the young Louis XIV is crowned at Reims yet denied real authority. The rebel Duke of Beaufort and his beloved Isabelle give voice to popular anger against the court, while Louis struggles to prove that he is more than a ceremonial king. He falls deeply in love with Marie Mancini, Mazarin’s niece, whose lack of royal birth makes their future politically impossible. Determined to demonstrate courage and independence, Louis joins his army in war despite Marie’s fears. When he is struck down by severe illness and presumed dead, the court begins to look toward his brother, Philippe—known as Monsieur—as a possible successor. Marie alone refuses to abandon him, keeping vigil until a doctor revives him.

Recovered and newly certain of his love, Louis asks Marie to marry him. Yet Anne, Mazarin, and the demands of state intervene: Marie is sent away, and Louis must marry the Spanish Infanta, Marie-Thérèse. Their separation leaves him wounded, but it also teaches him the price of kingship. After Mazarin’s death, Louis takes control of France and remakes himself as the Sun King. He gathers power around the splendour of Versailles, even as its luxury is sustained by heavy burdens on the people.

Louis seeks escape in pleasure and in his affair with the ambitious Madame de Montespan, with whom he has children. Court intrigue, scandal, the Poison Affair, and the shadow of the Man in the Iron Mask darken his reign. Eventually, Louis finds steadier affection in Françoise d’Aubigné, the Marquise de Maintenon, the governess of his children. Despite objections to her status, he marries her, achieving at last a private happiness that had been denied to him in youth.

The musical explores the conflict between personal love and the obligations of power. It traces Louis’s passage from controlled young monarch to absolute ruler, while questioning the human cost of grandeur, ambition, and public glory.

les souliers rouges the red shoes.en:
At the Paris Opera, Victor, a renowned choreographer, is haunted by shadowy forces that promise him renewed glory. Desperate to restore the theatre’s prestige, he undertakes an audacious production: The Red Shoes, a ballet surrounded by an ominous reputation. The spirits provide the means for its success—an exquisite pair of red shoes with the power to make their wearer a star. Their gift, however, carries a cruel condition: the woman chosen to wear them may attain fame, but she must renounce love.

Isabelle, a young dancer newly arrived in Paris, dreams of dancing at the Opera. Pure-hearted, ambitious, and seemingly destined for the stage, she is selected by the shoes themselves. Once she puts them on, her talent and presence transform the production. The Red Shoes becomes a triumph, and Isabelle rises from hopeful newcomer to celebrated principal dancer. Victor sees his risky bargain vindicated, yet he also understands that the supernatural forces behind the ballet will not allow success to come without a price.

While Isabelle’s fame grows, she meets Ben, a handsome young journalist. Their attraction quickly becomes love, offering Isabelle a life beyond rehearsal rooms, applause, and the demands of performance. But the romance places her directly in conflict with the shoes’ curse. The shadows surrounding the Opera exploit the couple’s feelings, turning love into the test that threatens both Isabelle and Victor’s hard-won triumph. Isabelle must confront an impossible choice between the artistic destiny the red shoes have granted her and the human happiness she finds with Ben. As the ballet’s acclaim reaches its height, the curse closes in, making clear that neither devotion to art nor devotion to love can remain untouched by its consequences.

The musical explores ambition, artistic obsession, and the seductive price of fame. It asks whether achievement is meaningful when it requires sacrificing love, freedom, and one’s own ability to choose.

茶花女.en:
In Paris, the celebrated courtesan Marguerite Gautier lives amid lavish parties, admirers, and expensive expectations, her signature camellias becoming an emblem of the fragile glamour that surrounds her. Though she is kept by wealthy men and accustomed to a life of luxury, her health is failing beneath the surface. Armand Duval, a sincere young man from a respectable family, has long admired Marguerite from afar. When they finally meet, his open devotion initially unsettles her: he cannot offer the wealth or protection of her patrons, but he offers a love untouched by bargain or status. Gradually, Marguerite allows herself to return it.

Armand urges her to leave Paris with him, and the pair withdraw to the countryside, where Marguerite experiences a brief, precious happiness in a quieter life. Yet the financial cost of abandoning her former world soon threatens their future. More devastatingly, Armand’s father visits Marguerite and appeals to her sense of duty. He warns that her relationship with Armand will stain the family name and imperil the prospects of Armand’s sister. Knowing that Armand would refuse to leave her if he understood the stakes, Marguerite agrees to sacrifice her happiness. She ends the relationship without revealing the true reason and returns to Paris.

Armand, convinced that she has discarded him for a richer protector, is humiliated and furious. At a public gathering he confronts Marguerite cruelly, making their private pain a spectacle. Isolated, burdened by debt, and weakened by illness, Marguerite loses the glittering world that once seemed to sustain her. Only her loyal maid Nanine remains close as her condition worsens. When the truth of Marguerite’s sacrifice finally reaches Armand, he returns to her, but reconciliation comes too late: Marguerite dies after their love has been broken by the very society that judged it.

The musical centres on love struggling against class, money, reputation, and social hypocrisy. It treats sacrifice as both an expression of devotion and a devastating consequence of a world that denies Marguerite dignity and freedom.

莫里哀.en:
In Paris in 1642, Jean-Baptiste Poquelin turns away from the secure royal post expected of him as the son of a master upholsterer. Drawn to the stage and to the actress Madeleine Béjart, he defies his father Jean Poquelin and helps found the Illustre Théâtre. Their dream quickly founders under debt; Jean-Baptiste, now calling himself Molière, is imprisoned as guarantor for the company’s losses. His father secures his release, and Molière, Madeleine, and their fellow actors leave Paris to survive by touring provincial towns and châteaux. Madeleine becomes his indispensable artistic partner, while Molière watches the people they encounter and begins to turn their follies into comedy. Their fortunes improve when Prince de Conti becomes the troupe’s patron, but Conti’s religious conversion ends that protection, sending the company back onto the road.

Molière eventually returns to Paris and wins the support of Monsieur, the King’s brother. Performing before Louis XIV, a solemn tragedy leaves the king unmoved, but Molière’s comic playing delights the Court and establishes his name. Competition, financial strain, and public attacks continue, until The Affected Ladies gives his company a decisive popular triumph—even as his father, who follows his son’s rise only from a distance, still cannot bring himself to be reconciled.

Success is complicated by Molière’s love for Armande Béjart, Madeleine’s daughter. They marry despite scandal and the hostility of his rivals. As his plays grow bolder—especially The School for Wives and Tartuffe—he answers criticism with satire, exposing hypocrisy among fashionable society and religious zealots. The devout party persuades the King to ban Tartuffe, but Molière refuses to yield. When political and religious circumstances change, the ban is lifted and the play becomes his greatest triumph, even as years of struggle and relentless work leave him exhausted.

The musical portrays artistic freedom as something earned through risk, failure, and persistence. It explores love’s shifting forms, the pressure of public judgment, and comedy’s power to confront hypocrisy.

tabaluga und lilli.en:
In a world threatened by the spreading cold of ice, the young dragon Tabaluga is expected to carry on the work of the dragons, whose fire has long protected all living things. His father, the old dragon Tyrion, knows that the enemy is Arktos, a merciless snowman determined to freeze the world completely. To oppose him, Tabaluga must discover the True Fire—the power that can end Arktos’s reign. Guided by a Magician, Tabaluga leaves the safety of home and begins a journey through a strange, vivid world. He encounters danger in the form of Tarantula, the Spider Woman, but also finds wonder and beauty in the creatures and landscapes along his path. Each encounter teaches him that life contains darkness as well as joy, and that the imperfect world around him is nevertheless worth defending.

Arktos recognises that Tabaluga’s quest is a threat to his plans. Rather than confronting the dragon only through force, he creates Lilli, a beautiful girl made of pure ice. Her assigned task is simple: make Tabaluga fall in love, distract him from the True Fire, and leave him powerless against Arktos. The scheme succeeds at first. Tabaluga is captivated by Lilli, while Lilli herself begins to change as she experiences feelings beyond the purpose for which she was made. Their relationship places Tabaluga between his duty to save the world and the tenderness he feels for someone who seems to belong to his enemy.

As the conflict deepens, Tyrion dies protecting his son. Devastated by grief, Tabaluga nearly abandons his mission, convinced that his life and purpose have lost their meaning. Yet through his love for Lilli, he finally understands what the True Fire truly is. Love awakens the strength within him, breaks Arktos’s power over ice, and enables Tabaluga to face the darkness threatening the world.

The musical explores the journey from innocence to responsibility, and the courage required to confront loss and fear. Its central idea is that love—not force alone—can transform both individuals and the world around them.

wahnsinn.en:
In the Ruhr district, a set of intersecting relationships begins at Whisky Bill, a neighbourhood pub where the young band Screamers is beginning to attract attention. Its frontman, Tobi, dreams of a life in music and is instantly drawn to Gianna, an independent, spirited young woman in the audience. Their chemistry is unmistakable, but Gianna sees Tobi’s ambitions as more than a romantic adventure: she wants a future with substance, while he is tempted by the freedom and possibility promised by success. Their burgeoning relationship is shadowed by the troubled marriage of Tobi’s parents, Gabi and Karsten. Gabi has long made peace with an ordinary, stable life, but Tobi’s determination to perform reawakens Karsten’s own abandoned musical aspirations—and his fear that he has settled for too little.

Another couple, Sabine and Peter, are at a breaking point. Peter, a haulier whose work keeps him away for long stretches, has forgotten their twentieth wedding anniversary, and Sabine—longing to travel and to feel truly seen—sets off alone for a yoga holiday on the sunny island of Bahia del Sol. Tobi and Gianna, meanwhile, pile into a battered old red VW Beetle to reach a music festival on that same island; when it breaks down on the road, they are picked up by Peter, who is chasing after his wife. Furious that his son has abandoned a steady apprenticeship, Karsten follows too, with Gabi at his side urging him to back Tobi rather than relive his own regrets. And Wolf, the lonely owner of Whisky Bill and Peter’s closest friend, has never let go of Jessica, the woman he loved in the 1980s—when the whole ragtag party finally reaches the island hotel, he comes face to face with her at last, and a long-buried misunderstanding surfaces. As old hopes, missed chances and fresh infatuations collide, each person must decide whether to cling to fantasy, speak honestly, forgive, or walk away. Tobi confronts the cost of pursuing his dream; Karsten faces the disappointments he has projected onto his son; and Peter, Sabine and Wolf are forced to reckon with the longings and regrets they have kept buried. The intertwined stories move toward reconciliation not as an easy escape from hurt, but as a choice to face it openly.

At its heart, the show explores love in its exhilarating beginnings, painful losses and difficult acts of forgiveness. It sets youthful ambition against middle-aged regret, asking whether people can reclaim hope without denying the consequences of their choices.

wir sind am leben.en:
In Berlin in 1990, the fall of the Wall has opened a thrilling but unstable new world. Nina Fröhlich, who escaped Wittenberg before the political change, has made a tentative home in the capital. Her brother Mario follows her there, leaving their mother Rosie behind and hoping to find freedom, music, love, and a life that feels like his own. They arrive at Konsum Hoffnung, a squatted old building in Friedrichshain whose residents have turned it into a makeshift refuge for outsiders. Alongside its communal household, Konsum Hoffnung operates an improvised helpline for people who have nowhere else to turn.

Nina tries to turn her ambition into a pop career, even as Berlin’s restless nightlife is increasingly captivated by techno. Mario finds the emotional connection he has been seeking when he falls for Nando, a Cuban dancer. Around them, the building’s residents form a chosen family: a fragile, exuberant community holding one another up while the city reinvents itself outside their doors. Yet their sanctuary cannot shut out the tensions of the wider world, nor the fears that accompany liberation.

Rosie then arrives unexpectedly, carrying a suitcase, old wounds, and an urgent need to repair her broken relationship with her children. Her presence disrupts the life Nina and Mario have built without her. Determined to reclaim a place in their lives, she is drawn into the noisy, demanding, exhilarating Berlin they now call home. As personal dreams, romantic hopes, and family resentments collide, each member of the household must confront what a new beginning really costs. The joy of the era is shadowed by the AIDS crisis, forcing the community to face vulnerability, loss, and the necessity of caring for one another.

The musical explores reinvention after upheaval, the pull between biological family and chosen family, and the courage to live openly. It balances the exhilaration of freedom and creativity with grief, uncertainty, love, and mutual care.

die weihnachtsbackerei.en:
Snow keeps Jonas, Paula, and Emily’s parents from returning home on the eve of their grandparents’ visit, leaving the three siblings and their dog, Muffin, in charge of preparing the family’s Christmas bakery. Determined to create a festive surprise despite the adults’ absence, the children set out to bake cookies themselves. Their confidence quickly gives way to alarm: the refrigerator is empty, the essential recipe has disappeared, and there is no money in the house to buy what they need. With time running short, each obstacle turns the simple plan into a Christmas adventure.

The siblings search their home for clues, ingredients, and possible solutions while trying to keep Muffin out of further trouble. Their efforts lead them beyond the kitchen and into encounters with the people around them, including the formidable neighbour Mrs Schnitzenbacher, whose role in the children’s predicament is not immediately clear. The children must decide whom they can trust, how to ask for help, and whether they can turn small resources into enough ingredients for a real Christmas baking day. Along the way, disagreements and setbacks test their patience with one another, but the need to welcome their grandparents gives them a shared purpose.

As the snowstorm continues and the hoped-for celebration seems increasingly impossible, Jonas, Paula, and Emily learn to improvise. They combine their different ideas, face the consequences of their mistakes, and discover that the most important part of the bakery is not a perfect recipe or a full cupboard. By the time the family gathering draws near, their efforts have transformed a potentially lonely evening into a warm, communal celebration shaped by courage, cooperation, and unexpected kindness.

The show centres on family, resourcefulness, and the joy of creating something together. It suggests that Christmas spirit grows through generosity, perseverance, and making room for others—even when plans go wrong.

9 to 5.en:
At Consolidated Industries, three very different women endure the daily humiliations inflicted by their boss, Franklin Hart, Jr. Violet Newstead is the capable senior supervisor repeatedly denied the promotion she has earned; Doralee Rhodes is Hart’s warm, sharp secretary, falsely targeted by gossip because Hart boasts that she is his lover; and Judy Bernly is a newly separated woman struggling through her first office job. When Hart promotes a less-qualified man over Violet and Doralee discovers the extent of his lies, the three women finally unite.

After sharing their fantasies of getting revenge, their joking takes a dangerous turn when Violet accidentally poisons Hart’s coffee. Hart survives, realizes what has happened, and tries to use the incident to intimidate them. The women, however, seize the advantage: Doralee restrains him, and the trio confines Hart in his own home while his wife is away. They tell the office that he is unavailable and take charge of Consolidated themselves.

With Violet leading, Judy gaining confidence, and Doralee refusing to be underestimated, the women transform the company into a more humane and productive workplace. They introduce practical changes that improve employees’ lives, including flexible hours, job-sharing, childcare support, and better treatment for staff. Violet also begins a tentative romance with Joe, the considerate junior accountant, while Judy grows beyond the dependence and insecurity left by her marriage. Meanwhile, Hart’s devoted assistant, Roz Keith, becomes increasingly suspicious of his disappearance.

The trio uncovers evidence that Hart has been embezzling from the company, but their plan is threatened when he escapes and returns to the office. Before he can expose them, however, Chairman Russell Tinsworthy arrives to congratulate Consolidated on its dramatically improved results. Hart’s misconduct is revealed, and Tinsworthy sends him to run the company’s remote Bolivian branch. Violet is promoted to lead the company, while Judy, Doralee, and their colleagues celebrate a workplace remade on fairer terms.

all shook up.en:
In a quiet Midwestern town in 1955, rules govern nearly every pleasure. Mayor Matilda Hyde and her watchful Sheriff Earl enforce the Mamie Eisenhower Decency Act, banning loud music, dancing, public affection, and anything else they deem improper. Into this stifled community rides Chad, a charismatic, leather-jacketed guitarist newly released from jail. When his motorcycle breaks down, Natalie Haller, the town’s gifted young mechanic, offers to repair it—and falls instantly in love with him. Natalie’s devoted best friend, Dennis, quietly wishes she would notice that he loves her instead.

Chad’s arrival energizes the town, especially Sylvia’s Honky-Tonk, run by the outspoken Sylvia. Chad sets his sights on Miss Sandra, the clever, cultured curator of the local museum, though she finds his swagger irritating. Natalie, convinced that Chad cannot see her as anything but a friend, disguises herself as a young man named Ed. As Ed, she becomes Chad’s confidant and helps him try to win Miss Sandra. The plan produces a tangle of misplaced affections: Miss Sandra finds herself drawn to Ed; Chad is unsettled by his growing attraction to Ed; and Natalie must hide both her identity and her heartbreak.

Elsewhere, Sylvia’s daughter Lorraine and Matilda’s obedient son Dean fall in love. Their relationship defies Matilda’s expectations, and Dean begins to challenge the rigid life his mother has imposed on him. Sylvia, meanwhile, longs for Natalie’s widowed father, Jim Haller, who is pursuing Miss Sandra. As the town prepares for a celebration at the fairgrounds, romance, rebellion, and deception collide. Natalie’s identity is revealed, Chad recognizes where his true feelings lie, and the various lovers finally confront what they want. Matilda’s authority weakens as the townspeople reject fear and repression in favor of music, connection, and joy.

The show celebrates the freeing force of love, music, and self-expression. It also explores how people grow when they resist prejudice, rigid social rules, and the roles others assign to them.

bat out of hell 50th anniversary.en:
In the ruined, authoritarian city of Obsidian, Strat leads The Lost, a band of young rebels whose bodies have been permanently frozen at eighteen. They live beneath the streets in abandoned tunnels and resist Falco, the city’s powerful ruler, whose private forces seek to clear them out. Falco’s daughter Raven, nearing adulthood, is kept secluded in Falco Towers: protected, controlled and desperate to discover a life beyond her father’s carefully guarded world.

When Strat encounters Raven, their immediate attraction becomes a dangerous act of defiance. Raven is drawn to the freedom, risk and intensity of Strat’s underground world, while Strat sees in her someone who might choose him despite the divide between them. But their future carries an unavoidable imbalance: Raven will continue to grow older, whereas Strat and the other Lost can never move beyond eighteen. Their romance also unsettles The Lost. Tink, who loves Strat, cannot hide his jealousy, while Zahara and Jagwire contend with their own frustrated devotion and conflict.

Falco responds to Raven’s rebellion with escalating force. His determination to destroy The Lost’s refuge and keep his daughter under his authority drives Raven further away, and exposes the strain within his marriage to Sloane. Sloane, increasingly disillusioned with the man Falco has become, recognises in Raven’s longing a need for escape that she has denied in herself. As Falco’s campaign closes in, Strat and Raven attempt to hold onto their connection amid betrayals, abductions, violence and a catastrophic confrontation.

The conflict ultimately forces each character to choose between possession and love, safety and freedom, or permanence and change. Raven’s decision to leave transforms the struggle from a forbidden romance into a reckoning for Falco, Sloane, Strat and The Lost.

The show explores youthful rebellion, oppressive control and the pain of loving someone whom time will inevitably change. It asks whether love can survive the demands to remain young, to let go, and to allow another person to be free.

bear grease.en:
Danny and Sandy meet at a summer powwow and fall quickly into a tender romance, promising to find one another again at the following year’s gathering. When Sandy unexpectedly arrives at their school, she assumes their connection will continue. Danny, however, is determined to preserve his status with the Thunderbirds and pretends that their summer relationship meant little to him. Hurt and disoriented in an unfamiliar social world, Sandy is taken in by the Pink Aunties, a close-knit group led by the sharp-tongued but protective Rezzo. Around them, their classmates trade jokes, rivalries, crushes, gossip, and bravado as school life unfolds through powwow-inflected music, dance, and contemporary Indigenous humour.

Danny’s performance of indifference creates a widening rift between him and Sandy. His friends—including Canuckie, Sonny Boy, Roger, and Butta—encourage the swaggering image he believes he must maintain, while Sandy learns that fitting in need not mean surrendering her self-respect. The Pink Aunties—alongside Jan, Marty, and Foxy—offer companionship, perspective, and a counterweight to the boys’ posturing. Rezzo, whose own hard-edged confidence conceals vulnerability, becomes a particularly important presence in the group’s shifting relationships.

As public rituals, parties, performances, and competitive displays bring the students together, Danny is forced to confront the cost of treating Sandy as an embarrassment. The story’s comic set pieces and heightened musical numbers repeatedly expose how easily young people mistake image for identity. By the climax, Danny chooses to stop hiding behind the expectations of the Thunderbirds and openly claims the love he had denied. Sandy meets that change on her own terms, and the two are reunited amid a communal celebration that gathers the school’s cliques into one exuberant final moment.

The show’s central themes are belonging, self-respect, and the courage to be openly affectionate rather than perform toughness for one’s peers. It celebrates Indigenous community, language, humour, dance, and musical expression while treating teenage romance as part of a larger collective life.

buddy holly story.en:
In Lubbock, Texas, Buddy Holly is determined to move beyond the country music expected of him and create a sharper, more urgent sound. With bassist Joe B. Mauldin and drummer Jerry Allison, he forms The Crickets and begins chasing a recording career despite the doubts of local gatekeepers. A disappointing Nashville session makes clear that Buddy will not compromise: he leaves rather than abandon rock ’n’ roll. The trio finds a more sympathetic ally in producer Norman Petty at his studio in Clovis, New Mexico, where Buddy’s songwriting, restless experimentation, and distinctive guitar style turn The Crickets into a rising sensation.

Success brings the band to New York, where Buddy meets Maria Elena. Their courtship moves quickly from attraction to marriage, while Buddy’s records climb and his reputation spreads. The Crickets face another test when they are booked at Harlem’s Apollo Theater: the management expects a Black act and fears how the audience will respond to three white musicians from Texas. Buddy refuses to retreat, and the band’s performance wins the room over. Yet acclaim also creates strain. Joe and Jerry grow tired of being treated as supporting players and long to return home, while Buddy believes he must remain in New York and keep pushing forward. They part, leaving Buddy to face a new stage of his career alone.

As Buddy continues writing and recording, he joins the demanding Winter Dance Party tour across the Midwest. Exhaustion, bad weather, and failing transport intensify the pressure. At Clear Lake, Iowa, after a final high-energy concert at the Surf Ballroom, Buddy arranges a small plane to reach the next engagement. Ritchie Valens and The Big Bopper take the remaining seats. The flight departs into the night, ending the story abruptly in tragedy.

The musical explores ambition, artistic independence, friendship, love, and the exhilarating force of a new musical voice. It also sets Buddy’s joyful creative momentum against the fragility of fame and a life cut suddenly short.

bugsy malone.en:
In 1929 New York, smooth-talking former boxer Bugsy Malone guides the audience through a neighbourhood shaken by gang warfare. Dandy Dan’s men have “splurged” Roxy Robinson, a valued member of Fat Sam’s outfit, using a new rapid-fire weapon that covers its victims in cream. At Fat Sam’s Grand Slam Speakeasy, the flamboyant boss vows retaliation, but his ageing arsenal of custard pies leaves him badly outmatched. His singer and girlfriend, Tallulah, is unhappy to find Bugsy back in her orbit, while Bugsy’s attention has already been caught by Blousey Brown, an ambitious young performer determined to get to Hollywood.

When Dandy Dan’s gang attacks the Grand Slam, Bugsy becomes caught between romance and the criminal feud. He wants to help Blousey realise her dream, promising to accompany her to Hollywood, yet he also agrees to work for Fat Sam. After proving resourceful during an attempted hit on Sam, Bugsy is drawn deeper into the boss’s collapsing empire. Fat Sam sends him to recruit the formidable Leroy Smith, and Bugsy eventually helps secure a shipment of Dandy Dan’s coveted splurge guns. But the work repeatedly derails his plans with Blousey. When he fails to meet her as promised, she leaves for Hollywood alone, convinced that Bugsy has chosen the gangsters’ world over her.

With Fat Sam newly armed, the Grand Slam seems ready to withstand Dandy Dan. Instead, Dandy Dan arrives with his mob for a final assault. The speakeasy erupts into a comic battle of splurge guns, custard pies, flour bombs, and frantic double-crosses, until both gangs are left thoroughly defeated and covered in mess. In the aftermath, Bugsy and Blousey reunite, and the feud between Fat Sam and Dandy Dan finally comes to an end.

The show turns gangland rivalry into playful chaos, suggesting that power struggles and bravado are ultimately ridiculous. At its centre, it contrasts the lure of easy status with loyalty, love, and the courage to pursue a genuine dream.

ceilidh.en:
At a ceilidh held in the present day, Ramsay MacLavaney welcomes the gathering as its caller and begins to tell the story behind his family’s place at its centre. The MacLavaneys have led dances for generations: their gift is not simply knowing the steps, but drawing strangers into time with one another. As Ramsay guides the room through reels and songs, he looks back to the young life of his father, Leo, whose warmth, skill and humility make him a natural heir to that calling.

In Scotland, Leo’s world expands when he meets Euna, a witty young Englishwoman who is initially an outsider to the traditions surrounding him. Their attraction grows through music, dancing and the energy of communal celebrations. Around them, a succession of weddings, parties and encounters shows how a ceilidh can hold romance, mischief, conflict and reconciliation in the same room. Leo and Euna build a life together, but the obligations and expectations attached to Leo’s family legacy complicate the private realities of love, aging and parenthood.

Ramsay’s narration moves between past and present, making the dance floor a place where memory becomes tangible. The younger Leo and Euna’s courtship is mirrored by their older selves, and Ramsay must confront the changes that time has brought to the parents he has known all his life. His own relationship with Lucas gives the story another emotional thread: while he inherits the role of caller, he must decide what it means to carry a tradition without losing the freedom to make a life of his own. By bringing the gathered community into the dancing, Ramsay transforms a family history into a shared act of remembrance and connection.

The show explores family inheritance, the bittersweet work of caring for those we love, and the tension between duty and self-determination. Above all, it presents shared music, dance and storytelling as ways people create belonging across generations.

curious case of benjamin button.en:
In a Cornish fishing village at the end of the First World War, Roger and Mary Button are horrified when their newborn son, Benjamin, arrives in the body of an old man. Ashamed and frightened, they hide him in the attic; Mary’s despair leads to her death, while Benjamin grows steadily younger instead of older. After a decade of confinement, he escapes to The Pickled Crab, where he meets Elowen Keene, the warm-hearted barmaid who becomes the love of his life. Their parents oppose the match, and a failed attempt to elope leaves both believing the other has abandoned them.

Benjamin takes work aboard the fishing boat The Salty Maid with Little Jack Trenlee and his family. When war reaches Cornwall, the boat is destroyed in an air raid and Benjamin and Little Jack enlist in the Royal Navy. On the eve of the Normandy landings, Benjamin unexpectedly reunites with Elowen in Portsmouth. They discover the truth about their missed rendezvous, spend the night together, and are reunited after the war as parents to Locryn and, later, Lowen.

As Benjamin’s appearance becomes ever younger, he conceals it with dye and make-up. Tragedy strikes when Lowen drowns in the harbour, exposing both his deception and the strain that his impossible condition has placed on the family. Unable to endure his grief, Benjamin leaves Elowen to search the world for a cure. Years later, rejected by Little Jack and ready to drown himself, he finds the message in a bottle he wrote to Elowen during the war. Its words persuade him to return home.

Elowen forgives him, though Locryn struggles with his father’s absence. Benjamin remains with them through Elowen’s final illness and death, then gradually rebuilds his relationship with Locryn. He continues backwards through adolescence, childhood, infancy, and finally vanishes exactly seventy years after his birth.

The musical explores how love can endure despite time, loss, secrecy, and change. It asks whether a meaningful life lies in controlling time—or in choosing to be present for the people one loves.

curtains.en:
In 1959, the Colonial Theatre in Boston is trying out Robbin’ Hood, a Broadway-bound Western musical with an excruciatingly untalented leading lady, Jessica Cranshaw. Moments after taking her opening-night curtain call, Jessica collapses and dies from poison. Lieutenant Frank Cioffi, the Boston detective assigned to the murder, arrives to seal off the theatre and question everyone involved. A devoted musical-theatre fan as well as a careful investigator, Cioffi is thrilled to be among performers but quickly recognizes that virtually the entire company had reason to despise Jessica.

Producer Carmen Bernstein urgently wants the show to continue; director Christopher Belling fears disaster; leading man Bobby Pepper sees an opening; and lyricist Georgia Hendricks, Jessica’s understudy, must suddenly take the starring role. Georgia’s songwriting partner and former husband, Aaron Fox, struggles with their unresolved relationship, while young performer Niki Harris conceals a personal connection to the dead actress. As Cioffi follows shifting alibis, cryptic notes, and grudges concealed beneath theatrical bravado, he also begins revising Robbin’ Hood with the company and falls for Niki.

The pressure intensifies when another member of the production is murdered, proving that the killer is still inside the theatre and prepared to strike again. Cioffi gathers the cast for a final reconstruction of the crime, using the musical’s rehearsal process to expose contradictions in their stories. The murderer turns out to be Daryl Grady, the Boston Globe theatre critic, whose concealed identity and history explain the killings. He attempts to escape amid the chaos of the reopening performance, but Cioffi unmasks him and prevents further violence. With the case closed, Robbin’ Hood is able to resume, its company newly united and its revised production finally ready for an audience.

The show treats theatre as both a workplace full of insecurity and rivalry and a place where people can remake themselves through collaboration. Its central themes are the tension between illusion and truth, the danger beneath show-business ambition, and the sustaining power of love, creativity, and communal performance.

death takes a holiday.en:
In 1921, shortly after World War I, the Lamberti family returns to Villa Felicita outside Venice after the engagement celebration of Grazia Lamberti and Corrado Danielli. Their car is stopped by a mysterious figure, and Grazia is thrown from it—yet emerges wholly unhurt. Shaken by her near escape, she begins to question whether marriage to Corrado is the life she truly wants. The figure is Death, weary of his endless work and captivated by Grazia. He assumes the body and identity of Prince Nikolai Sirki, a recently deceased friend of Duke Vittorio Lamberti, and asks Vittorio to shelter him for a weekend while he discovers why human beings treasure life and fear death. Vittorio, terrified for his daughter, agrees; the household is told only that Prince Nikolai is an honored guest.

At the villa, Sirki experiences ordinary pleasures with astonishment and is drawn irresistibly to Grazia. Their intimacy grows beside the lake and in a nearby grotto, prompting Grazia to end her engagement. Corrado is devastated, while Alice—Grazia’s widowed sister-in-law—briefly hopes Sirki may return her affection before recognizing his love for Grazia. Major Eric Fenton, Roberto Lamberti’s former comrade, senses something uncanny in Sirki and eventually uncovers that the real prince is dead. Meanwhile, Vittorio and the frightened majordomo Fidele understand the danger of Death’s presence, and the family’s wartime grief rises to the surface.

As midnight approaches, Death reveals that he intends to take Grazia with him. Vittorio confronts him, arguing that real love requires allowing Grazia to live through joy, pain, and choice rather than possessing her forever. Death accepts the lesson and resolves to leave her—until Grazia comes to him of her own will. Learning his true identity does not change her decision: she declares her love, takes his hand at midnight, and walks with him into the light.

The musical explores mortality as the condition that makes life precious. It treats love as both a surrender to loss and a force that transcends fear, even death itself.

dirty rotten scoundrels.en:
On the glamorous French Riviera, the elegant con man Lawrence Jameson makes a luxurious living in Beaumont-sur-Mer by persuading wealthy women that he is a displaced prince collecting funds for his troubled homeland. His polished routines are supported by Andre Thibault, the town’s compromised chief of police, and regularly enriched by credulous visitors such as Muriel Eubanks. Lawrence’s territory is disrupted by Freddy Benson, a brash, small-time American swindler who earns modest sums through tales of his dying grandmother. Lawrence initially tries to drive Freddy away, then attempts to train him in more sophisticated deception. Their partnership quickly gives way to rivalry: neither man is willing to share a resort town—or its wealthy targets—with the other.

They settle their dispute with a wager. The first man to obtain $50,000 from Christine Colgate, an apparently naïve young American heiress newly arrived in town, may remain in Beaumont-sur-Mer; the loser must leave for good. Lawrence approaches Christine as a cultivated, attentive suitor, while Freddy invents a new identity as Ruprecht, Lawrence’s supposedly unstable and emotionally volatile brother. Their schemes collide as each manipulates Christine, recruits Andre, and tries to make the other appear untrustworthy. Freddy’s elaborate performance produces chaos, and Lawrence’s control of the situation begins to weaken when Christine proves unexpectedly perceptive.

As the contest escalates, Freddy and Lawrence each believe he has outmaneuvered the other. Christine seems to yield to their deceptions, only for the men to discover that she has been playing a confidence game of her own. The two rivals must reassess who has truly been in charge, while their competitive alliance shifts into a more mutually useful partnership.

The musical explores deception as both a weapon and a performance, asking whether charm, status, and sympathy can ever be trusted at face value. It also turns rivalry into an unlikely form of connection, as two self-serving men encounter someone every bit as clever as they are.

dolly.en:
Set between the Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee and the glittering stages of Nashville and Hollywood, Dolly: A True Original Musical follows Dolly Parton’s journey from a spirited girl with an outsized voice and even larger ambitions to an artist determined to shape her own destiny. Little Dolly grows up in a crowded but loving mountain home, where scarcity cannot dim her imagination. Encouraged by the music around her and sustained by a fierce belief that her songs can carry her beyond the hills, she begins to picture a life no one else can yet see.

As Dolly pursues that dream, she carries the people and values of home with her—particularly the enduring friendship of Judy Ogle and the influence of Uncle Bill. Leaving familiar ground for Nashville means confronting the uneasy gap between who she has been and the woman the entertainment world expects her to become. Her talent attracts notice, and a pivotal professional partnership with Porter Wagoner opens the door to national fame. Yet success brings pressures of control, image, loyalty, and artistic independence. Dolly must decide whether opportunity is worth the compromises demanded of her, and whether she can protect both her voice and her sense of self.

The story traces her evolution into a performer, songwriter, and public figure whose warmth masks a resolute business instinct. Her relationship with Carl Dean offers a private counterpoint to the highly visible life she is building, while Sandy Gallin represents the wider world of celebrity and new possibilities beyond country music. Moving through professional setbacks, heartbreak, creative breakthroughs, and increasingly vast stages, Dolly learns that reinvention does not require abandoning the past. By insisting on writing, choosing, and speaking for herself, she turns personal history into songs that reach audiences far beyond Tennessee.

At its heart, the musical is about self-determination: the courage to pursue a dream without surrendering ownership of it. It also celebrates loyalty, generosity, resilience, and the transforming power of a voice that remains rooted in home even as it travels around the world.

dolly partons smoky mountain christmas c.en:
On Christmas Eve, 1936, a blizzard bears down on Morton's Holler, a struggling coal-mining town tucked into the Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee. Its wealth, services, and livelihoods are controlled by Ebenezer Scrooge, the town’s hard-hearted mining magnate. While Depression-era hardship presses on his neighbors, Scrooge guards every dollar, dismisses charity, and shows little mercy to his clerk, Bob Cratchit. He also rejects an invitation to celebrate with his nephew Fred, choosing solitude and profit over family and fellowship. As night closes in, Scrooge is confronted by the spirit of his dead business partner, Jacob Marley, who arrives burdened by the consequences of a selfish life and warns Scrooge that he still has one chance to change.

Marley sends three visitors to lead Scrooge through the truth he has refused to see. The Ghost of Christmas Past carries him back to the hopes, losses, and choices of his younger years, including the affection he once shared with Fanny and the warmth of Fezziwig’s generosity. The Ghost of Christmas Present reveals the life continuing around him: the Cratchit family’s loving but precarious Christmas, Tiny Tim’s fragile health, and the resilience of the people of Morton's Holler despite the deprivation Scrooge’s rule has deepened. Finally, the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows him a cold future in which his death inspires no grief, only relief and indifference, while the people he neglected endure the cost of his cruelty.

Terrified by this vision, Scrooge vows to live differently. On Christmas morning, he throws open his doors and his heart, bringing aid and celebration to the Cratchits, reconciling with Fred, and sharing his prosperity with the town. In Morton's Holler, a man who once treated people as entries in a ledger begins to recognize them as neighbors, family, and fellow human beings.

The musical’s central themes are redemption, compassion, and the belief that a person can choose a more generous life. It also celebrates community: hardship becomes bearable when people care for one another, and love proves more valuable than wealth.

escape to margaritaville.en:
On a small Caribbean island, Tully Mars spends his days singing at the faded Margaritaville resort, charming visitors, and treating romance as a holiday pastime. Around him are the resort’s spirited owner, Marley; his loyal but lovelorn friend Brick; busboy Jamal; and J.D., an eccentric regular who records his remarkable memories on bar napkins. Tully’s easygoing life is disrupted when Rachel, a driven environmental scientist from Cincinnati, arrives with her best friend Tammy for a pre-wedding getaway.

Rachel intends to relax only briefly while collecting volcanic soil samples for her work, and she initially sees Tully as exactly the kind of carefree distraction she avoids. Yet his warmth and apparent sincerity draw her in. Their flirtation becomes a genuine connection, forcing Tully to confront the possibility that he wants more than another temporary affair. Meanwhile, Tammy, worn down by the demands and criticism of her controlling fiancé Chadd, finds unexpected confidence on the island. Brick, who has quietly loved Tammy from afar, encourages her to recognize that marriage should not mean surrendering herself.

The vacation turns chaotic when Chadd arrives to retrieve Tammy and impose his plans. As the island’s volcano becomes increasingly active, old assumptions erupt alongside it: Tammy reconsiders her engagement, Rachel must choose between professional certainty and emotional risk, and Tully faces the prospect of leaving his familiar paradise. After the eruption scatters the guests and ends the holiday, Rachel returns to Cincinnati. Realizing that he cannot simply let her disappear into the life she left behind, Tully travels to Ohio to prove that his feelings are not confined to the beach. Tammy also makes her own choice, rejecting a future shaped by Chadd and embracing the possibility of love with Brick.

The show explores the tension between escape and commitment, asking whether a carefree life can coexist with emotional responsibility. It celebrates friendship, self-worth, and the courage to choose a life that feels genuinely one’s own.

finians rainbow.en:
Finian McLonergan arrives in Rainbow Valley, Missitucky, with his daughter Sharon and a stolen crock of gold. Believing that gold buried near Fort Knox will multiply, Finian secretly plants it on the land of a struggling community of Black and white tobacco sharecroppers. The Valley is under threat: Senator Billboard Rawkins, a loudly racist politician, wants the residents driven out over unpaid taxes so that he can control the property. Woody Mahoney, the young landowner and protector of the sharecroppers, returns with money to stop the auction, and he and Sharon quickly fall in love. Finian’s plans are complicated by Og, the leprechaun from whom he took the gold. Og has followed him across the Atlantic because, unless the crock is recovered, he will lose his magic and become permanently mortal.

When geological surveyors discover that Rainbow Valley contains valuable gold deposits, Rawkins and his henchman Buzz Collins intensify their efforts to seize the land. The crock’s magic grants wishes to anyone standing near it, but its power is dangerous when used impulsively. Sharon, appalled by Rawkins’s prejudice, wishes that he could become Black and understand the hatred he inflicts on others. Her wish comes true. Rawkins, now forced to live under the discrimination he once promoted, is confronted by the social world he helped create and gradually changes his outlook. Meanwhile, Finian’s secret, the crock, and Sharon’s unwitting wish bring the community into conflict with the authorities; Sharon is arrested on a charge of witchcraft.

As the crisis reaches its height, the people of Rainbow Valley unite to protect Sharon and their homes. Og ultimately makes a wish that restores Rawkins and resolves the immediate danger, but it also sacrifices Og’s chance to regain immortality. Finian accepts that riches cannot secure happiness, while Sharon and Woody look toward a shared future in the Valley.

forever plaid.en:
Sparky, Smudge, Jinx, and Frankie are four earnest young men who meet in high school through the Audio Visual Club and discover a shared devotion to close-harmony singing. Calling themselves Forever Plaid, they rehearse in the basement of Smudge’s family plumbing-supply company, model themselves on the polished vocal groups they admire, and pursue every modest booking they can find: family parties, fund-raisers, supermarket openings, and proms. Their ambitions remain larger than their venues. Frankie works in dental supplies, Smudge in bathroom fixtures, Jinx in auto parts, and Sparky in better dresses, but nights and weekends belong to the quartet and its dream of professional success.

At last, on February 9, 1964, the Plaids secure what feels like their breakthrough: an engagement at the Airport Hilton cocktail bar, the Fusel Lounge. While driving in their cherry-red 1954 Mercury to collect their custom-made plaid tuxedos, they rehearse the finale for the show they have waited years to perform. Their car is struck broadside by a school bus carrying Catholic schoolgirls to see the Beatles’ American television debut on The Ed Sullivan Show. The girls survive, but the four Plaids are killed instantly, their first major performance ending before it begins.

The musical starts from that unfinished moment. Suspended beyond death, the quartet receives an extraordinary chance to return to Earth and give the concert denied to them in life. They arrive still bound by their anxieties, comic habits, old rivalries, and fiercely precise ideas about harmony. As they work through the long-awaited programme, each man confronts the vulnerability beneath the matching jackets and cheerful stage manner. Their performance becomes both a final bid for the fame they never reached and a farewell to the lives that stopped in mid-phrase. Once they have fulfilled their “Mission of Harmony,” they must leave the stage and return to the cosmos.

The show’s central themes are friendship, perseverance, and the need to complete an unfinished dream. It finds tenderness in the way shared music can preserve identity, connection, and hope even after loss.

franz and marie.en:
In an isolated military outpost in a warped late-nineteenth-century European world, Franz Woyzeck returns from the front line carrying wounds no one can see. Nightmares and visions of fire in the sky stalk him, and his grip on reality weakens as the soldiers wait without purpose for further orders. Franz’s one certainty is Marie, the woman he loves, and Georgie, their baby. Because military rules have kept him from taking leave, Franz and Marie have never been able to marry; nevertheless, he is determined to provide a future for them.

That determination leaves Franz vulnerable to the men above him. Sergeant Ursid, Captain Peccary, and the unsettling Doctor Simian exert authority over a soldier with little money, little status, and diminishing control over his own mind. Their pressure turns Franz’s daily life into a series of humiliations and tests, while the military outpost becomes a place where cruelty is treated as routine and vulnerability as a weakness to exploit. Marie, meanwhile, must make her own choices within the same harsh social order. Her hopes, needs, and compromises carry as much weight as Franz’s suffering, rather than existing merely at its edges.

As Franz’s poverty, exhaustion, and traumatic visions intensify, distrust enters the couple’s relationship. The formidable Drum Major Varg embodies a seductive alternative to Franz’s powerlessness, while figures around the outpost watch, judge, provoke, or profit from the lovers’ precarious circumstances. Franz tries ever harder to protect Marie and Georgie, but every effort seems to tighten the forces closing around them. Love becomes entangled with fear, possession, shame, and desperation, driving the family toward an irreversible and heartbreaking fate.

The musical examines how war trauma, class prejudice, and institutional brutality can deform intimate love. It also places Marie’s survival and agency beside Franz’s collapse, confronting the damage wrought by toxic masculinity and unequal power.

galileo.en:
Galileo Galilei peers through his telescope and finds a universe far more startling than the one the authorities have declared settled. His celestial observations persuade him that the Earth is not the fixed centre of creation, and he begins to speak with the conviction—and provocation—of a man who believes evidence should outweigh inherited certainty. As his ideas spread, Galileo’s brilliance attracts admiration, scrutiny, and increasingly dangerous opposition.

At the heart of the conflict is Galileo’s connection with Bishop Maffeo Barberini, a trusted confidant whose rise within the Church turns friendship into a fraught test of loyalty. Galileo hopes that Barberini’s influence will protect room for inquiry, but the political and religious pressures surrounding Rome make compromise ever harder. Cardinal Morosini and Bishop Grasso regard Galileo’s claims not merely as an academic dispute but as a challenge to the order that sustains their authority, while a wider rebellion leaves the institution particularly unwilling to tolerate dissent.

Galileo’s struggle also reaches into his home. His daughter, Virginia Galilei, shares his intelligence and aspirations, yet must live with the consequences of his defiance in a world that grants her far less freedom. Her relationship with Alessandro Tarantola offers a personal counterpoint to the public battle, as love, family expectation, and social standing collide. Galileo’s pursuit of truth therefore becomes inseparable from the futures of those closest to him.

Summoned to Rome, Galileo must defend what he has seen before the most powerful religious institution in the world. As the confrontation escalates, each central figure faces a choice between principle, ambition, safety, affection, and survival. Galileo’s discoveries may transform humanity’s place in the cosmos, but their immediate cost threatens to break the relationships that once gave his work meaning.

The musical explores the collision of evidence with institutional power, and the price individuals pay when they refuse to abandon conviction. It also treats curiosity, belief, ambition, friendship, and familial love as forces that can draw people together—or pull them irrevocably apart.

girls night.en:
Twenty-two years after the death of their friend Sharon, four women reunite for a raucous evening at a karaoke bar to celebrate the engagement of Sharon’s daughter, Candy Rose. Sharon herself is present in spirit: wearing angel wings, she narrates the night and slips into the action, delighted to observe the friends she left behind. The gathering brings together Carol, Sharon’s high-spirited, hard-partying friend; Carol’s younger sister Kate, the sensible longtime designated driver; sharp-tongued Anita, whose blunt honesty masks old insecurities; and Liza, who appears to have a comfortable family life but is increasingly unhappy in her marriage.

As drinks flow and the women take turns at the microphone, their exuberant performances become a way of saying what ordinary conversation has kept hidden. They revisit their teenage years, trade jokes and grievances, remember shared losses, and confront the disappointments that adulthood has delivered. Carol’s bravado gives way to vulnerability, Liza wrestles with whether she can remain in a loveless relationship, and Anita reveals the hurt beneath her fearless manner. Kate, usually the cautious observer responsible for everyone else, begins to shed the role that has confined her and risks stepping outside the safe life expected of her.

Sharon’s presence initially seems to unite the group around a cherished memory. Yet, as the night grows messier and more candid, Kate and Carol uncover unsettling truths about Sharon’s past and about the story they have told themselves since her death. The discovery tests their loyalty and forces them to see both Sharon and one another as flawed, complicated people rather than idealized versions of their younger selves. By the end, the friends have not solved every problem, but they have reclaimed honesty, laughter, and a renewed connection.

The musical explores female friendship as a source of refuge, confrontation, and survival across decades of change. It balances grief, romantic dissatisfaction, self-image, and growing older with the liberating possibility of speaking plainly and celebrating life together.

hair.en:
In New York City during the Vietnam War, a loose-knit Tribe of young hippies creates its own world of friendship, sex, drugs, music, protest, and restless idealism. At its center are Claude, sensitive and uncertain; Berger, his irreverent, charismatic friend; and Sheila, a politically committed student whose feelings and loyalties complicate her relationships with both men. Around them are Woof, Hud, Jeanie, Dionne, Crissy, and the rest of the Tribe, who turn parks, streets, apartments, and demonstrations into spaces of communal celebration and defiance.

The Tribe rejects the rules of conventional America while confronting the pressures that those rules impose. They mock authority, argue over race, class, sexuality, and personal freedom, and take part in anti-war action. Sheila leads a protest rally, while Berger goads and entertains the group with a combination of bravado and provocation. Beneath their exuberance, however, the approaching war is increasingly inescapable. Claude receives a draft notice, forcing him to choose between resisting military service and meeting the expectations of his conservative parents and wider society.

Claude’s inner conflict becomes the show’s central journey. He is drawn to the Tribe’s promise of peace, love, and personal liberation, yet fears the consequences of refusing the draft. In a hallucinatory sequence shaped by drugs, anxiety, and fantasy, his private desires and terrors collide: romantic longing, racial violence, war, family pressure, and images of national power overwhelm the Tribe’s hopeful vision. His friends urge resistance, but their solidarity cannot make the decision for him. Claude ultimately submits to induction and leaves the world of the Tribe behind. The final image places him among the dead of the Vietnam War, as the Tribe and audience are confronted with the human cost of the conflict.

The musical explores the clash between individual freedom and institutional conformity, asking what personal conviction costs when political power demands obedience. It also treats love, communal belonging, sexual liberation, racial tension, and pacifism as inseparable from its condemnation of war.

high society.en:
At the Lord family’s waterfront estate in Oyster Bay, Long Island, glamorous socialite Tracy Samantha Lord prepares to marry the upright, status-conscious George Kittredge. The wedding weekend is already complicated by Tracy’s estranged father Seth, whose affair threatens to become public, and by the arrival of Tracy’s charming former husband, C. K. Dexter Haven. Dexter has been pressured into admitting two Spy magazine employees, journalist Mike Connor and photographer Liz Imbrie, to the house as supposed wedding guests; in return, the magazine will suppress its damaging story about Seth.

Tracy, Dinah, and the family decide to play along while making the reporters’ task as difficult as possible. Dinah and Tracy confuse Mike and Liz with absurd disguises and false introductions, while Tracy initially presents Uncle Willie as her father and then passes the real Seth off as Willie. Amid the deception, Dexter challenges Tracy’s habit of judging others harshly, and her confidence in George begins to weaken. George’s stiff propriety looks less appealing beside Mike’s warmth and Dexter’s lingering affection.

At Uncle Willie’s pre-wedding party, champagne loosens Tracy’s restraint. She dances recklessly, clashes with George, and grows close to Mike, who recognizes that George is not the husband she needs. Tracy impulsively invites Mike to go swimming; however, she becomes too intoxicated, and Mike carries her safely to bed. The next morning, Tracy’s incomplete memory of the night leaves her ashamed and fearful of scandal, while George assumes the worst and reacts with cold outrage.

The misunderstandings unravel. Liz refuses to exploit the family, Seth and Margaret move toward reconciliation, and Mike realizes that his true love is Liz. Tracy finally rejects George and recognizes that Dexter understands her flaws without demanding perfection. With the wedding already arranged, Dexter takes George’s place, and Tracy and Dexter begin again.

The musical explores the gap between polished social appearances and imperfect private lives. It argues for compassion, self-knowledge, forgiveness, and choosing love over pride or social ambition.

hms pinafore w sarasota opera.en:
Aboard HMS Pinafore, anchored in Portsmouth Harbour, the captain’s daughter Josephine is expected to marry Sir Joseph Porter, the First Lord of the Admiralty. Sir Joseph is wealthy, politically powerful, and accompanied everywhere by an adoring retinue of sisters, cousins and aunts, yet Josephine cannot return his affection. She secretly loves Ralph Rackstraw, an able seaman aboard her father’s ship. Although Ralph is honourable, courageous and devoted, Josephine believes that the gulf between an officer’s daughter and a common sailor makes their union impossible.

Captain Corcoran, who prides himself on a style of enlightened authority—courteous to his crew but firm in rank—encourages Josephine to accept Sir Joseph. Sir Joseph himself urges the captain to treat the sailors as equals, unaware of the contradiction between his democratic slogans and his expectation that Josephine will marry him. Ralph, despondent after Josephine initially rejects him, resolves to take his own life. Josephine stops him and admits that she loves him. With the help of the crew, the couple plan to elope that night.

Their plan is betrayed by Dick Deadeye, a blunt and cynical sailor who objects to the disruption of order aboard ship. Captain Corcoran discovers the intended escape and has Ralph placed in irons. Matters are transformed when Little Buttercup, a dockside vendor who has long loved the captain, reveals a secret from the past: as a baby-farmer, she accidentally switched two infants in her care. Those children were Ralph and Captain Corcoran. Ralph is therefore the captain by birth, while Corcoran is the common sailor.

The social order immediately rearranges itself. Ralph assumes command of HMS Pinafore and is free to marry Josephine; Captain Corcoran, now reduced in rank, may marry Buttercup; and Sir Joseph turns his attention to his cousin Hebe.

The show satirizes class, authority and social ambition by showing how easily status can be overturned by an arbitrary accident of birth. It also celebrates romantic loyalty while exposing the absurdity of judging people’s worth by rank rather than character.

holiday inn.en:
In 1946, Jim Hardy performs in a New York nightclub with his best friend and dance partner, Ted Hanover, and his fiancée, Lila Dixon. Longing for a quieter future, Jim proposes to Lila and reveals that he has bought Mason Farm in Midville, Connecticut, where he imagines they will settle down and raise a family. Lila, however, is devoted to the stage. When Ted receives an opportunity to tour, she chooses professional ambition over Jim’s rural dream and joins Ted instead. Jim moves to Connecticut alone, only to discover that farming is far harder—and lonelier—than he expected.

His fortunes change when he meets Linda Mason, a local schoolteacher whose warmth, voice, and dancing talent reveal a buried desire for performance. Linda has a personal connection to the farmhouse, and she and Jim quickly become partners in a new plan: transforming the struggling property into the Holiday Inn, a venue that opens for major holidays and offers guests elaborate entertainment. Through festivities from Thanksgiving to Independence Day, the inn becomes a success, and Jim and Linda’s working partnership turns into love.

Ted eventually arrives in Midville, still chasing larger opportunities. Impressed by Linda’s ability, he sees her as the ideal replacement for Lila and tries to persuade her to leave Connecticut for a Hollywood career. Jim’s insecurity and Ted’s charm create a painful rift between the friends, while Linda must decide whether her future lies in the glamour of a new career or in the life she has built with Jim. Misunderstandings threaten both the inn and the romance, but the competing ambitions are finally resolved. Jim and Linda marry at the Holiday Inn, while Ted and Lila reunite, each accepting the life—and partner—that suits them best.

The show explores the tension between ambition and belonging, asking whether happiness comes from public success or from a life built with someone else. It also celebrates reinvention, friendship, and the way shared creativity can turn an uncertain place into a home.

hot mess.en:
Earth, vibrant, self-possessed and newly single after the catastrophic end of her long-ago relationship with the dinosaurs, has spent millions of years enduring disastrous dates. Then she meets Humanity, who introduces himself as Hu: young, excitable, and instantly enchanted by everything she is. Their attraction is immediate, but Earth is wary of being hurt again. Hu wins her over with earnest fascination, and the two begin a tender partnership. As their relationship grows, Hu learns how to cultivate the land, build homes, harness energy and shape a future with Earth at its centre. Together they share discovery, comfort and a thrilling sense that anything might be possible.

Yet Hu’s admiration gradually twists into insecurity. Feeling small beside Earth’s age, strength and abundance, he becomes determined to prove himself through relentless growth. What begins as curiosity becomes appetite: he takes more space, demands more resources and pursues ever grander achievements. Cities rise, industry accelerates, and Hu reaches beyond Earth’s embrace in a journey to the Moon—an act that feels, to Earth, like betrayal. His work, ambitions and need for progress increasingly replace the care and attention that once defined their romance.

Earth tries to make Hu see the damage he is causing. She bears the consequences of his neglect while he insists that his choices are necessary, inevitable or somehow separate from their relationship. The love affair becomes volatile: affection is tangled with anger, dependence, denial and grief. As Earth’s patience reaches its limit, Hu must confront the truth that the future he is chasing may destroy the person—and the home—he claims to love. Their rupture leaves the possibility of repair uncertain, demanding honesty, responsibility and a radically different kind of devotion.

The show frames environmental collapse as the painful breakdown of an intimate relationship. Its themes are love and interdependence, the costs of unchecked ambition, and the fragile hope that recognition can still lead to change.

im every woman.en:
Chaka Khan appears at a family recovery meeting, where the pressures of fame, addiction and painful memory hang over her. From there, the story returns to Chicago, where she is still Yvette Marie Stevens: a gifted young singer growing up amid her parents’ volatile relationship and her father Charles Stevens’s heroin addiction. Seeking both identity and purpose, she becomes involved in civil-rights activism, meets Fred Hampton and Hassan Khan, and is given the name “Chaka” at an Afrocentre. Her powerful voice launches her into music, first as the lead singer of Rufus and then toward a solo career that will carry her from Chicago to international stages.

Success brings artistic exhilaration as well as forces determined to control her. Chaka forms friendships with Joni Mitchell and later Prince, encounters fellow musicians including Stevie Wonder, Miles Davis, Luther Vandross and Steve Winwood, and battles a music business shaped by racism, sexism and commercial calculation. At home, her relationship with Hassan deteriorates through jealousy and infidelity; motherhood deepens the stakes when her daughter Milini needs her presence. A second marriage, to Richard Holland, initially promises escape but becomes engulfed in drugs, partying and abuse. As career setbacks and substance dependency compound the damage, Chaka confronts the cost of the persona the world celebrates—and the ways those closest to her have been hurt.

The narrative follows her through withdrawal, family reckoning and renewed determination. Chaka gradually claims the authority to protect her children, define her own art and return to performance not merely as an icon, but as a woman who has survived the forces that tried to silence her.

The show centres on finding a voice amid racism, sexism, addiction and private trauma. It presents resilience not as effortless triumph, but as the continuing work of reclaiming truth, family and self-possession.

last ship.en:
Set in Wallsend, on the River Tyne, The Last Ship follows a shipbuilding community facing the loss of its livelihood. As a boy, Gideon Fletcher dreams of a life beyond the shipyard and its inherited expectations. He leaves town—and leaves behind Meg Dawson, the girl who loves him—promising a freedom that never includes the responsibility he has abandoned. Seventeen years later, Gideon returns to a Wallsend transformed by industrial decline. The yard’s last unfinished vessel has no buyer, the workers are told it will be broken up for scrap, and generations of skilled labour face redundancy.

Meg now runs the local pub and has built a life without Gideon, carrying the hurt of his disappearance. Their reunion becomes still more difficult when Gideon discovers that Meg’s teenage daughter, Ellen, is also his daughter. Ellen, a sharp-willed aspiring musician, resents the mother who tries to protect her and the father who has suddenly appeared too late. Her own wish to leave for London echoes Gideon’s youthful escape, forcing Meg to confront the fear of being left behind once again.

Around them, the yard’s workers struggle to decide whether resistance is futile. Jackie White, the shipyard foreman, tries to hold the men together while concealing a serious illness from his wife Peggy, the yard’s nurse.
