Union voices including Billy Thompson and Davey Harrison clash over compromise, loyalty, anger, and what dignity demands when management withdraws support. In the end, the workers refuse to watch the last ship be destroyed. They seize the chance to complete it themselves, turning an abandoned industrial project into an act of collective defiance. As the vessel is prepared to sail, Gideon must decide whether he will once more run from Wallsend or accept a place within the community—and within Meg and Ellen’s lives.

The musical’s themes are belonging, family, working-class solidarity, and the human cost of economic abandonment. It contrasts escape with commitment, asking whether a damaged community—and the people within it—can still choose to build a future together.

lizzie.en:
In the oppressive heat of late summer 1892, Lizzie Borden lives in the Borden family home in Fall River, Massachusetts, with her domineering father Andrew, her stepmother Abby, her older sister Emma, and the household maid Bridget Sullivan. The house projects respectability, but inside it is governed by Andrew’s cruelty, control, and a suffocating sense that the sisters’ lives and inheritance are not their own. Emma, worn down by years of resentment, has learned to survive by nurturing Lizzie’s anger while avoiding open confrontation. Bridget, sharp-eyed and disillusioned, sees the household’s tensions building toward disaster.

Lizzie seeks refuge from the atmosphere of fear in the barn and in the companionship of Alice Russell, the Bordens’ neighbour. Alice offers tenderness, desire, and the possibility of a life beyond the rules of the Borden home. Yet Lizzie cannot fully escape the violence that shapes her world. When the threat and humiliation she experiences invade even the places she considers safe, her fear hardens into fury. Emma’s buried rage, Bridget’s fatalistic insight, and Alice’s efforts to protect Lizzie all converge as Lizzie reaches a point where she believes there is no way back.

Andrew and Abby Borden are then murdered in their home. In the immediate aftermath, the women face the practical and emotional wreckage of the crime: suspicion, conflicting loyalties, the need for an alibi, and the question of who will bear responsibility. Lizzie is arrested and held in Taunton while the evidence and testimony around the killings remain uncertain. Alice must decide whether to stand by Lizzie; Emma must confront both her complicity and her grief; Bridget watches the family’s private nightmare become public spectacle. At trial, the gaps in the case against Lizzie prove decisive, and she is acquitted, leaving the women to live with what has—and may not have—been said.

The musical explores repression turning into rage, and the devastating cost of denying women safety, autonomy, and a voice. It also leaves guilt, truth, love, and liberation deliberately entangled: the ending offers escape, but not uncomplicated peace.

lost boys.en:
In Santa Carla, California, Lucy Emerson arrives with her sons, Michael and Sam, determined to rebuild their lives after leaving a troubled home behind. Michael resents the move and longs to become someone other than the angry, displaced teenager he has been. On the boardwalk, he is captivated by Star and drawn toward David, the magnetic frontman of a local rock band. David, Marko, Dwayne, and Paul offer Michael the exhilaration, danger, and belonging he has been missing, while Star warns him that their world carries a cost. As Michael follows them into Santa Carla’s nocturnal underworld, he is pushed toward a transformation that will make leaving impossible.

Meanwhile, Sam senses that something is wrong. He finds unexpected allies in Alan Frog and Edgar Frog, two intense young vampire hunters whose comic-book certainty begins to look less ridiculous as people disappear and Michael’s behaviour changes. Their investigation reveals that David’s band is not merely a band: its members are vampires, and Michael has become trapped between ordinary life and their promise of eternal freedom. Lucy, unaware of the full danger surrounding her sons, begins a tentative romance with Max, a kindly-seeming local whose connection to the vampires is far more sinister than it appears.

As Michael struggles to resist David’s influence and protect Star, Sam, Alan, and Edgar race to uncover how to save him. The brothers’ conflict becomes a fight for Michael’s life, forcing Lucy to confront both the secrets of Santa Carla and the consequences of trying to begin again. In the final confrontation, the Emerson family and their allies challenge the vampires’ hold over the town, testing whether Michael can reclaim himself before the night claims him permanently.

The musical explores the hunger to belong, especially when freedom and acceptance are offered at a devastating price. It also centres on family loyalty: the imperfect but fierce bonds that can pull someone back from isolation, fear, and self-destruction.

mexodus.en:
Set in 1851, Mexodus follows Henry, an enslaved Black man in Texas who is forced to flee after an altercation with the master on the plantation where he is held. Rather than attempting the better-known escape northward, Henry heads south, toward the Rio Grande and Mexico—a country where slavery has been abolished. His flight is urgent and perilous: slave catchers pursue freedom seekers, and the possibility of betrayal shadows every mile of the journey. Crossing the river promises liberation, but it does not immediately erase the dangers created by the border, prejudice, poverty, and the competing interests of people on both sides of it.

Wounded and close to death, Henry is discovered by Carlos, a Mexican farmer and former combat medic of the Mexican-American War. Carlos is haunted by his wartime experiences and by guilt over leaving his fellow soldiers behind. He initially hesitates to endanger himself by helping Henry, while Henry has little reason to trust a stranger who might turn him in for a reward. Yet necessity brings the two men together. As Carlos shelters Henry and they navigate the risks surrounding the border, each confronts the assumptions and wounds he carries.

Their tentative partnership gradually becomes a bond built through shared struggle. Henry fights to claim the freedom that has been denied to him, while Carlos must decide whether he can act with courage and solidarity despite fear, trauma, and the social pressures around him. Their route toward Mexico is not a simple passage from captivity to safety; it is a journey through a contested landscape where racial hierarchy, nationalism, war, and economic desperation shape every choice. By relying on one another, Henry and Carlos begin to imagine a future that neither could reach alone.

Mexodus is about the pursuit of freedom across borders and the moral risks of choosing to help another person survive. It explores Black and Brown solidarity, the persistence of racial oppression, and the possibility that courage, trust, and community can interrupt cycles of fear and violence.

midnight at the never get.en:
In 1965 New York, cabaret singer Trevor Copeland returns to The Never Get, a Greenwich Village nightclub, to perform a midnight tribute to Arthur Brightman: his gifted pianist, songwriter, collaborator, and lost lover. As Trevor addresses the audience and sings Arthur’s songs, he reconstructs the couple’s history—though his memories shift, correct themselves, and gradually reveal how much grief has shaped the story he wants to tell.

Trevor and Arthur first find an artistic home at The Never Get, where their act, “Midnight,” lets them perform love songs about men without disguising their meaning. In a city where their relationship is illegal, the club becomes both refuge and declaration. Their work wins an enthusiastic audience, and their creative partnership deepens into a romance. Trevor’s voice gives life to Arthur’s increasingly daring songs; Arthur, encouraged by Trevor and by the freedom of the room, begins to write with a candour unavailable in the wider world.

Success, however, brings demands. Industry figures see commercial potential in Arthur’s music, but expect the lovers’ songs to be made acceptable to mainstream audiences by changing male pronouns and concealing their truth. Arthur resists the compromises at first, yet becomes frustrated by the limits of the small, clandestine world in which he and Trevor can live openly. Meanwhile, a more militant movement for gay liberation gathers force around them. Trevor and Arthur do not respond to its urgency in the same way, and their differences—about art, ambition, identity, and what freedom should require—place mounting pressure on their love.

When Arthur leaves New York for opportunities on the West Coast, Trevor is left with absence, resentment, and an unfinished version of their life together. His memorial performance becomes an attempt to bring Arthur back through music, while confronting the possibility that remembrance can preserve love only by altering it.

The musical explores love lived under prohibition, the cost of artistic self-censorship, and the tension between private happiness and public liberation. It also asks whether memory is an act of devotion, an evasion of pain, or both.

miracle on 34th street.en:
In New York City, Doris Walker, Macy’s hard-driving Special Events Coordinator, is preparing the Thanksgiving Day Parade while raising her practical young daughter, Susan, to distrust make-believe. When the man hired to play Santa arrives drunk, Doris turns to a kindly stranger who has been watching the parade preparations: Kris Kringle. He performs so brilliantly that Macy’s keeps him on as its in-store Santa, though his frank declaration that he is the real Santa Claus soon unsettles the company’s executives.

Kris becomes an unexpected success with children, especially because he refuses to promote toys that Macy’s does not stock and instead directs families to other stores when that is where they can find what they need. His generosity delights customers and turns Macy’s apparent loss into a public-relations triumph. Susan, who has absorbed Doris’s skeptical outlook, initially resists Kris’s warmth and certainty. Their neighbour, Fred Gaily, encourages her to allow room for wonder, while gradually falling in love with Doris. Doris, however, fears disappointment and keeps Fred at a distance.

Macy’s public-relations chief, Marvin Shellhammer, worries that Kris’s claims will damage the store. After an incident leads to Kris being questioned about his sanity, Mr. Sawyer presses for him to be committed. The case reaches court, where Fred takes on Kris’s defence before Judge Martin Group. Prosecutor Thomas Mara argues that Kris is deluded; Fred argues that goodwill, belief, and the public’s response make the question more complicated than a medical diagnosis. When letters addressed to Santa Claus are delivered to the courthouse, they offer a dramatic answer: the institution entrusted with the nation’s mail has effectively recognized Kris as Santa. The judge dismisses the case, and Susan’s wish for a real home and family begins to come true as Doris finally accepts both Fred and the possibility of a miracle.

The musical celebrates faith in possibilities that cannot be measured or bought, and the power of generosity to change a commercial world into a more humane one. It also follows a mother and daughter learning that love and hope need not require certainty.

murder for two.en:
At Arthur Whitney’s isolated rural New England mansion, a surprise birthday party becomes a crime scene when the celebrated mystery novelist arrives and is immediately shot dead. Officer Marcus Moscowicz, a small-town policeman who longs to become a detective, reaches the house before the official investigator can get there. With the real detective due within an hour, Marcus claims the case—and the chance to prove he is more than a uniformed officer—while relying on the silent assistance of his unseen partner, Lou.

Every guest has reason to wish Arthur dead. His widow, Dahlia Whitney, is theatrical, grieving, and possibly eager for a more dramatic final act than her marriage allowed. Their neighbours, Murray and Barb Flandon, bring a lifetime of domestic bickering and resentment. Arthur’s niece, Steph Whitney, has her own frustrations, while Barrette Lewis, a prima ballerina, moves through the interrogation with suspicious poise. Dr. Griff, the local psychiatrist, knows far too much about everyone’s private troubles, and the remnants of an antiquated boys’ choir—Timmy, Yonkers, and Skid—supply further disorder. A late arrival, Henry Vivaldi, adds another layer to the increasingly tangled gathering.

Marcus questions, accuses, reenacts, and sings his way through a succession of clues, alibis, confessions, reversals, and absurd revelations. The dead man’s unpleasant personality has left a trail of wounded egos, compromised ambitions, and people who had been transformed into material for his fiction. As the clock runs down, Marcus’s hunger for professional recognition collides with the practical need to identify the killer. The investigation grows ever more chaotic, culminating in the discovery that the night holds more than one crime and that Marcus himself must confront what he is willing to do for the badge—and the title—he wants.

At its heart, Murder for Two turns the classic whodunit into a comic examination of ambition, performance, and the stories people tell about themselves. It suggests that beneath theatrical grief, rivalry, and self-interest, the search for truth can also expose the investigator’s own desires.

nunsense.en:
At Mount Saint Helen’s School, five surviving members of the Little Sisters of Hoboken take the stage for an emergency benefit performance. A disastrous batch of vichyssoise prepared by the convent cook, Sister Julia, Child of God, has poisoned fifty-two sisters. After earlier fundraising efforts are diverted to expensive convent video equipment, four of the dead remain unburied in the convent freezer. The evening’s variety show is therefore both a memorial and a last attempt to earn enough money for their proper burial.

Mother Superior Sister Mary Regina presides over the event with equal parts authority and a hunger for the spotlight. Her second-in-command, Sister Mary Hubert, tries to keep the programme disciplined while quietly challenging the Reverend Mother’s dominance. Sister Robert Anne, a sharp-tongued Brooklyn nun, brings irreverent energy and repeatedly tests the limits of Regina’s patience. Sister Mary Leo, the young novice, treats the benefit as an opportunity to pursue her dream of becoming the world’s first ballerina nun. Meanwhile, gentle Sister Mary Amnesia—whose memory was lost after a crucifix struck her head—searches for clues to her identity while discovering her own unexpected talents.

What begins as a supposedly orderly fundraiser becomes a loose, audience-facing sequence of songs, comic routines, personal testimonies, and improvised disruptions. Each sister gets a moment to reveal the ambitions, disappointments, and eccentricities hidden beneath her habit. Rivalries flare, technical problems and programme changes threaten the show’s rhythm, and the women must negotiate who controls the stage and what their community truly needs. Yet their conflicts never erase their shared responsibility: the performance must succeed for the sisters waiting in the freezer. As the finale approaches, the nuns turn their disorder into collective momentum, inviting the audience into their mission and affirming that their unconventional show is also an act of loyalty to the absent members of their order.

The show’s themes are community, resilience, and the comic humanity beneath religious formality. It celebrates self-expression while suggesting that cooperation—and a willingness to laugh at hardship—can turn grief and financial crisis into a shared purpose.

one day.en:
On 15 July 1988—St Swithin’s Day—Dexter “Dex” Mayhew and Emma “Em” Morley meet after their graduation from the University of Edinburgh. Dex is charming, wealthy and apparently carefree; Em is sharp, idealistic and uncertain of her future. They spend an intimate but ultimately platonic night together, then separate in the morning, beginning a friendship that will be revisited on the same date each year. As their twenties unfold, their lives head in markedly different directions. Dex pursues glamour, travel and television, embracing a reckless lifestyle that gradually exposes his insecurity and self-destructive impulses. Em returns to Leeds, works in a restaurant, struggles to turn her talent into a purposeful career, and endures an unhappy relationship with the well-meaning but mismatched Ian.

Despite distance, missed calls and growing complications, Dex and Em remain emotionally central to one another. They travel together, quarrel over Dex’s careless treatment of others, reconcile, and repeatedly find that desire and timing are misaligned. Emma becomes a teacher and begins to find her voice as a writer, while Dexter’s professional success deteriorates alongside his family life. He marries Sylvie, and they have a daughter, Jasmine, but the marriage fails. The death of his mother, Alison, leaves him devastated; estranged from his father, Stephen, and facing addiction and failure, Dex is forced to confront the person he has become.

When Dex is at his lowest, Emma helps him rebuild. Their long-deferred connection finally becomes a relationship, and they make a home together in London, with Emma’s writing bringing her real confidence and success. Their happiness is abruptly shattered when Emma is killed in a cycling accident. Dex withdraws into grief, reliving their shared history and struggling to imagine a future without her. Over time, however, he returns to Edinburgh and to the place where their story began, accompanied by Jasmine and able at last to hold both his loss and his love for Emma.

The musical explores how friendship, love and personal growth are shaped by timing as much as by choice. It also considers grief, class, ambition and the difficult work of becoming someone capable of giving—and receiving—love.

ride the cyclone.en:
Six members of the Saint Cassian Chamber Choir from Uranium City, Saskatchewan, die when the Cyclone roller coaster derails during a school outing. They awaken in a strange limbo presided over by The Amazing Karnak, an antique mechanical fortune-telling machine. Karnak offers them an impossible bargain: one of them may return to life, but only if the group can decide who deserves the chance. To make their cases, the teenagers recount the selves they hid behind school reputations, fantasies, bravado, and fear.

Ocean O’Connell Rosenberg, the choir’s domineering overachiever, assumes her accomplishments make her the natural choice. Noel Gruber, isolated as the only gay boy in town, imagines a glamorous, doomed alter ego—Monique Gibeau—as a way to claim the dramatic life he never felt permitted to live. Mischa Bachinski projects the image of a hardened rapper, yet reveals the tenderness of his devotion to Talia, the fiancée he knows only through the internet. Ricky Potts, unable to speak in life, finds his voice in death and describes the rich interstellar world that flourished inside his mind. Constance Blackwood, known as “the nicest girl in town,” admits the anger, loneliness, and self-contempt beneath her obliging exterior.

The sixth student, Jane Doe, cannot remember her name, history, or face; she is defined only by absence. Her terror of being no one gradually forces the others to confront how fragile their own claims to importance are. Ocean initially treats the contest as something to win, but begins to understand that the group’s worth cannot be measured by achievement or suffering. She ultimately gives Jane the chance to live. Jane is restored as Penny Lamb, while the remaining choir members accept their deaths as Karnak’s power fades and their limbo comes to an end.

The musical explores mortality, identity, and the longing to have one’s life recognized as meaningful. It argues that empathy—not competition or self-mythology—allows people to see one another fully, even at the edge of oblivion.

rocky.en:
In working-class Philadelphia, Rocky Balboa scrapes by as a small-time club boxer and occasional collector for a loan shark. Though he wants a future in the ring, his trainer Mickey sees only squandered ability and urges him to give up. Rocky’s modest life changes when he begins courting Adrian Pennino, the painfully shy clerk at a pet shop. Adrian is accustomed to living under the domineering shadow of her brother, Paulie, and at first resists Rocky’s clumsy invitations. Yet his persistence and sincerity gradually win her trust. On their awkward first date at an ice rink, and later in Rocky’s cramped apartment, the two begin to recognize in each other a longing to be seen, valued, and loved.

Meanwhile, world heavyweight champion Apollo Creed is scheduled to defend his title in Philadelphia on New Year’s Day, during the nation’s Bicentennial celebrations. When his opponent withdraws with an injury, Apollo refuses to cancel the lucrative spectacle. Looking for a local unknown who can be marketed as a patriotic novelty, he selects Rocky, whose ring nickname, “the Italian Stallion,” seems perfect for the occasion. Rocky initially doubts the offer, aware that Apollo and the press regard him as an easy opponent. But the chance to prove that he is more than a loser pushes him to accept.

Mickey returns to train Rocky in earnest, and Rocky undertakes a punishing regimen across Philadelphia: running, boxing, and working in a meat locker. As public attention grows, so does Rocky’s bond with Adrian. She gives him emotional courage, while Rocky helps her claim a more confident voice. On the night of the championship, Rocky enters the ring resolved not necessarily to win, but to go the distance against the undefeated champion. In a brutal, exhausting fight, he repeatedly rises after being knocked down, forcing Apollo to confront an opponent he has underestimated. By the final bell, Rocky has transformed his own sense of what he can endure and achieve.

The musical is about resilience, self-worth, and the decision to keep standing when others expect defeat. Its central victory lies in Rocky and Adrian finding strength through love, mutual belief, and the courage to define success for themselves.

rudolph the red nosed reindeer.en:
Sam the Snowman recounts the year Christmas nearly failed. In Christmastown at the North Pole, Santa Claus and Mrs. Claus oversee a hectic holiday season while the elves make toys and the reindeer prepare for their future roles on Santa’s sleigh team. Donner and Mrs. Donner proudly introduce their newborn son, Rudolph—but his glowing red nose immediately marks him as different. Though Rudolph tries to hide it, the other young reindeer laugh at him during Coach Comet’s flying lessons, especially the boastful Fireball. Hurt and humiliated, Rudolph runs away.

Elsewhere, Hermey the Elf confesses that he does not want to make toys; he dreams of becoming a dentist. Branded a misfit by the Boss Elf, Hermey leaves Christmastown too. He and Rudolph meet on the road, and their shared sense of not belonging quickly makes them friends. Their travels bring them to the adventurous prospector Yukon Cornelius, who is searching for silver and gold, and then into danger when they encounter Bumble, the enormous Abominable Snow Monster.

After escaping Bumble, Rudolph and Hermey reach the Island of Misfit Toys, ruled over by King Moonracer. There they meet toys who have been rejected because of their unusual traits, including Charlie-in-the-Box and the Spotted Elephant. Rudolph promises to ask Santa to find homes for them. Yet Rudolph worries that he may endanger his friends and family, so he leaves on his own. As winter passes, he returns to Christmastown and discovers that his family and Clarice, the gentle reindeer who had encouraged him, have been searching for him. Yukon confronts Bumble and removes the monster’s threatening teeth, revealing that Bumble can become a helpful member of the community.

On Christmas Eve, a fierce snowstorm makes flying impossible. Santa realizes that Rudolph’s shining nose can cut through the darkness and asks him to lead the sleigh. Rudolph guides Santa safely across the sky, while Santa also fulfils Rudolph’s promise by delivering the Misfit Toys to children.

The musical celebrates belonging, self-acceptance, and the courage to be different. It shows that qualities once mocked or feared can become a source of strength, friendship, and purpose.

ruthless.en:
Eight-year-old Tina Denmark is certain she was born for stardom. Living with her sweetly conventional mother, Judy Denmark, Tina sets her sights on playing the title role in her school production of Pippi in Tahiti, The Musical. Her formidable would-be agent, Sylvia St. Croix, recognizes Tina’s uncanny talent and feeds her appetite for fame. But Tina’s teacher and director, Miss Myrna Thorn, gives the role to Louise Lerman, leaving Tina as understudy. Refusing to accept a supporting position, Tina engineers an “accident” that removes Louise from the cast permanently, allowing Tina to take centre stage. The triumph does not last: once Tina’s crime comes to light, she is sent to the Daisy Clover School for Psychopathic Ingenues.

Tina’s grandmother, the acid-tongued theatre critic Lita Encore, arrives amid the aftermath and exposes the theatrical history behind the Denmark household. Judy learns that her birth mother was Ruth Del Marco, a celebrated Broadway star whose career and life were devastated by Lita’s reviews. Stirred by the revelation that performance runs in her blood, Judy abandons domestic anonymity, adopts the name Ginger Del Marco, and becomes a Broadway diva herself.

Years later, journalist Emily Block probes Ginger’s carefully constructed public image and uncovers her past as Judy Denmark—as well as the existence of Tina. Tina returns from the Daisy Clover School to Ginger’s luxurious penthouse, where Ginger’s unstable assistant Eve becomes increasingly possessive and resentful. Mother and daughter are reunited, but their reunion makes clear that Tina’s ambition has not diminished. As identities, family histories, and old rivalries collide, the household becomes a new stage for betrayals, reversals, and increasingly extravagant revelations. Tina ultimately asserts her claim to the spotlight with the ruthless conviction that first defined her.

The musical satirizes the entertainment industry’s hunger for child stars, celebrity reinvention, and theatrical ego. It treats ambition, inheritance, and maternal rivalry as both darkly comic forces and engines of melodrama.

schmigadoon.en:
Josh Skinner and Melissa Gimble, two New York doctors whose long relationship has stalled, set out on a backpacking trip in the hope of reconnecting. Instead, another argument leaves them lost in the woods, where they cross a bridge and arrive in Schmigadoon: a sunny, self-contained town in which everyone expresses life through song, dance, and unwavering romantic certainty. When the pair tries to leave, the bridge inexplicably returns them to the town square. A Leprechaun reveals the condition of their escape: they must find true love.

Melissa is enchanted by Schmigadoon’s warmth and possibility, while Josh treats its musical logic with impatience and disbelief. Their search for a way out pulls them into the townspeople’s intersecting lives. Melissa finds herself drawn to Danny Bailey, the charismatic, troubled man associated with the local carnival. Josh attracts the energetic Betsy McDonough, who pursues romance with wholehearted abandon, and develops a connection with Emma Tate, the thoughtful schoolteacher. Meanwhile, the town’s polished cheer masks frustrations and secrets: Mayor Menlove struggles to live honestly beneath the expectations of his office and marriage to Florence; Mildred Layton enforces the community’s strict propriety while concealing her own discontent; and other residents confront desires that do not fit the roles Schmigadoon has assigned them.

As romances shift and the town’s carefully ordered surface begins to crack, Josh and Melissa are forced to stop treating their unhappiness as the other person’s fault. The apparent solution—finding a new, storybook partner—proves less meaningful than facing the emotional habits that have kept them distant. By acknowledging what they need, what they fear, and what they still choose in one another, they finally satisfy the town’s demand for true love. Changed by the experience, they cross the bridge and return to their own world together.

The musical explores love as an active, honest choice rather than a perfect romantic ending. It also contrasts comforting fantasy with the messier work of self-knowledge, authenticity, and mutual acceptance.

scrooge.en:
On Christmas Eve in London, Ebenezer Scrooge, a wealthy moneylender, rejects every appeal to generosity. He keeps his exhausted clerk, Bob Cratchit, at work until late, dismisses his nephew Harry’s invitation to Christmas dinner, and turns away those seeking charity. While the city prepares for celebration, the Cratchit family shops modestly and looks forward to a precious holiday together, especially Bob’s frail but bright-spirited son, Tiny Tim. Alone in his gloomy rooms, Scrooge is confronted by the ghost of his dead business partner, Jacob Marley. Burdened by the chains forged through a selfish life, Marley warns Scrooge that he may yet escape a similar fate—but only if he heeds three visiting spirits.

The Ghost of Christmas Past takes Scrooge through scenes that reveal the roots of his isolation: his unhappy childhood, lonely schooldays, and a happier period as an apprentice under the warm-hearted Mr. Fezziwig. He also sees Young Scrooge lose Isabel, whose love cannot survive his growing devotion to money. The Ghost of Christmas Present then shows him the life he has chosen to ignore: Harry’s convivial household, the kindness and resilience of the Cratchits, and Tiny Tim’s vulnerable health. Though the Cratchits have little, their home is filled with affection.

Finally, the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come shows a colder London. Businessmen speak casually of an unloved man’s death; Mrs. Dilber and others sell the dead man’s possessions; and the Cratchits grieve beside Tiny Tim’s empty place. Scrooge is forced to recognize the neglected grave as his own. Terrified, he vows to change. Awaking on Christmas morning, he sends a turkey to the Cratchits, gives freely to charity, joins Harry’s celebration, and becomes a compassionate friend to Bob and Tiny Tim.

The musical explores redemption as an active choice: Scrooge’s future changes because he accepts responsibility for the harm he has done. It celebrates generosity, human connection, and the possibility that compassion can restore a life hardened by fear and greed.

sinatra.en:
Frank Sinatra stands on the brink of a career-defining appearance at New York City’s Paramount Theatre, where the young singer’s voice turns him into a national sensation. Surrounded by devoted fans and driven by the ambitions of his close-knit Italian-American family, Frank rises swiftly from band vocalist to solo star. His wife, Nancy Sinatra, and their children represent the home life he wants to protect, while his mother Dolly and father Marty take fierce pride in the son whose success seems to validate all their sacrifices.

But fame brings pressures that neither Frank nor his family can contain. In Hollywood, he is drawn into a volatile romance with film star Ava Gardner. Their attraction is immediate and consuming, yet it puts Frank’s marriage, public standing and sense of self under increasingly painful strain. Gossip columnist Hedda Hopper and journalist Lee Mortimer turn his private turmoil into public spectacle, while friends and fellow performers—including Judy Garland, Billie Holiday, Nat King Cole and Gene Kelly—move through a changing entertainment world that both celebrates and exploits celebrity.

Frank’s professional fortunes then collapse as quickly as they rose. Record and film opportunities disappear; audiences thin out; and the force of his own choices leaves him isolated from Nancy, his children and the career that once seemed secure. With Ava’s relationship with him also fraying, he confronts despair and the possibility that his greatest days are behind him. Yet Frank refuses to accept obscurity. Returning to his craft with renewed resolve, he finds an artistic partner in arranger Nelson Riddle, rebuilds his professional life, and fights his way toward a comeback that restores both his confidence and his standing.

The musical explores the cost of ambition when public adoration collides with private responsibility. It is also a story of reinvention: a flawed performer facing failure, love, family and shame before reclaiming his voice.

smartest giant in town.en:
George is tired of being known as the scruffiest giant in town. His old gown and worn-out sandals make him feel untidy and unfashionable, so when he spots a shop selling clothes made especially for giants, he eagerly goes inside. He emerges delighted with his transformation: smart trousers, a crisp shirt, a striped tie, shiny shoes and a fine belt. Striding through town, George sings proudly that he is now the smartest giant in town.

His celebration is interrupted when he meets a giraffe with a cold neck. George gives the giraffe his striped tie to use as a warm scarf, and continues home feeling pleased that he could help. Soon he finds a goat whose sail has blown away, leaving his boat stuck. George removes his new shirt and offers it as a sail. Further along, a fox has lost its sleeping bag and is shivering in the cold; George gives away one of his socks as a cosy replacement. At each encounter, George parts with another treasured piece of his new outfit, choosing an animal’s need over his own wish to look smart.

Eventually, George meets a family of mice whose home has been destroyed. Without hesitation, he gives them his shoe as a shelter. Now barefoot and left only in his underwear, George feels cold, scruffy and rather sad. He returns to the shop hoping to buy another gown, but it has closed for the day. With nowhere else to turn, he puts on his familiar old gown and sandals again, convinced that he is no longer the smartest giant in town.

Then the animals George has helped arrive. Grateful for his kindness, they present him with a golden paper crown and proclaim him the kindest giant in town. George discovers that their affection means far more than his elegant new clothes ever did.

The show celebrates generosity, empathy and the practical power of helping others. It suggests that true greatness comes not from appearance or status, but from responding kindly when someone is in need.

spongebob musical.en:
In Bikini Bottom, SpongeBob SquarePants begins an ordinary day with Gary before heading to the Krusty Krab, where Mr. Krabs dismisses his dream of becoming manager: SpongeBob is, in his boss’s view, “just a simple sponge.” The routine shatters when Mount Humongous begins to rumble. Perch Perkins reports that the volcano is about to erupt, threatening to destroy the entire town. Panic spreads quickly. While the citizens consider evacuation, Plankton and Karen promote supposedly protective escape pods, secretly intending to hypnotize everyone into loving the Chum Bucket’s food.

SpongeBob refuses to surrender Bikini Bottom. Determined to prove that an ordinary sponge can matter, he recruits his best friend Patrick Star and the inventive Sandy Cheeks for a mission up Mount Humongous. Sandy plans to build an Eruption Interrupter that can stop the blast with bubbles, and the three set out to save their home. Meanwhile, Mr. Krabs turns the impending catastrophe into an “apocalypse sale,” Pearl resents his fixation on money, and Squidward Tentacles sees a chance to realize his own artistic ambitions at a benefit concert. Patrick’s accidental remarks also inspire a group of sardines, who elevate him into a reluctant spiritual leader.

As the deadline approaches, Bikini Bottom fragments under fear. The Mayor imposes authoritarian control, and an angry mob turns on Sandy, blaming her science for the crisis. SpongeBob and Sandy continue toward the volcano, but Plankton and Karen attempt to stop them with the Avalanche Maker 3000. Patrick ultimately rejects the worship offered by the sardines and rejoins his friends. Though the group is separated and Sandy must finish the ascent alone, she reaches the summit and deploys the Eruption Interrupter. The volcano does not erupt; bubbles drift down over a saved Bikini Bottom. Plankton and Karen’s deception is exposed, the townspeople regret their behavior, Sandy is welcomed back, and Mr. Krabs finally recognizes SpongeBob’s potential as a future manager.

The show is about optimism meeting action: courage does not depend on status, size, or conventional ideas of heroism. It also argues that communities survive crises through friendship, trust in one another, and cooperation rather than fear, greed, scapegoating, or manipulation.

summer.en:
Diva Donna, a poised and seasoned Donna Summer, steps before the audience to revisit the decisive chapters of her life. Her memories take shape through two younger selves: Duckling Donna, a gifted but uncertain girl growing up in Boston, and Disco Donna, the ambitious young woman determined to turn her voice into a future. In a crowded family home, Donna discovers the liberating force of singing, even as the expectations and tensions around her make self-belief difficult. Her parents, Andrew and Mary Gaines, and her sisters Mary Ellen and Dara form the emotional foundation from which she first reaches outward.

Disco Donna leaves Boston for Germany, where artistic possibility is shadowed by isolation and a damaging relationship with Gunther. She pursues work, learns to survive in unfamiliar places, and refuses to let fear extinguish her ambitions. Her path eventually carries her to the United States, where she encounters producer Giorgio Moroder, collaborator Pete Bellotte, and the head of Casablanca Records, Neil Bogart. Their partnership transforms her into a worldwide star, placing her at the center of the exuberant yet merciless nightlife of Los Angeles and Manhattan.

Success brings wealth, acclaim, and a carefully marketed public image, but it also leaves Donna struggling to protect her agency from executives, expectations, and the men who claim to know what her career requires. As her private burdens intensify, she confronts exhaustion, addiction, fear, and the emotional cost of being treated as an emblem rather than a person. Her sister Dara offers support during a particularly dark period, while Bruce Sudano becomes a steady, loving partner and helps Donna imagine a life beyond the demands of celebrity. Throughout, Diva Donna looks back with tenderness and candour, reconciling the frightened child, the fearless performer, and the woman who endured both.

The musical explores self-invention, artistic independence, and the price of fame. It also affirms the healing power of family, love, faith, and reclaiming one’s own voice.

sylvia.en:
Sylvia Pankhurst stands at the breaking point of her life: expelled in 1913 from the Women’s Social and Political Union led by her mother, Emmeline Pankhurst, and sister Christabel. From this rupture, the story moves back through the Pankhurst family’s political awakening in Manchester and London, where Sylvia grows up in the shadow of Emmeline’s formidable leadership and Christabel’s brilliance. The family builds the WSPU into a force demanding votes for women, joined by committed campaigners including Annie Kenney, Flora Drummond and Emily Davison.

As hostility intensifies, the organisation turns towards increasingly militant tactics. Demonstrations meet police violence, arrests and imprisonment; activists endure hunger strikes and brutal treatment. Sylvia shares the commitment to women’s enfranchisement and participates in the struggle, yet she cannot accept that the movement should pursue victory at any cost—or that it should speak chiefly for women with greater social privilege. Her relationship with the Labour leader Keir Hardie deepens her sense that the fight for political rights must also confront poverty, insecure work and class inequality.

The conflict becomes personal as Sylvia challenges Emmeline and Christabel’s authority. While they demand discipline and loyalty to the WSPU’s strategy, Sylvia insists on organising with and for working people. After her expulsion, she finds a new political home in London’s East End. With George Lansbury, she establishes the East London Federation of Suffragettes and helps working-class women claim a voice in public life. Sylvia leads an East End delegation to Parliament as hopes rise around a Conciliation Bill that could extend the franchise. But when the possibility of reform is made dependent on ending militant action, her attempt to persuade her mother and sister to compromise fails. Sylvia chooses her own path, accepting the cost of separation from the family movement she helped build.

The show explores the collision between family loyalty and political conviction, and the price of refusing to obey an unjust hierarchy—even within a movement for liberation. It argues that equality cannot stop at the ballot box: it must include the poor, working women and all those excluded from power.

thelma and louise.en:
Louise, a sharp-tongued waitress, invites her best friend Thelma—trapped in an unhappy marriage to the controlling Darryl—to leave town for a weekend escape. Thelma slips away with a note rather than ask permission, packing Darryl’s gun in her purse. Their first stop, a roadside honkytonk, turns the trip irrevocably darker: after Thelma accepts attention from Harlan and dances with him, he takes her outside and attacks her. Louise arrives with the gun and forces him to back away, but when Harlan taunts them as they leave, she shoots him dead.

Shaken, the women flee. Thelma wants to report what happened, but Louise believes the authorities will judge Thelma’s drinking and dancing rather than believe her account of the assault. They decide to head for Mexico, avoiding Texas for reasons Louise will not yet explain. Along the way, Thelma calls Darryl and begins to push back against his demands, while Louise’s boyfriend Jimmy tries to persuade her to return. Their flight brings them into contact with JD, a charming young drifter whom Thelma invites along. After a night together, Thelma discovers that JD has vanished with Louise’s savings.

Devastated but newly determined, Thelma takes charge and robs a convenience store, applying what JD taught her. As police investigator Hal traces the women through witnesses, phone calls, and the unmistakable green Thunderbird, their journey becomes a public manhunt. Thelma and Louise evade a state trooper, humiliate Darryl through a phone call, and turn their desperation into a fierce, defiant partnership. Yet the net closes around them. Reaching the Grand Canyon with law enforcement surrounding them, they reject Hal’s plea to surrender. Holding hands, they choose to keep driving rather than submit to capture.

The musical explores friendship becoming a source of liberation under extreme pressure. It confronts misogyny, violence, and institutional judgment while asking what freedom can mean for women denied safe or ordinary choices.

thrill me.en:
At Joliet Prison in 1958, Nathan Leopold appears before a parole board for the fifth time, required once again to explain the crime that has kept him imprisoned for decades. Pressed to reveal his motive, Nathan relives the summer of 1924 in Chicago, when his consuming desire for Richard Loeb drew him back into Richard’s orbit. Richard has returned from college cool and withholding, while Nathan desperately seeks to restore their intimate bond before they leave for separate law schools. Richard offers him a way back in: an evening of arson at an abandoned warehouse. The shared danger reignites their connection, but it also establishes the unequal terms of their relationship.

Nathan soon begs Richard to abandon crime, yet Richard—intoxicated by ideas of intellectual superiority and contempt for ordinary rules—demands a formal bargain instead. They create a written contract: Richard will give Nathan the affection he craves, while Nathan will provide loyalty, ingenuity, and assistance in Richard’s escalating criminal games. Signed in blood, the pact binds them through thefts, vandalism, and fires. Nathan finds himself increasingly uneasy, but every protest risks Richard’s rejection.

Petty offenses eventually lose their appeal for Richard. He proposes an act so audacious that it will prove their supposed superiority: they will abduct and murder a child, then stage a ransom scheme and evade detection. Nathan recoils, yet agrees rather than lose Richard. They prepare their tools, select Bobby Franks, and carry out the plan. What Richard imagines as a flawless crime begins to unravel when a small but devastating piece of evidence leads investigators toward them. Their confidence fractures under questioning, and their partnership—built on manipulation, fear, and longing—cannot withstand the consequences.

Returning to the parole hearing, Nathan finally gives the account he has withheld for years. He receives parole, but the prospect of freedom is shadowed by Richard’s absence: Richard has long since died in prison, leaving Nathan to confront the life and guilt that remain.

The musical examines obsessive love turned into control, and the terrible price of surrendering moral judgment for another person’s approval. It also exposes how fantasies of superiority and “perfect” control collapse when confronted with human conscience, chance, and responsibility.

trainspotting.en:
In 1980s Edinburgh, Mark Renton drifts through life with Sick Boy, Spud, Tommy, Begbie and Kelly, a tight but unstable circle bound by drugs, drink, bravado and a shared contempt for respectable “normal” life. Their days revolve around finding money, finding heroin and escaping consequences, while each friendship is strained by rivalry, self-interest and the danger that follows their addictions. Renton is clever, restless and increasingly conscious that the life he has chosen is consuming him; yet every attempt to step away pulls him back toward the people and habits he knows.

The group’s chaos takes different forms. Spud’s gentleness and loyalty leave him especially vulnerable, while Sick Boy turns charm and cynicism into weapons. Begbie, volatile and violent, brings menace even when he is not using drugs, turning ordinary social encounters into threats. Tommy, initially more hopeful and disciplined than the others, is gradually drawn into their destructive orbit. Around them, women including Kelly, Alison and Lizzie confront the emotional and physical costs of the men’s behaviour, while Renton’s parents, Cathy and Davie, represent the worried domestic world he repeatedly abandons and returns to.

As Renton tries to get clean, the apparent promise of a fresh start exposes how difficult it is to change without changing one’s environment. Relapses, betrayals and loss make clear that addiction is not simply an individual choice but a force that reshapes friendships, love, family and identity. When an opportunity arises to leave Edinburgh’s deadening cycle behind, Renton faces a decisive choice: remain loyal to a group that has repeatedly harmed him, or seize a future that may require him to betray them first. The story drives toward that act of escape with no easy moral resolution.

The show explores addiction, alienation and the urge to reject a conventional life whose promises feel hollow. It also examines friendship as both refuge and trap, asking what survival costs when loyalty, self-preservation and betrayal become inseparable.

two strangers carry a cake across new yo.en:
Dougal Todd, an irrepressibly optimistic young Englishman, arrives in New York at Christmas for the wedding of his wealthy father, Mark—a man he has never met. He is collected from JFK by Robin Rainey, Melissa’s weary, sharp-tongued sister. Robin has little patience for Dougal’s tourist enthusiasm or his belief that the city will resemble the films he loves, but she reluctantly brings him into Manhattan. The next day, Melissa sends Robin to collect the extravagant wedding cake from Flatbush, and Dougal insists on accompanying her. Carrying the cake across the city forces the mismatched pair into an awkward day together. They talk about Robin’s disappointing dating life, her affection for the neighbourhood where she grew up, and Dougal’s intense hope that meeting Mark will complete something missing in his life.

Their fragile cooperation collapses when Robin accidentally drops and destroys part of the cake outside Melissa’s home. Already alienated from her sister and trapped in a life that feels stagnant, Robin resists Dougal’s cheerful advice to simply be happy. Yet Dougal persuades her to abandon her responsibilities for one night. With Mark’s credit card, they indulge in a whirlwind Manhattan adventure: hotels, shops, landmarks, and a version of New York that both of them can briefly inhabit without consequence. By morning, however, the fantasy gives way to discomfort and hard truths.

Robin reveals that Melissa invited Dougal partly to hurt Mark after his infidelity, and that Mark has kept Dougal’s existence hidden. Dougal refuses to let the revelation destroy his long-awaited chance to meet his father—until he learns that Mark’s affair was with Robin. Their argument separates them just as the wedding approaches. Outside Trinity Church, Dougal finally recognises that the father he imagined cannot be found inside. He leaves rather than enter. Robin, confronting her habit of withdrawing from people and possibilities, decides to change. They reunite at a Chinese restaurant, share a stolen tier of wedding cake, invent their own ceremony, and spend the remaining hours together before Dougal returns home.

The musical is about the gap between fantasies and the imperfect people who replace them. It finds hope in choosing honesty, connection, and a self-made sense of belonging when family, romance, and even a dream city fail to follow the script.

unauthorized hallmark ish parody musical.en:
Holly Mark, an exhausted executive from Big City, heads back to Small Town for Christmas to help her mother, Merry, keep the family business afloat. Determined to handle the visit efficiently and return to her career, Holly instead finds herself pulled into a hometown holiday whirlwind: festive traditions, a high-stakes cookie contest, an impending corporate merger, and the alarming news that a moose is loose in town. The seemingly simple trip becomes a crisis when the town’s Christmas spirit—and perhaps its future—appears to be at risk.

Back home, Holly reconnects with Mark Hall, the town sheriff and her old flame. Their uneasy reunion stirs unresolved attraction as Mark represents the life and community Holly left behind. Meanwhile, Cookie, a formidable local rival, turns the cookie contest into a battleground of ambition, suspicion, and escalating sabotage. With Cody caught up in the unfolding schemes and townspeople embracing each new absurd complication, Holly must navigate family expectations, professional pressure, and a conspiracy surrounding the competition.

As the corporate threat closes in, Holly faces a choice between the advancement promised by Big City and the relationships she has rediscovered in Small Town. The missing pieces of her family history, including the truth about her absent father’s unusually Christmas-centered work, add still more surprises to the mounting holiday chaos. The runaway moose, the contest scandal, and the merger collide in a final push to preserve the town’s celebration. Holly ultimately learns that saving Christmas requires more than solving a business problem: it means trusting the people around her, confronting what she has avoided, and recognizing what Mark, Merry, and the community mean to her. With the crisis resolved, romance and communal celebration prevail.

The show celebrates connection, belonging, and the possibility of choosing love and community over relentless career ambition. It also finds warmth in holiday excess, turning rivalry, romance, family secrets, and seasonal chaos into a joyful affirmation of shared tradition.

waistwatchers.en:
At Cook’s Women’s Gym, four women confront the daily pressures of diets, exercise, aging, romance, and the endlessly shifting idea of the “perfect” body. An exuberant personal trainer keeps the sessions moving at full speed, urging the women to stretch, sweat, dance, and push past their excuses. But the gym quickly becomes more than a place to work out: it is a refuge where candid confessions, comic arguments, and private insecurities can safely surface.

Connie arrives burdened by self-consciousness about her weight and by the fear that her husband no longer finds her desirable. Around her, Carla, Cindy, and Cheryl bring their own complicated relationships with food, appearance, love, sex, and self-worth. Their conversations swing between calorie-counting schemes, fantasies of instant transformations, frustrations with exercise, and memories or encounters that expose what lies beneath their jokes. Each woman tries to reconcile what she believes she should look like with who she actually is, while the trainer’s relentless optimism and the group’s shared routines turn individual struggles into collective entertainment.

As the women work through their problems, they repeatedly turn embarrassment into performance. Their anxieties are enlarged into comic musical numbers, and everyday battles—resisting temptation, fitting into clothes, facing a partner, or stepping on a scale—become occasions for laughter and solidarity. The group’s teasing can be sharp, but it is rooted in affection: they recognize versions of themselves in one another’s fears. Rather than following a single dramatic quest, the story builds through these intersecting personal revelations, showing how friendship gives each woman room to be vulnerable, angry, hopeful, and imperfect.

By the end, the women have not discovered a magic diet or achieved a final, flawless transformation. They have instead found strength in being seen honestly by friends, in laughing at the demands imposed on them, and in continuing to show up for themselves and each other.

The musical explores body image, food, aging, desire, and the pressure to measure personal worth through appearance. Above all, it argues that humor, friendship, and self-acceptance can be more sustaining than any promise of physical perfection.

wanted.en:
In 1893 Texas, twin sisters Mary and Martha Clarke face the destruction of their family when their mother, Tallulah, is trapped beneath a crushing sharecropping debt that threatens their home and future. Light-skinned Black women in a violently segregated world, the sisters discover that they can pass as white beyond the boundaries imposed on their family. Leaving home to find a way to save Tallulah, they enter a West where appearance determines safety, opportunity, and who is believed.

Their search brings them to the world of Jesse Whitewater, a prosperous white hotel and saloon owner whose charm conceals the power he holds over those around him. Mary, careful and inwardly conflicted by the freedom their assumed identity affords, draws Jesse’s attention. Martha, more forceful and unwilling to accept injustice quietly, forms a connection with Elijah, a Black man employed in Jesse’s orbit. Around them are Flo and Sissy, women who see the risks beneath the sisters’ new lives and the precariousness of survival in a society built on racial hierarchy.

As the debt remains unpaid and the forces threatening the Clarke family press closer, Mary and Martha are driven from desperate improvisation into open rebellion. Passing as white grants them access to spaces and resources otherwise withheld from them, but it also places them in continual danger: exposure could mean the loss of everything, while success demands that they keep concealing parts of themselves. Their different temperaments sharpen the strain between them, even as their shared purpose keeps them bound together.

The sisters ultimately choose to seize the money and power denied to their family, crossing the line from farm girls into notorious outlaws. Guided by the presence of the Kinfolk—ancestral voices surrounding their journey—they pursue a future in which Tallulah’s home, their family’s dignity, and their own autonomy cannot be taken from them. Their flight turns them into figures of legend: women whose defiance reshapes the terms on which they will live.

whispering jack.en:
In 1986, John Farnham is a gifted but financially strained performer, a father nearing middle age whose earlier fame has faded while Australian rock culture moves around him. Still playing club dates and carrying the weight of a career that has never quite delivered the security he needs, John faces a choice: accept that his best years are behind him, or risk everything on one more attempt to be heard. His wife, Jill Farnham, understands both the warmth and restlessness behind his public persona, while the people around him must decide whether his ambition is faith, folly, or both.

John reconnects with manager Glenn Wheatley, whose belief in John’s voice is matched by his willingness to gamble on an unlikely comeback. Joined by Gaynor Wheatley and a new circle of collaborators, John begins work in a suburban garage in outer Melbourne. There, with producer Ross Fraser, musician David Hirschfelder, singers Venetta Fields and Cherie Romaro, and fellow artists including Graeham Goble, Beeb Birtles, Brett Garsed and Darryl Sambell, he tries to turn uncertainty into an album with a sound strong enough to cut through the noise.

The recording process becomes a test of nerve. John has to confront old disappointments, the pressure of providing for his family, scepticism from the industry and his own fear that the public has already made up its mind about him. As the songs take shape, Glenn pushes for a bold release strategy, and 2DayFM executive Cherie Romaro takes the decisive step of putting “You’re the Voice” on air again and again. The song catches fire, transforming a precarious recording project into a national phenomenon. John’s return culminates not simply in renewed popularity, but in the recognition that the voice he doubted still has the power to unite a vast audience.

white christmas.en:
On Christmas Eve 1944, Army entertainers Bob Wallace and Phil Davis perform for the 151st Division on the Western Front. Their commanding officer, Major General Henry Waverly, announces that he is being reassigned; when danger strikes, Phil saves Bob’s life, binding the two men in lasting friendship. Ten years later, Bob and Phil are celebrated producers and performers in New York. Phil introduces Bob to the Haynes Sisters, Betty and Judy, a talented sister act facing trouble with their travelling show. The men help them out of an awkward situation and, intrigued by the women, follow them to their seasonal engagement at the Columbia Inn in Pine Tree, Vermont.

They arrive to find an unusually snowless Vermont and a nearly empty inn. To their surprise, its owner is General Waverly, now retired and struggling financially after putting his savings into the business. Bob, Phil, Betty and Judy resolve to save the inn by mounting a lavish Christmas production that will attract guests regardless of the weather. Inn concierge Martha Watson and the General’s spirited granddaughter, Susan Waverly, join the enterprise as rehearsals transform the quiet lodge into a bustling theatrical headquarters.

Romance develops unevenly. Phil and Judy grow closer, while Bob and Betty fall for one another but are hindered by Bob’s reserve and Betty’s distrust of grand gestures. When Betty overhears part of Bob’s private plan to summon the General’s former troops, she mistakenly concludes that Bob intends to exploit Waverly’s predicament and buy the inn. Hurt, she returns to New York, leaving the production and Bob behind. Bob attempts to explain, but the misunderstanding deepens until he turns to television to invite Waverly’s old division to Vermont.

On opening night, Waverly discovers that the show is also a tribute: his former soldiers have returned to honor the leader they never forgot. Betty realizes Bob’s true purpose and reunites with him; Phil and Judy also declare their love. With the inn filled, the show succeeds, snow finally falls, and the company celebrates together.

The musical centers on friendship, loyalty, and the enduring debt people feel toward those who supported them in difficult times. It also treats Christmas as a chance for reconciliation, community, generosity, and renewed hope.

wild about you.en:
On the day of his high-school graduation party, Billy is already uneasy about the future that everyone else seems eager to celebrate. Raised to believe that his mother, Olivia, abandoned him when he was a child, he has learned to live with the unanswered absence at the centre of his life. Then he discovers a trunk filled with letters Olivia wrote to him. The letters overturn the version of the past he has been given and draw Billy into the complicated, intimate story of a woman he never had the chance to know.

With his best friend Scoot beside him, Billy follows the trail Olivia has left behind. As the two move through the people, places, and turning points that shaped her life, Billy encounters the emotional consequences of Olivia’s choices: the romances she pursued, the relationships she could not sustain, and the fierce love she carried for her son. What begins as a search for facts becomes a confrontation with inherited hurt. Billy must decide whether the mother in the letters can be reconciled with the mother he has imagined for years.

Olivia’s story does not offer a simple explanation or a single villain. Instead, it reveals a person striving to be seen, loved, and forgiven while navigating a life marked by desire, fear, mistakes, and loss. The more Billy learns, the less certain he is that identity can be reduced to family stories told by others. His journey forces him to question not only where he came from, but what he wants to carry forward into adulthood.

By the time Billy reaches the emotional truth behind Olivia’s absence, graduation has become more than a ceremonial ending. It is the threshold of a new relationship with his own past—and a chance to step into the future with a fuller, more compassionate understanding of himself.

will rogers follies.en:
Will Rogers welcomes the audience to a dazzling Follies spectacular, where Florenz Ziegfeld’s unseen voice continually reshapes the evening into a suitably glamorous account of Will’s life. Between jokes, political asides, and rope tricks, Will takes the story back to Indian Territory, Oklahoma, where Clem Rogers and Will’s sisters celebrate his birth on the family ranch. Clem expects his only son to inherit the cattle business, but the restless young Will longs to see the wider world. At nineteen, he leaves home to pursue cowboy life in Argentina, while Ziegfeld insists that any proper romance requires Will to meet “the girl.”

That girl is Betty Blake. Though their real-life connection is initially plainspoken, Ziegfeld embellishes it with theatrical moonlight and spectacle. Will and Betty fall in love, but their wedding is postponed because Ziegfeld wants it to provide a grand first-act finish. In the meantime, Will’s career develops through Wild West entertainments, with Betty joining him on the road. They marry, raise four children—Will Jr., Mary, James, and Freddy—and travel through America as Will’s talent for roping and offhand humor turns him into a popular performer.

His success accelerates when he enters vaudeville and joins the Ziegfeld Follies. Soon he becomes a leading figure on stage, radio, in newspapers, and in Hollywood, beloved for treating public affairs with comic common sense. Fame brings wealth and influence: Will is even urged to seek the presidency. Yet the constant touring and performing distance him from Betty, who feels increasingly alone while he chases the next engagement.

As the Great Depression darkens the country, financial trouble strikes the world around Will, and he confronts the limits of celebrity and prosperity. He reconnects with Clem and offers the nation reassurance in hard times. Finally, his pilot friend Wiley Post invites him to fly to Alaska. Will bids Betty goodbye, boards the plane with Wiley, and the journey ends in the crash that takes both men’s lives.

The musical explores the tension between public adoration and private devotion, using show-business fantasy to frame a life of ambition, humor, and affection. It also celebrates generosity of spirit and plainspoken resilience while acknowledging the cost of a life lived in perpetual motion.

wonderland.en:
In present-day Manhattan, Alice Cornwinkle is an overworked, divorced mother struggling to hold her life together. She worries about money, clashes with her precocious daughter Chloe, and longs for the confidence she once had before adulthood became a succession of disappointments. One difficult night, after an argument with Chloe and a cascade of unpaid bills, Alice finds herself following a White Rabbit into a strange subterranean world called Wonderland. There she is greeted by a troupe of eccentric inhabitants who insist that she is the “real” Alice—the woman destined to challenge the tyrannical Queen of Hearts.

Alice encounters Caterpillar, a wise but elusive guide; the Cheshire Cat, whose shifting advice is both playful and unsettling; and Mad Hatter, March Hare, and Dormouse, who preside over a feverish tea party. Their world is dazzling, comic, and dangerous, yet its characters seem to echo elements of Alice’s own life and fears. The Queen of Hearts rules through intimidation, demanding obedience and staging trials whose verdicts are determined before anyone speaks. As Alice is drawn into the Queen’s orbit, she is tempted by the promise of escape: a place where she can shed responsibility, avoid painful choices, and remain someone other than the woman she has become.

Meanwhile, Chloe searches for her mother in Manhattan, refusing to accept that Alice has simply abandoned her. In Wonderland, Alice gradually understands that the Queen’s power depends on people surrendering their own agency. When the Queen threatens those Alice has come to care about, Alice must confront the insecurity and self-doubt that have shaped her life above ground. She rejects the Queen’s authority, reclaims her voice, and helps free Wonderland from its fearful order. Alice returns to Manhattan changed, ready to repair her relationship with Chloe and face her future with renewed courage.

At its heart, Wonderland is about reclaiming identity when life feels overwhelming. It explores courage, self-acceptance, and the choice to stop letting fear dictate one’s story.

pride.en:
In London in 1984, idealistic activist Mark Ashton brings together a small, outspoken group of lesbian and gay friends to support striking miners and their families. They call themselves Lesbians and Gays Support the Miners, raising cash in pubs, on the street and through ever-more audacious events. Among them are Mark’s steadfast friend Mike; Steph, who refuses to soften either her politics or her personality; Jonathan and his Welsh partner Gethin, whose bookshop Gay’s the Word becomes a vital base; and anxious, closeted student Joe, known to the group as “Bromley.” Drawn into the campaign almost by chance, Bromley finds in LGSM both a political purpose and the first place where he can begin to live honestly.

Unable to find a union branch willing to accept the donation, LGSM makes contact with a mining community in South Wales. Its members travel there uncertain of the reception they will receive. The villagers’ first response ranges from bemusement to suspicion, particularly from Maureen, but Hefina refuses to allow prejudice to dictate the community’s behaviour. Dai, the miners’ representative, Cliff, and the increasingly confident Siân help turn the visitors’ arrival into a genuine welcome. Shared meals, dancing, fundraising and blunt conversation slowly replace the initial awkwardness. Gethin’s return to Wales forces him to confront memories of leaving home after coming out, while Bromley’s growing confidence is tested by the fear of discovery and rejection.

The partnership is strained as the strike grinds on, police pressure and political hostility intensify, and homophobia surfaces on both sides. The threat of AIDS also casts a dark shadow over the London group. Yet the two communities keep choosing one another: the Welsh supporters stand alongside LGSM when it matters, and the London campaigners refuse to abandon the miners even as defeat becomes increasingly likely. By the end, the alliance has changed the participants’ sense of who belongs in their struggle and what collective action can achieve.

The musical explores solidarity across identities that initially seem irreconcilable, showing friendship as something made through practical commitment rather than sentiment alone. It also traces courage in private and public life: coming out, speaking up, resisting prejudice, and refusing isolation in the face of political defeat and personal loss.

our ladies of perpetual succour.en:
Six Catholic schoolgirls from Oban—Orla, Chell, Kay, Manda, Kylah and Fionnula—travel to Edinburgh to sing in a choir competition. Their teachers expect discipline, piety and musical excellence; the girls, facing a rare day beyond the reach of their convent school, see the city as a chance to drink, flirt, shop, escape and reinvent themselves. After performing, they slip away from supervision and fan out through Edinburgh, their lively collective adventure becoming a series of sharply different private journeys.

Fionnula drives the group’s bravado, pushing the others towards risk and excitement. Kylah, ambitious and self-possessed, pursues a possible route out of Oban through talent, attention and sheer determination. Manda’s apparent innocence masks confusion and longing, while Chell’s loyalty to her friends is tested as the day becomes more complicated. Kay, often treated as the outsider, carries the burden of an unplanned pregnancy and is forced to confront what the future may demand of her. Orla, whose life has already been shaped by illness, moves through the day with a mixture of comic openness and a hard-won awareness of mortality.

Alcohol, chance encounters, arguments and romantic or sexual experiments pull the friends apart and throw them back together. Their plans do not unfold as expected: excitement turns frightening, jokes expose real pain, and casual cruelty leaves scars. As night falls, the girls must negotiate the consequences of their choices—especially the crisis surrounding Kay—while the pull of home, school and their shared history remains unavoidable. By the end, the trip has become a threshold experience: not a clean break from childhood, but an unruly, emotional confrontation with the adult lives approaching them.

The musical explores friendship as both refuge and pressure, showing how loyalty can coexist with jealousy, judgment and betrayal. It sets youthful desire for freedom against religion, class, illness, sexuality and pregnancy, finding comedy and defiance alongside vulnerability.

vape the grease parody.en:
At Rydell High, new student Sandy arrives from Australia still glowing from a beach romance with Danny, the swaggering leader of the T-Bros. When they discover that they attend the same school, Sandy expects their connection to resume; Danny instead performs cool indifference for his friends, leaving her to navigate a hallway culture driven by vaping, phones, social status, dating-app logic, and conspicuous online self-presentation. The #PinkSquad—Rizzo, Frenchy, Marty, and snack-devoted Jan—takes Sandy in, though their advice on love, sex, image, and confidence is as erratic as the school’s rules.

Danny’s crowd includes his loyal, possibly more-than-platonic best friend Kenickie and the routinely overlooked Sonny. Their everyday rivalries and poses spiral through comic set pieces, while characters openly acknowledge the absurdity of a high school populated by adults who erupt into synchronized songs. Sandy and Danny repeatedly circle one another: she asks for respect and clarity, while he keeps trying to preserve his reputation without admitting how much he cares. Their friction reaches its public peak at the school dance, where Danny’s attempt to impress Sandy collapses amid competition, jealousy, and the arrival of the flamboyant Cha Cha DiGregorio.

Meanwhile, Frenchy’s attempt to reinvent herself through beauty school becomes a glittering fiasco, interrupted by Teen Angel’s extravagant warning that a makeover cannot solve every problem. Rizzo projects fearless sexual confidence but reveals more vulnerability beneath it, challenging the assumptions that turn young women’s choices into gossip. Principal Miss Lynch presides over the chaos with elderly confusion, while cheerleader Patty Simcox appears in puppet form, a deliberately surreal embodiment of school-spirit perfection.

At the drive-in, Danny finally confronts the difference between wanting Sandy and treating her well. By the school’s final celebration, the lovers move toward reunion not through simple conformity but through a knowingly exaggerated reinvention, as every clique, flirtation, and rivalry collides in a vapor-clouded finale.

midnight.en:
In the nineteenth-century American South, twelve lives—six Black and six white—are bound together by the violent social order they have inherited. At the story’s centre is Rail, a young Black man who was sold into slavery as a child. He longs for a life larger than the role forced upon him and finds warmth with Lily Rose, a spirited young Black woman whose affection offers him a fragile sense of hope. Their bond develops amid the watchful, restrictive world around them, where even private happiness is vulnerable to the demands of power and property.

Elsewhere, Scarlet, Rail’s young owner, prepares for a ball held by her family and becomes infatuated with Richard, a wealthy neighbouring man. Richard’s ambitions lead him to select Rail to work with him and a mixed group of Black and white labourers on the house he plans to build. What begins as an arrangement shaped by hierarchy gradually becomes something more unsettling to everyone around them: Rail and Richard discover an unexpected intellectual and emotional connection. Their growing friendship turns into mutual respect, then into a love that defies the racial, social, and personal boundaries governing their lives.

As the other characters—among them Charlotte, Ethel, Happy, Violet, Harry, Horace, Squeak, and Sylvester—respond to shifting loyalties, desires, resentments, and fears, the web of relationships tightens. Each person sees the others through assumptions formed by race, class, gender, and status, yet each is also confronted with feelings that refuse to fit those assumptions. When Rail is brutally attacked, the consequences spread through every relationship, compelling those involved to reckon with the harm they have enabled, the identities they have performed, and the choices still available to them.

At its heart, Midnight examines love and connection under a system designed to divide people. It asks whether empathy can survive inherited prejudice, and whether people can claim moral agency even when they cannot choose the circumstances into which they are born.

one sleepy night.en:
In present-day Detroit, retired Grandpa Benny Wilson finds himself drifting apart from both his wife, LaToya, and the warmth of the holiday season. When their granddaughter, Shantelle, reveals that she does not know the Christmas story, Benny reluctantly takes up the task of telling it. With the help of a magical telescope, the Wilson family is drawn into the tale itself, their familiar relationships transformed into figures on a perilous nighttime journey.

Benny becomes Kaspar, the determined leader of the Wise Men, while LaToya becomes Mrs. K. Shantelle takes command as the Boss Shepherd, guiding her three older brothers through the confusion and excitement that surround an extraordinary announcement. Across deserts, fields, and crowded roads, the travelers confront wrong turns, comic setbacks, doubt, and the pressures of following a star whose destination remains uncertain. The Angel of the Lord brings startling news, setting shepherds and Wise Men alike in motion toward Bethlehem.

As the separate groups press onward, their journeys gradually converge. Kaspar must learn that leadership is not control, Mrs. K. challenges the assumptions that keep the travelers divided, and Shantelle discovers that courage can mean speaking up even when those around her dismiss her. Their arguments, accidents, and moments of fear give way to cooperation as each character recognizes that the journey is larger than personal pride. At last, all roads lead to Bethlehem, where the travelers gather at the manger and encounter a quiet, life-changing wonder.

The story then returns to Detroit. Carrying the insight of the journey back into their own lives, Benny and LaToya confront the distance between them. In an everyday check-out line, a small but meaningful act opens the way for forgiveness, and the family reunites in joy late one sleepy night.

The musical explores love as a choice renewed through listening, humility, and reconciliation. It also celebrates faith, family, and the possibility that an ordinary night can become a moment of shared hope.

a mardi gras carol.en:
On Lundi Gras in New Orleans, Ebeneezer “Bubba” Scrooge is determined to shut himself away from the city’s Carnival spirit. Bitter and dismissive, Bubba sees Mardi Gras as nothing more than noise, beads, king cake, and needless commotion; the parades, music, costumes, and exuberant neighbors that delight everyone else only deepen his irritation. While the city readies itself for celebration, Bubba’s refusal to join in leaves him isolated from the community around him.

That night, however, he is confronted by three spectral visitors: the ghosts of Carnival Krewes Past, Present, and Future. Each takes Bubba on a journey through a different vision of New Orleans and its people. The first forces him to revisit the experiences that hardened his heart and obscured the joy he once knew. The second immerses him in the living, breathing Carnival celebration he has rejected: streets alive with jazz, parades, neighborhood rituals, and the warmth of people who make room for one another. Bubba begins to understand that the season’s pleasures are not simply decorations or distractions, but expressions of belonging.

The final visitor shows him the cost of continuing unchanged. In a future without generosity, connection, or shared celebration, Bubba sees how thoroughly he has cut himself off from the life of his city.
