Faced with the prospect of being remembered only for his resentment, he recognizes that his contempt has deprived him as much as anyone else. By morning, he resolves to embrace the spirit he once scorned, opening himself to his neighbors and to the pleasures of Carnival.

con musical.en:
The Con Musical centers on the high-stakes world of deception, following a group of ambitious figures whose personal histories and competing loyalties collide as a carefully constructed scheme begins to unravel. The story moves through a landscape where confidence, performance, and manipulation are tools of survival, and where each character must decide how far they are willing to go to obtain security, recognition, or escape. As alliances form and fracture, apparent victims reveal unexpected agency, while those who believe they control the game discover that they, too, may be targets.

At the heart of the action is an escalating con that depends on flawless timing and mutual trust—two conditions that become increasingly impossible to sustain. Secrets from the past intrude on the present plan, romantic and emotional attachments complicate calculated decisions, and the line between a professional deception and a personal betrayal grows blurred. Every new revelation forces the players to revise their assumptions about one another, turning what began as a promising opportunity into a volatile test of nerve. The closer the scheme comes to its intended payoff, the more the participants must confront the costs of the identities they have invented and the truths they have concealed.

Ultimately, the musical explores deception not merely as a criminal act but as a form of performance: the roles people adopt to be loved, protected, admired, or free. It asks whether real connection can survive a relationship built on illusion, and whether honesty is liberation—or simply another risk.

santa claus.en:
On Christmas Eve at the North Pole, Santa Claus and Mrs. Claus make an astonishing announcement: after one thousand years of delivering presents, Santa is ready to retire. The workshop elves are thrilled by the prospect of finding a successor, but Head Elf Henchy privately believes that the job should be his. He knows every rule, every route and every detail of Christmas operations, and he cannot imagine why anyone else could deserve the red suit.

Santa and Mrs. Claus have chosen Nick, a website designer and single father, as the next Santa. Nick is practical rather than magical, overwhelmed by the demands of the workshop and uncertain that he has the warmth, confidence or Christmas spirit required for the role. His daughter Beatrice—known as Bee—is far more at ease with problem-solving. Clever, self-reliant and technologically gifted, she quickly finds herself drawn into the extraordinary world behind Christmas, where every system must work perfectly before Santa’s sleigh can leave.

Henchy refuses to accept the decision. Determined to prove that Nick is unfit, he disrupts preparations with a series of mischievous schemes and pranks. As Christmas Eve approaches, the pressure on Nick intensifies: he must learn the traditions of the workshop, earn the trust of the elves and confront the possibility that he may fail when children around the world are counting on him. Bee repeatedly helps untangle the chaos, and the crisis gradually brings father and daughter closer together. Through the efforts of Santa, Mrs. Claus, Bee and the workshop community, Nick begins to understand that being Santa is less about knowing every answer than caring deeply enough to keep trying.

When Henchy’s sabotage threatens Christmas itself, the elves must decide whether to compete or cooperate. Nick rises to the challenge, Henchy is forced to face the consequences of his jealousy, and the workshop unites in time to keep Christmas alive. Santa can finally entrust the future to a new pair of hands.

The show celebrates generosity, teamwork and the idea that traditions can endure by being passed on rather than merely preserved. It also frames Christmas magic as an expression of empathy: a father and daughter reconnect, and an ordinary person discovers the capacity to do something extraordinary.

8 scott ave night at the towers.en:
In 8 Scott Ave – Night at the Towers, Jimmy Smith hears a talent quest advertised on the wireless: Tudor Towers, Rotorua’s glittering cabaret venue, is offering a $100 cash prize. Jimmy, a local bookie taking illegal bets on horse races, immediately sees a way to turn entertainment into profit. Rather than take the stage himself, he enters his four sisters, convinced that their family’s natural musical spirit can carry them to victory. The plan carries them far beyond the familiar routines of their everyday lives: work at the local sewing factory, evenings at home, and card games among family.

At Tudor Towers, the Smith sisters must confront a world of polish, spectacle and nightclub confidence. The modest women, unused to getting dressed up for a major performance, find themselves competing against experienced acts with Auckland engagements and television appearances behind them. Jimmy’s supposedly simple moneymaking scheme becomes a comic collision between the Smith family’s unvarnished warmth and the cabaret’s glamorous expectations. As they attempt to rise to the occasion, the family’s nerves, ambitions and loyalties are tested under the lights of a venue where music, dancing and larger-than-life entertainment set the rules.

The contest gives the Smiths a chance not merely to chase the prize, but to discover whether their ordinary lives have prepared them for an extraordinary night. Their journey through Tudor Towers turns the intimidating competition into a lively family adventure, as the sisters face seasoned rivals and Jimmy tries to keep his gamble from going awry. By placing the family in a setting so different from 8 Scott Ave, the story finds humour in their discomfort while allowing their songs and shared resilience to speak for themselves.

The musical explores family solidarity, working-class pride and the courage required to step into an unfamiliar world. It also celebrates how music can transform an ordinary household into a force capable of meeting glamour, competition and self-doubt head-on.

rollers forever.en:
On a Saturday night in Scotland, lifelong friends Jenny and Susan meet again at a familiar haunt from their youth. Their reunion quickly becomes a headlong return to the 1970s, when their lives revolved around tartan, pop records, shared crushes and an all-consuming devotion to the Bay City Rollers. As the two women talk, sing and tease one another, the ordinary details of teenage life re-emerge with vivid force: waiting by phone boxes, scanning mail-order catalogues, choosing outfits, navigating first romances and finding every possible excuse to be near the excitement surrounding their favourite band.

Their memories move between the present and the height of Rollermania. Young Jenny and Susan chase televised appearances, absorb the latest fashions and turn the band’s songs into the soundtrack for their hopes, friendships and private dramas. A first glimpse of the Rollers on television becomes an event of huge importance; a night of dancing beneath Edinburgh Castle feels like an escape into a world made larger, louder and more glamorous by music. Their fandom is not merely a pastime but a language through which they understand loyalty, desire, independence and belonging.

The reunion also brings Susan’s brother Alec into the evening. His larger-than-life personality and strong football loyalties create comic friction, while his own connection to the Rollers unsettles the assumptions Jenny and Susan formed years earlier. Old rivalries, embarrassments and family memories surface, but so does the recognition that the passions of adolescence never vanished as completely as adulthood suggested. As the night gathers momentum, the friends confront the distance between the girls they were and the people they have become, finding that their shared history still gives them a way back to one another.

country girl.en:
In rural Ireland, Rosie Ryan runs the small-town pub she inherited from her family, trying to keep its doors open while carrying the weight of the women who came before her—especially her late mother and grandmother. Fiercely independent yet increasingly restless, Rosie feels pulled between the life and community rooted in the pub and the possibility of leaving for Australia, where a new future seems to promise freedom, distance, and a chance to become someone beyond the role she has inherited.

One fateful night, Luke Adams walks into Rosie’s pub. Luke is an international country-music star whose public success masks a private exhaustion: the touring, attention, and constant demands of fame have left him longing for a place where he can simply breathe and be unknown. In Rosie’s corner of Ireland, far from the pressures of Nashville and the stage, Luke finds an unexpected refuge. Their meeting brings together two people who appear to want opposite things—Rosie dreams of escape, while Luke, who has spent his life in motion, yearns for stillness and belonging.

As their connection deepens, the pub becomes a meeting place not only for Rosie and Luke but for the people whose humour, opinions, loyalties, and histories shape Rosie’s world: Brenda, Blinky, Harry, Jazz, Mike, Peggy and Geraldine. Amid country songs, local warmth and emotional confrontations, Rosie must decide whether preserving her family’s legacy means staying exactly where she is or having the courage to redefine it for herself. Luke, meanwhile, faces the question of whether stepping away from the career that made him can cost him the future he has built.

Their romance is tested by the pressures of fame, distance, expectation and old wounds. Rosie and Luke must each confront the difference between running away and choosing a life, discovering that love cannot erase sacrifice—but it may help reveal where home truly lies.

The musical explores love across different worlds, the pull between roots and freedom, and the loneliness that can exist behind both ordinary responsibility and celebrity. At its heart, it asks whether home is the place one inherits, the place one leaves for, or the people one chooses to let in.

最美的一天.en:
Jingya has raised her spirited young daughter alone for years, ever since her husband vanished without explanation. Their life is modest but loving: Jingya works tirelessly, protects her daughter from adult worries, and turns ordinary routines into small adventures. Beneath this warmth, however, she carries loneliness, exhaustion, and an unspoken fear of what would happen to her child if she were no longer there.

That fear becomes real when Jingya is diagnosed with terminal stomach cancer. Given only a few months to live, she is thrown into an impossible choice. She can devote herself to painful, uncertain treatment in the hope of gaining more time, or she can accept the limits of her illness and make every remaining day with her daughter as full, secure, and joyful as possible. As Jingya struggles with anger, denial, and grief, she tries to arrange a future for the child who still expects her mother always to come home.

The story unfolds alongside a recurring fairy-tale vision. A hunchbacked girl longs to be seen and loved, while a winged woman appears as a figure of comfort, protection, and release. Their fable-like journey echoes Jingya’s own emotional passage: the child’s vulnerable need for reassurance, the mother’s desire to shelter her, and the painful recognition that love cannot prevent separation. Reality and imagination gradually draw closer, allowing mother and daughter to face what neither can fully name.

Jingya’s final months become a series of precious lessons and memories. She teaches her daughter not only practical things, but how to receive love, endure loss, and continue living without mistaking departure for abandonment. Years later, the daughter has grown up and become a mother herself. Carrying forward the tenderness, courage, and care she received, she understands anew what Jingya gave her.

At its heart, One Fine Day is about a mother’s love confronting time, illness, and inevitable loss. It finds beauty not in escaping sorrow, but in choosing to love fully, leave courage behind, and let that love continue across generations.

pinocchio.en:
In a tightly traditional Italian town, Geppetto is an unpopular, restless inventor whose grand schemes have brought him little except ridicule. Longing for a life beyond the rules and routines that govern his neighbours, he accepts an enchanted piece of wood from the Carpenter and carves it into a puppet he hopes will make his fortune. Instead, the puppet springs into life. Geppetto names him Pinocchio, and their prickly partnership quickly becomes something more like a family: Geppetto must learn to care for someone other than himself, while Pinocchio—impulsive, loud, and delighted by every new sensation—must discover how to make choices in a world he barely understands.

Pinocchio’s first rush of freedom takes him through a succession of strange encounters. The flamboyant Giacomo Cricket offers him a few basic lessons, but cannot keep him from charging after excitement. Pinocchio is drawn to Franzini, the sardonic owner of a travelling puppet show, who recognises the extraordinary possibility in a puppet that can move and speak for himself. Yet the road is also filled with people eager to exploit a naïve wooden boy. Fox and Cat trick Pinocchio out of what little he has, leaving him stranded and in danger, until the Blue Fairy intervenes.

Still, rescue does not make Pinocchio wise. He is tempted again by the Coachman, whose alluring Toyland promises endless pleasure without rules, responsibility, or consequence. Pinocchio must confront what that promise conceals and, amid the chaos of his adventures, finds himself swallowed by a whale. Inside its belly he is reunited with Geppetto. Their reunion brings the journey into focus: neither has found the life he expected, but each has found someone worth protecting. Pinocchio finally earns the chance to become flesh and blood, while Geppetto discovers that belonging is not achieved by escaping a community, but by learning how to love within one.

The musical centres on freedom, self-discovery, and the difficult work of becoming human. It treats family as something made through care, accountability, and mutual change rather than something simply given.

pinocchio musical.en:
In a cold late winter, the lonely woodcarver Geppetto discovers that an ordinary piece of wood can speak and move. He fashions it into a puppet, Pinocchio, hoping at last to have a son and perhaps to earn a living by presenting him in the streets. But the newly made boy is all impulse: he runs from Geppetto’s workshop almost at once, rejects the Talking Cricket’s warning that freedom without judgment brings trouble, and begins a restless search for amusement, shortcuts, and independence.

On his way to school, Pinocchio sells the spelling book Geppetto has sacrificed to buy for him and is drawn instead to Mangiafuoco’s travelling puppet theatre. His unexpected arrival disrupts the performance, yet the frightening master puppeteer is moved by Pinocchio’s concern for Geppetto and releases him with money for his father. The Fox and the Cat quickly smell opportunity. Pretending to be his friends, they tempt him with a scheme to bury his coins in the Field of Miracles, where they promise wealth will grow overnight. Their betrayal leaves Pinocchio robbed, endangered, and repeatedly rescued by the Blue Fairy, whose care offers him another chance to change.

Even then, Pinocchio struggles to keep his promises. Lies bring immediate consequences, while his longing for play leads him into the company of Lampwick and toward the pleasures of the Land of Toys. The boys’ carefree escape turns cruel when they are transformed into donkeys and exploited for profit. Pinocchio eventually escapes, only to discover that Geppetto has vanished while searching for him. Determined at last to act rather than merely wish, Pinocchio crosses the sea and is swallowed by a gigantic dogfish. Inside its belly, he finds Geppetto alive. Together they flee, and Pinocchio devotes himself to caring for his exhausted father. His hard-won generosity, perseverance, and love bring his journey to its final transformation.

The musical follows a child’s passage from reckless freedom to accountable choice. It presents love, sacrifice, and compassion as the forces that turn experience, failure, and courage into genuine maturity.

fan letter.en:
In 1930s Gyeongseong, aspiring writer Jung Sehun learns that a novel attributed to the late, enigmatic female author Hikaru is about to be published—and that its author’s concealed identity may be exposed. Alarmed, he seeks out Lee Yoon, a poet and novelist held in detention, and begs him to prevent the publication. Yoon refuses to intervene without an explanation, but he has something Sehun desperately wants: the final letter that Hikaru received from the celebrated novelist Kim Haejin. To obtain it, Sehun recounts the story behind Hikaru.

Years earlier, Sehun is a shy young admirer of Haejin, whose work has made him a central figure among the writers of the Seven. Longing to be acknowledged as a writer himself, Sehun writes a passionate fan letter under the female pen name “Hikaru.” Haejin is overwhelmed by the beauty and sensitivity of the letter. Believing Hikaru to be a woman, he falls in love with the unseen correspondent and begins an intense exchange of letters with her. Sehun initially intends to correct the misunderstanding, yet fear, admiration, and the thrill of being understood by his idol keep him silent.

As the correspondence deepens, Hikaru seems to acquire a life beyond Sehun’s control. Haejin and Hikaru begin to create a novel together, while the imagined woman becomes Haejin’s muse, confidante, and emotional refuge. Sehun is torn between joy at sharing in Haejin’s artistic life and guilt at deceiving a man who has entrusted him with his heart. Haejin’s fragile health worsens, making the deception increasingly unbearable. When the truth can no longer remain hidden, Sehun must confront what Hikaru has become—not merely a false name, but a presence shaped by longing, literature, and the needs of two isolated writers.

The musical explores how art can offer freedom and connection in an oppressive world, while also becoming a place to hide from reality. It is ultimately about admiration turning into obsession, the unstable boundary between creator and creation, and the painful desire to be loved for one’s truest self.

brothers karamazov.en:
In a provincial Russian town, Fyodor Karamazov, a wealthy landowner notorious for his sensual appetites and neglect of his family, is murdered in his home. Suspicion immediately falls on his eldest son, Dmitry, who has loudly vowed to kill him. Dmitry is desperate for money he believes his father has withheld from him, and their feud has been sharpened by their rivalry for Grushenka. When Fyodor is found dead and robbed, Dmitry’s public rage, poverty, and sudden possession of cash make him the obvious accused.

The investigation draws together the other sons whom Fyodor abandoned long ago. Ivan, the intellectual brother studying in Moscow, returns carrying an icy contempt for his father and a faith in reason that leaves him unable to escape questions of responsibility. Alyosha, a novice monk, tries to meet the family’s cruelty with compassion, but he too must watch the brothers turn distrust upon one another. In the Karamazov household is Smerdyakov, the servant long treated as an inferior yet believed to be Fyodor’s illegitimate son. Like the others, he has grown up under Fyodor’s humiliation and neglect.

As Dmitry awaits judgment, Ivan presses Smerdyakov for the truth. Smerdyakov confesses that he killed Fyodor, claiming he acted in accordance with Ivan’s unspoken wish that his father should die. He leaves Ivan with the unbearable knowledge that ideas, silence, and hatred can become forms of complicity, then takes his own life. At Dmitry’s trial, Ivan attempts to expose Smerdyakov as the murderer and admits his own moral guilt, but his revelation cannot rescue his brother. Dmitry is condemned, while the surviving brothers confront the damage left by their father and the choices each has made.

The musical examines how resentment can pass through a family until violence seems inevitable. Yet amid guilt, betrayal, and judgment, it asks whether love, forgiveness, and shared responsibility can still offer a path out of inherited cruelty.

oedipus.en:
In Thebes, King Laius and Queen Jocasta receive a dreadful prophecy: their newborn son will one day kill his father and marry his mother. Terrified, they order the infant to be abandoned on a mountainside. A shepherd cannot bring himself to complete the task and passes the child to a Corinthian herdsman, who delivers him to King Polybus and Queen Merope. The boy is raised as their son and named Oedipus, never knowing where he truly came from.

As a young man, Oedipus hears a rumour that he is not Polybus and Merope’s natural child. Seeking certainty, he consults an oracle, but instead receives a warning that he will murder his father and wed his mother. Believing Polybus and Merope to be his parents, Oedipus leaves Corinth so that he can never harm them. On the road, at a narrow crossroads, he quarrels with an arrogant older traveller and his attendants. In anger, Oedipus kills them, unaware that the traveller is Laius.

Arriving outside plague-stricken Thebes, Oedipus encounters the Sphinx, whose riddle has held the city hostage. He answers correctly, frees Thebes, and is rewarded with its throne and the hand of the widowed Jocasta. Years later, a new pestilence falls upon the city. Determined to save his people, Oedipus vows to find Laius’s murderer. His inquiry brings him into conflict with Creon and the blind prophet Tiresias, who insists that Oedipus himself is the guilty man. Oedipus rejects the accusation, convinced that others seek to overthrow him.

A messenger from Corinth announces Polybus’s death, then reveals that Oedipus was adopted. The surviving shepherd finally confirms the truth: Oedipus is the abandoned child of Laius and Jocasta. Jocasta takes her own life; Oedipus finds her, blinds himself in horror, and accepts exile from Thebes.

The musical centres on the collision between human choice and an inescapable destiny. It explores the destructive force of hidden truth, pride, guilt, and a ruler’s determination to pursue justice even when that pursuit turns against him.

paganini.en:
In 1844, four years after the death of the celebrated violin virtuoso Niccolò Paganini, his teenage son Achille appears before a religious court to secure his father’s burial in consecrated ground at Genoa. The Church has refused the request, convinced that Paganini’s astonishing gifts prove that he was a servant of the Devil. Opposing Achille is the priest and inquisitor Lucio Amos, who argues that the musician’s notoriety, unconventional life, and seemingly superhuman performances condemn him even after death. With his father’s body still denied a final resting place, Achille asks to tell the court what truly happened—and the action returns to Paris in 1836.

There, the grand opening of Casino Paganini is underway. Aristocrats, investors, and guests gather around Colin Bonner, the ambitious businessman behind the venture, and Charlotte de Vernier, Colin’s fiancée. Paganini arrives carrying official authorization that permits the building to operate only as a performance venue, not as a gambling house. While the decision protects him from being made the public face of a casino, it destroys Colin’s plan for immense profits. Paganini insists on honoring music rather than money and prepares to give the opening concert; Colin, humiliated and financially endangered, decides to turn the violinist’s fame into a weapon against him.

Colin seeks out Lucio, who is already determined to expose supposed devilry wherever he finds it. Together they cultivate the old suspicions surrounding Paganini: his uncanny technique, his mesmerising presence, and a public eager to explain genius through superstition. As scandal, manipulation, and religious accusation close in, Charlotte becomes a compassionate witness to the artist beneath the legend, while Achille’s later testimony reveals the human cost paid by a father whose sole refuge was his music. The past and the courtroom confrontation converge as Achille fights not merely for a burial, but for the right to define who Niccolò Paganini was.

The musical explores the conflict between artistic freedom and institutions that fear what they cannot control. It also asks how greed, envy, superstition, and public judgment can transform extraordinary talent into a curse—and how filial love can resist that verdict.

shadow.en:
In 1762, Crown Prince Sado is imprisoned by his father, King Yeongjo, in a rice chest after an accusation that Sado tried to kill him. On the first night of confinement, Sado—whose personal name is Yi Hwon—writes his name on a page from the mystical Scripture of the Jade Pivot. The chest becomes a breach in time, carrying him from the stillness of approaching death into the past. There he encounters a frightened young prince named Yi Geum, unaware at first that this lonely, anxious boy will become King Yeongjo—the father who has condemned him.

Sado returns repeatedly through the opening created by the pages of the scripture. Each crossing reveals Yi Geum at another stage of life: a vulnerable child who craves his elder brother’s protection, a prince learning to survive the perilous demands of court, and finally a ruler haunted by suspicion, loss, and the terrible burden of authority. Sado becomes a confidant to the younger Yi Geum, offering the tenderness and reassurance that neither man can give freely in their own present. In doing so, Sado begins to see behind the stern monarch he has feared and resented all his life.

Meanwhile, the physical world closes in. Sado remains trapped in the rice chest, growing weaker while reliving the night he raised a sword against his father. The time journeys gradually reveal that their conflict is not simply a clash between a cruel king and a victimized son: both have been shaped by isolation, fear, pride, and the violence demanded by power. When Sado finally meets Yi Geum as the king he knows, the two confront the accusation, the witnessed attack, and the political reality that makes their survival together seem impossible. Yeongjo offers Sado the chance to strike him down, but Sado cannot do it. Instead, he relinquishes vengeance and asks his father for forgiveness as the rice chest carries him toward his unavoidable death.

The musical explores how love can be buried beneath duty, trauma, and suspicion—yet still survive in the need to be understood. Its time-crossing encounters turn a tragic father-and-son conflict into a search for empathy, forgiveness, and the courage to choose compassion over revenge.

摇滚浮士德.en:
In the shattered aftermath of Black Monday, John Faust, once a rising Wall Street broker, watches his wealth, status, and imagined future vanish in a single catastrophic collapse. The loss leaves him furious, humiliated, and spiritually adrift. At his side is Gretchen, the woman who loves him and believes that endurance, compassion, and faith can still give their lives meaning. John cannot accept her consolation. Convinced that the world has abandoned him, he becomes vulnerable to a force that promises not comfort, but control.

Two mysterious presences, X-White and X-Black, observe John as the object of a wager. X-White trusts that even a damaged person can choose conscience and human connection; X-Black insists that desire, pride, and the hunger for pleasure will ultimately prevail. X-Black approaches John with an offer: a route back to success, power, and the exhilaration of winning. Despite Gretchen’s warning, John accepts. His return begins spectacularly. He becomes a formidable figure in the ruthless world of deals and acquisitions, surrounded by money, parties, luxury, and the intoxicating illusion that he has mastered fate.

Yet each advance estranges him from the person he was. John’s ambition hardens into exploitation, and the bargain that seems to restore his life slowly consumes it from within. Gretchen watches the man she loves become increasingly unreachable. Her efforts to pull him back are acts of devotion, but they also expose her to fear, confusion, and visions in which reality and nightmare blur together. While X-White struggles to preserve a possibility of redemption, X-Black feeds John’s sense of invincibility and urges him deeper into corruption.

As John’s prosperity rises, the emotional cost becomes impossible to ignore. He must confront whether success obtained through betrayal and moral surrender can ever compensate for the loss of Gretchen, his conscience, and his own capacity to love. The contest around him becomes inseparable from his own final choices.

The musical explores the conflict between conscience and appetite, love and possession, and spiritual integrity and worldly triumph. It asks whether a person destroyed by failure can reclaim humanity after choosing power at any cost.

狂炎奏鸣曲.en:
In a gloomy late-1970s apartment, J is a gifted composer who has become trapped by the shadow of his own earlier success. His teacher, K, demands another masterpiece and treats artistic greatness as an obligation rather than a possibility, but J can no longer summon the emotion that once animated his music. His closest friend, S, remains a compassionate presence: confidant, collaborator, and the person whose affection and musical sensitivity once helped J find his voice. Yet J experiences this intimacy not only as comfort, but as a painful reminder of his creative dependence.

An accidental drunken hit-and-run ruptures J’s paralysis. Confronted with death and the extremity of his own actions, he suddenly feels music return. Instead of recoiling from that revelation, he begins to believe that transgression is the price of creation. Each violent act seems to unleash another passage of music, and J records the process obsessively as he works toward a new sonata. K recognizes the growing power in J’s compositions and, rather than firmly stopping him, becomes a disturbing catalyst—at once mentor, judge, and tempter—pressuring J to finish what he has begun.

S acts as both J’s friend and the emotional witness to his decline, bringing J’s private writings and fractured inner life into view. Memories of their earliest music-making reveal that S had helped initiate the melody that became J’s first great work. This discovery devastates J: he interprets it as proof that his talent may never have belonged to him alone. In his warped pursuit of absolute originality, he comes to see S—the person he loves, envies, and needs—as the final barrier between himself and artistic completion. J’s attempt on S’s life becomes the horrifying culmination of his belief that beauty can be extracted from destruction, forcing the audience to confront how completely he has confused inspiration with violence.

The musical examines the seduction of artistic obsession and the terror of treating human suffering as material for art. It also asks where responsibility lies when genius, ambition, mentorship, and moral surrender become entangled.

納爾齊斯與歌爾德蒙.en:
Narcissus and Goldmund opens in a castle dungeon, where Goldmund awaits execution after a forbidden affair with a countess. Expecting a priest for his last confession, he prepares to attack the visitor and escape—only to discover Narcissus, his estranged friend and now a powerful abbot, who has risked his own standing to save him. Their reunion releases a flood of memories. Goldmund recalls arriving as a boy at Mariabronn Abbey, where the brilliant young monk Narcissus recognises both his intelligence and the restless, vulnerable nature that sets him apart from monastic life. Goldmund admires Narcissus and hopes to emulate his discipline, while Narcissus sees that his friend’s path lies beyond the cloister.

An encounter outside the abbey awakens Goldmund to desire and to the sensory world. He tells Narcissus that he must leave; despite the pain of parting, Narcissus accepts this truth and sends him out to seek the life that calls him. Goldmund wanders through love affairs, danger, loss, and fleeting happiness, eventually discovering an aptitude for sculpture. As an apprentice, he creates a figure of John the Apostle—the name Narcissus adopted at ordination—turning his unspoken attachment to his friend into art.

Years later, plague and personal grief shatter Goldmund’s faith in any orderly divine purpose, especially after the death of a woman carrying his child. He returns to the cloister seeking a place to work, and his sculptures fill its grounds. Yet his most important work remains incomplete: Maria, a veiled figure whose face seems connected to the mother he can scarcely remember. Goldmund again leaves, convinced that art requires the risks and experiences of the outside world. When he finally returns to Narcissus, he is near death but has recovered the memory of his mother and the peace he had pursued. Narcissus remains beside him until the end.

The musical explores the pull between intellect and instinct, religious discipline and sensual experience, and the different ways people search for wholeness. At its heart is an enduring friendship in which each man helps the other understand love, mortality, and the life he could not have lived alone.

days.en:
In 2022, Cha Jung-hak, now a senior officer in the Blue House security service, faces a crisis when Hana, the President’s daughter, disappears together with her assigned bodyguard, Daesik. The case evokes a disappearance that has haunted Jung-hak for three decades: in 1992, as South Korea prepared to establish diplomatic relations with China, the young security officer had begun work alongside Kang Mu-young, a gifted but irreverent new colleague whose impulsive warmth sharply contrasted with Jung-hak’s discipline. Their first major assignment was to guard a woman identified only as She, an enigmatic interpreter whose identity and political importance are deliberately concealed from them.

Jung-hak and Mu-young grow from rivals into partners as they try to protect her from threats they cannot fully understand. Mu-young, increasingly drawn to She’s loneliness and determination, sees the person behind the classified assignment, while Jung-hak tries to uphold the procedures that define his life. Then, without warning, She vanishes—and Mu-young disappears with her. Their absence leaves Jung-hak with unanswered questions, professional disgrace, and the painful suspicion that his friend chose a private promise over duty.

Thirty years later, the search for Hana and Daesik retraces the old mystery. As Jung-hak follows clues across Seoul, fragments of the past return: the guarded young interpreter, the friendship between two men who understood loyalty differently, and the decision that separated them. The new disappearance gradually reveals its connection to the earlier one, forcing Jung-hak to confront what Mu-young had sacrificed and why he could never simply abandon She. The two timelines converge as Jung-hak recognizes that the missing people are not merely security failures to be recovered, but individuals acting under the pressure of love, memory, political change, and promises that official records cannot contain.

At its heart, The Days explores friendship tested by opposing ideas of duty, as well as the cost of choosing compassion over institutional obedience. It treats memory as both a burden and a path toward understanding the sacrifices hidden behind history’s public events.

stravinsky.en:
In war-torn Switzerland in 1917, Igor Stravinsky lives in a shabby room with little but a piano, a chessboard, and the company of Shum, his sharp-tongued oldest companion. Cut off from income and unable even to secure a proper funeral for the nanny who raised him, Igor retreats into chess as if calculation can hold catastrophe at bay. Shum challenges that illusion. After fourteen months without selling a composition, he tells Igor to stop writing music: the problem, he insists, is not merely war or poverty, but that Igor’s music has ceased to matter. Igor refuses to accept it and wagers that a new work will prove Shum wrong.

As Igor searches for something saleable yet artistically uncompromising, their argument unlocks memories of the dazzling Ballets Russes years. He relives the triumphs and tensions surrounding The Firebird, Petrushka, and The Rite of Spring: the creative frictions with Sergei Diaghilev and Vaslav Nijinsky, the pressure to revise music for a production, and the lingering wound of a notorious failure. In the present, he tries to devise piano music ordinary people might play, revising one idea after another—pieces are too difficult, too slight, or rejected outright. A visit to potential patrons ends in humiliation when Igor is invited to perform Glazunov rather than his own music.

The blows accumulate. A telegram reveals that the Bolsheviks have confiscated his family property and labelled him a traitor; a hospital call forces him to choose cremation for his dying nanny because burial is beyond his means. Shum presses the final solution: sell the piano, abandon composition, and spare Igor’s wife and children further sacrifice. At his lowest point, Igor joins Shum in discarding Russian books and scores, ready to burn the past. But dawn changes the game. He recognizes that Shum’s accusations, doubts, and “noise” are inseparable from the force that drives him to create. Rather than silence them, he chooses to write again and asks Shum to remain beside him.

The musical explores artistic endurance under exile, poverty, grief, and public rejection. It frames creativity as both a burden and a form of survival: the very inner voice that torments Igor also keeps him moving toward an uncertain future.

红莲.en:
Hongryeon is brought in chains to Cheondojeong, the court of the dead, for what Princess Bari declares will be its 139,998th—and final—trial. Assisted by the underworld messengers Gangrim, Woljik, and Iljik, Bari hears the accusations against the girl: Hongryeon is said to have murdered her father, Bae Mu-ryong, and mutilated her half-brother, Jangsoe. Hongryeon admits that she harmed them, yet insists she merely delivered the punishment that heaven had failed to impose. She rejects the rumours told in the world of the living about the deaths of herself and her twin sister, Janghwa, and bitterly observes that no one cared to hear an abused girl’s voice while she was alive.

Bari summons the spirit of Bae Mu-ryong, who condemns Hongryeon as an evil ghost rather than a daughter. His indifference becomes plain when he asks not for Hongryeon’s return, but for Jangsoe’s body to be restored. Hongryeon lashes out at Bari as well, invoking Bari’s own history as an abandoned child. Rather than end the hearing, Bari persists, determined to uncover why Hongryeon cannot cross the Samdocheon, the river separating death from whatever lies beyond.

The interrogation draws out fragments of Hongryeon’s past. Janghwa repeatedly shielded her younger sister from the violence of their stepmother, Lady Heo, and consequently became the chief target herself. Before Janghwa’s marriage, Jangsoe steals the sisters’ treasured keepsake from their late mother; during the ensuing struggle, Janghwa is gravely injured and left unattended until she dies. Hongryeon’s grief curdles into guilt: she believes she failed her sister, then insists she later avenged her.

But Bari exposes the impossibility of the confession. Hongryeon could not plausibly have carried out the violent acts she describes, and her memories begin to collapse under the weight of their contradictions. As her soul threatens to fracture, Janghwa’s final letter reaches her: each sister had loved the other desperately. Hongryeon tries to destroy herself in the fires beyond the Samdocheon, but Bari begins a cleansing ritual and restores the truth. Hongryeon took her own life soon after Janghwa’s death; she never killed Bae Mu-ryong or harmed Jangsoe. The countless “trials” were not punishments at all, but a compassionate attempt to rebuild her shattered memory. Freed from self-condemnation, Hongryeon removes her red restraints and walks peacefully toward the white-lit gate beyond the river.

The musical is ultimately about the damage inflicted by family violence, silence, and unequal power, as well as the way survivors can turn grief inward as blame. Through Bari’s intervention, it frames healing not as forgetting injustice, but as recovering truth, receiving compassion, and learning to forgive oneself.

mad hatter.en:
In London in 1851, with the Great Exhibition approaching, fourteen-year-old Noah is determined to find steady work and earn enough to survive. After losing a harsh chimney-cleaning job, he is hired at Hector’s hat factory, where workers endure relentless hours producing fashionable hats for a growing city. There Noah meets Jocelyn, Hector’s sheltered son. The boys initially see hats in opposite ways: Noah regards them as necessities—objects that can secure wages, food, and shelter—while Jocelyn imagines a distinct hat for every individual, shaped by that person’s memories, feelings, and desires.

Their brief breaks become the beginning of a friendship. But Noah notices something deeply wrong in the felt workshop: workers cough, tremble, lose focus, and behave erratically. With Jocelyn’s help, he traces the cause to mercury vapour used in the manufacturing process. When Noah confronts Hector, Hector dismisses the danger as an acceptable cost of keeping the factory productive. To him, a theoretical illness matters less than the immediate threat of unemployment and hunger. Refusing to stop using mercury, Hector fires Noah.

Cast back onto the streets, Noah is shaken by the ease with which workers can be discarded. Yet he refuses to accept that the only choices are obedience or destitution. He gathers unhoused people who want work and, with Jocelyn at his side, opens a small hat shop. Instead of standardised hats made for status and profit, they create unusual, personal hats that hold customers’ private stories: lost loves, family memories, hopes, frustrations, and small acts of self-definition. Their shop gives people a way to be seen in a city that has treated them as interchangeable.

As their hats attract attention around the Exhibition, Hector attempts to turn Noah’s difference into a spectacle. Noah nevertheless continues to make hats that speak openly about exploitation, poisoned workplaces, stolen time, and the value of lives deemed inconvenient. Jocelyn ultimately walks beside him, choosing their shared vision over his father’s authority.

The musical explores friendship as a force that turns isolation into solidarity. It asks who gets to define what is useful, normal, or valuable, and celebrates imagination as a means of insisting that every person has the right to occupy space, be recognised, and live without harm.

laundry.en:
In a shabby hillside neighborhood of Seoul, Na-young, a 27-year-old woman who left her provincial hometown with hopes of studying and building a better life, rents a tiny room and works at Jeil Bookstore. Her dreams have narrowed into the routines of low-paid city survival. Next door lives Solongo, a young man from Mongolia who came to Korea to earn money for his family. Once a literature student, he now works in a factory under precarious circumstances, vulnerable to abuse, withheld wages, and deportation because of his immigration status. Their houses share a rooftop where residents hang their washing, and Solongo, immediately drawn to Na-young, repeatedly tries to speak with her. She initially keeps her distance, but an item of laundry blown across the roof begins a hesitant connection.

Around them, the tenants carry private burdens. Hee-jung’s Mother, lively and outspoken despite her own disappointments, fills the neighborhood with noise and warmth. The elderly Landlady, whose harsh manner disguises fierce devotion, cares for her severely disabled daughter. At work, Na-young sees a colleague dismissed after questioning wrongdoing; when she protests, the bookstore’s domineering owner, Bread, retaliates by transferring her to an isolated warehouse. Exhausted and humiliated, she drinks with colleagues and returns home in despair.

Solongo finds her on the street and offers gentle help. Their fragile closeness is interrupted when the landlord confronts them. Afraid that police attention could expose him, Solongo endures the man’s violence rather than defend himself, a sacrifice that makes Na-young recognize both his vulnerability and his kindness. Later, when the Landlady’s daughter needs urgent help, Hee-jung’s Mother and Na-young join in supporting the household. Their shared tears and everyday acts of care turn the rooftop laundry into a place of release and companionship. As the neighbors’ circumstances shift, Na-young and Solongo choose to live together, and Solongo finally gives voice to the word he has struggled to claim: love.

The musical is about people pushed to the margins by poverty, precarious work, migration, sexism, disability, and loneliness, yet refusing to become invisible to one another. Its laundry lines bind private sorrow to communal care: pain may not disappear, but it can be aired, shared, and met with tenderness.

inside me.en:
Bokja is the woman behind Inbyeol, a dazzling social-media persona whose polished posts, devoted followers, and “Influencer of the Year” award make her appear to have achieved everything. Online, Inbyeol is stylish, desirable, confident, and endlessly successful; away from the screen, Bokja is increasingly exhausted by the effort of maintaining that image. Raised by her grandmother in rural Haenam, she has learned to treat visibility and approval as measures of worth, so each post, reaction, and burst of public attention becomes another reason to conceal the parts of herself that do not fit the idealized Inbyeol brand.

Her boyfriend, the kind-hearted emerging composer Jinhyeok, watches this transformation with growing concern. He loves Bokja, not the persona she performs for strangers, but he finds himself pushed to the margins as her dependence on social media intensifies. Their relationship is tested when Jinhyeok receives the opportunity to compose a new song for the superstar Shanti—a professional breakthrough that should bring the couple joy. Instead, it exposes how far Bokja has drifted from the person he once knew. As Inbyeol’s public ambitions and private anxieties collide, she struggles to distinguish her own desires from the demands of the audience she has built around herself.

The pressure to remain admired deepens Bokja’s loneliness. Encounters with the people and roles surrounding her—fans, celebrities, friends, family figures, and the ever-changing voices of the online world—keep reflecting back versions of the self she is expected to be. Clinging to the validation of her digital life, she loses sight of what is real and ultimately breaks with Jinhyeok. In the aftermath of that separation, the glittering image of Inbyeol can no longer protect her from emptiness. Forced to confront Bokja, the self she has neglected, she begins to look inward and reclaim the honesty, connection, and self-acceptance that fame could not supply.

The musical asks whether a life shaped for other people’s approval can still feel like one’s own. Its central themes are identity, the cost of performative online perfection, and the discovery that inner truth matters more than outward image.

portrait of a boy.en:
Set between present-day Italy and Venice in 1530, Portrait of a Boy follows the restoration of Portrait of the Baron, a long-lost work attributed to the respected painter Marcello. In the present, art restorer Viola is asked to examine the painting and finds anomalies beneath its surface: an unfamiliar signature and crude layers of paint that seem intended to conceal an earlier image. As Viola follows these physical clues, the musical moves back to Marcello’s Venetian workshop, where the hidden history of the portrait begins to emerge.

There, Rosina is a gifted young painter whose work must nevertheless remain under Marcello’s name. Her ability is unmistakable, but as a woman she is denied public authorship and professional independence. Marta, Rosina’s close friend and assistant, supports her as she tries to preserve both her artistic conviction and her dignity in a world that treats her talent as something to be used but not acknowledged. When the workshop receives a commission to paint a portrait of a boy from an aristocratic family, Rosina becomes the true artist behind the commission. Yet the sitter is not the noble boy expected by the patrons. Jacopo, an open-hearted, free-spirited boy, is brought in to stand before the canvas as a substitute.

Rosina sees Jacopo not as a formal emblem of rank, but as a living person. Rather than merely reproducing a face, she paints him in a moment of animation and pleasure, capturing the warmth of his character. But the portrait is built on concealment: Jacopo performs another boy’s identity, while Rosina paints behind Marcello’s name. Their individual truths are covered over by the social arrangements that make the painting possible. In the present, Viola’s painstaking restoration gradually reverses that erasure, revealing Rosina’s hand and recovering the story hidden beneath the official attribution.

The musical explores how identity can be obscured by class, gender, authority, and necessity—and how art can preserve what history tries to suppress. It is ultimately about recognition: the long-delayed return of a name, a voice, and a life to the work that has carried their trace across centuries.

gone tomorrow.en:
In 1884, Joseon stands at a breaking point. Kim Okkyun, a young reformer determined to lead his country into a new age, joins King Gojong in an uprising meant to modernize the nation. Their hopes collapse almost immediately: Qing intervention and Japan’s abandonment destroy the coup within three days, leaving Kim branded a traitor and forced into exile in Japan. The King remains on the throne, but his authority is hollowed out, while Prime Minister Yi Wan tightens his grip over the court and turns the failed rebellion into a dangerous secret.

Years later, Gojong summons Han Jeong-hoon, a man who has survived by remaking himself. Having lived in France under the name Hong Jong-u, Han returns to Joseon using that identity and is offered a chance to reclaim a place in his homeland. The price is a private royal command: travel to Japan and murder Kim Okkyun. Gojong cannot risk Kim living long enough to expose the King’s own involvement in the uprising, and Han—caught between necessity, ambition, and fear—accepts the assignment.

In Japan, Han finds not the monstrous traitor he expects but a solitary, wounded Kim, still sustained by his vision for Joseon. Kim welcomes Han into his orbit, and the two spend a week playing Go. Their games become a wary conversation in which each move tests loyalty, motive, and conviction. Kim’s steadfastness gradually unsettles Han, while Kim recognizes the purpose behind his visitor’s arrival. Elsewhere, Gojong’s unease intensifies under Yi Wan’s pressure, and he renews his order for Kim’s death.

At their final meeting, Kim reveals that he has understood Han’s mission all along. He turns his back, gives Han permission to act, and Han fires the gun. Kim’s death completes the King’s attempt to bury the past, but it also leaves Han carrying the moral weight of the ideals he has helped silence.

The musical examines how political failure can fracture friendship, identity, and trust. It asks whether a defeated vision can endure through those who remember it, even after its most visible champion has fallen.

western story.en:
In 1886, Jane Johnson runs the Diamond Saloon in Green Valley City, Arizona, an isolated outpost surrounded by desert. Desperate to escape the West and begin again in New York, Jane concocts a scheme with her loyal twin friends, Bud and Harry: she will sell the saloon at an inflated price by spreading the rumour that a railroad is about to pass nearby. To make the con work, however, she needs notorious figures—and the money, attention, and danger that follow them—to converge under her roof.

Her bait draws three celebrated names of the frontier. Wyatt Earp, a former sheriff and legendary gunman looking for his next opportunity, arrives and unexpectedly reunites with Josephine Marcus, his former lover and a formidable figure in her own right. Johnny Ringo, feared as a merciless outlaw, also enters the saloon, turning Jane’s carefully planned swindle into a volatile contest of bluffing, shifting alliances, and mutual suspicion. Each newcomer sees a chance to gain wealth or advantage, while Jane struggles to keep her false story alive and maintain control of the increasingly crowded room.

The situation changes decisively with the arrival of Billy Hooker, a hot-tempered gunman who has crossed the West seeking revenge for his father’s death. Billy’s determination to settle an old score threatens not only Wyatt, Josephine, and Johnny but also Jane’s plan to sell the Diamond Saloon and leave town. As old grudges, invented identities, private regrets, and competing ambitions surface, the saloon becomes a pressure cooker. Jane, Bud, and Harry must improvise their way through escalating deceptions, while the famous gunslingers are forced to confront whether their public legends match the people they really are.

At its heart, Western Story is about people trying to rewrite the lives that the frontier—and their own reputations—has assigned them. It treats revenge, romance, greed, freedom, and reinvention as equally combustible forces, finding comedy in the gap between heroic myths and flawed human beings.

sunny ten.en:
In Seoul, Jun-ho is a chronically unlucky television producer whose career has stalled after a marriage-proposal broadcast unexpectedly collapses when the featured couple disappear. His chance to escape professional obscurity arrives with a condition from the station director: if Jun-ho can date—and win the affection of—the director’s daughter Hye-young for ten days, he will be given the programme he has long wanted to make.

Hye-young, an independent, hardworking animation artist, has just been hurt by a boyfriend she had intended to marry. Disillusioned with love, she is nevertheless thrilled when the opportunity arises to pursue a long-desired course of study in England. Her father, however, has a condition of his own: she must go on a blind date, and she will be allowed to leave only if the man rejects her within ten days. The chosen date is Jun-ho. Thus, without either initially grasping the full symmetry of their predicament, the pair enter the same arranged encounter with entirely opposed objectives. Jun-ho needs Hye-young to like him; Hye-young needs him to leave her.

Their ten-day courtship becomes a series of comic maneuvers, misunderstandings, staged impressions, and increasingly difficult emotional calculations. Jun-ho tries to overcome his bad luck and present himself as the man Hye-young might choose, while Hye-young sets out to make herself impossible to love. Around them, friends, family members, Hye-young’s former boyfriend, and Jun-ho’s colleagues complicate every plan, sometimes helping and sometimes derailing the fragile bargain on which both futures seem to depend. As the deadline draws nearer, the performances they give each other begin to reveal real vulnerabilities: Hye-young must confront the hurt that made her afraid to trust again, while Jun-ho discovers that winning a job is not the same thing as winning someone’s heart. What began as a contest of incompatible schemes gradually becomes a genuine romance, forcing them to choose between the futures they planned and the connection neither expected.

The show explores how love can emerge when people stop treating one another as solutions to personal problems. It balances fate, ambition, emotional recovery, and the courage to risk disappointment for an honest relationship.

screwtape letters.en:
In the infernal offices of the Devil Special Agency, Screwtape—an accomplished, irritable senior devil—wages an unending covert war against the Enemy, Jesus. Frustrated that his operations do not always proceed as planned, he takes charge of a special training assignment: shaping his nephew Wormwood, a novice tempter, into a more effective corrupter of human souls. With the seasoned demon Lilith as part of the operation, Screwtape instructs Wormwood in the art of turning the Enemy’s human “patients” away from faith, responsibility, and genuine love.

Their campaign does not depend on spectacular crimes so much as on the steady distortion of ordinary life. Screwtape teaches his protégés to exhaust people until they become irritable, to make them speak piously while neglecting the duties immediately before them, and to turn faith into a tool for worldly ambition rather than a source of transformation. They encourage people to stop asking whether something is true or false, to surrender their judgment to fashion, convention, and public opinion, and to chase glittering visions of the future until anxiety and dissatisfaction consume the present. Even prayer becomes a target: the devils seek to foster hollow spirituality and self-regard while steering people away from humble, obedient prayer.

Screwtape’s instructions expose a wider battlefield in homes, relationships, desire, conflict, laughter, love, pleasure, and fear. He and his fellow devils alternate between intimidation, flattery, deception, and manipulation, convinced that weakness can be made habitual if it is treated as normal. Yet every scheme meets resistance from the Enemy. The patients are not simply passive victims, and the forces the devils despise repeatedly interfere with their carefully prepared temptations. As failures accumulate, Screwtape’s confidence gives way to mounting exasperation, placing Wormwood and Lilith under increasing pressure while the Agency’s campaign slips toward crisis.

The musical portrays temptation as an assault on attention, truthfulness, responsibility, and authentic spiritual life. Its central struggle contrasts cynical manipulation and self-absorption with grace, humility, discernment, and the possibility of moral renewal.

pilgrims progress.en:
A warning that the City of Destruction faces ruin shatters Pilgrim’s ordinary life. He begs his family and neighbours to heed it, but they dismiss him as mad and turn away. Alone, carrying the crushing weight of his sin, Pilgrim leaves the city in search of the Celestial City, the living city beyond the narrow road. His first steps bring no easy release: he sinks into the Slough of Despond, where hopelessness threatens to swallow both his courage and his purpose. Yet he rises and continues, determined to find the promised way.

The road repeatedly tests whether Pilgrim’s desire for salvation can outlast fear, pain, and deception. He is drawn toward easier answers and confronted by the powers that rule the City of Destruction. Most terrifyingly, Apollyon pursues him and challenges him in a fierce struggle, seeking to reclaim the traveller who has escaped his dominion. Pilgrim refuses to turn back. Scarred but unbroken, he presses onward through darkness and danger, sustained by the conviction that the Celestial City is real.

At Vanity Fair, a glittering city of distraction, pleasure, and compromise, Pilgrim encounters his close companion Faithful. Their refusal to embrace the city’s values makes them targets. Faithful is taken from Pilgrim, leaving the traveller to confront grief as well as peril. The loss deepens Pilgrim’s loneliness, but it does not end his journey. He continues along the hard road toward the heavenly destination, discovering that each trial asks him to choose once more between retreat and trust. Through suffering, temptation, combat, and bereavement, Pilgrim becomes less a frightened fugitive from destruction and more a traveller able to endure for the sake of the city he seeks.

The musical portrays a journey from guilt and fear toward faith, perseverance, and hope. It explores the cost of refusing easy compromises, the sustaining force of companionship, and the belief that hardship can be endured when one keeps sight of a greater destination.

rabbits eight sufferings.en:
Toja’s story begins in the shadow of a narrow escape. His father, Tobu, returns to the land from the Underwater Palace after deceiving the Dragon King into believing that rabbits keep their livers ashore. He scarcely has time to rejoice with his wife, Tomo, and their son before disaster strikes: Tobu is seized by an eagle, and Tomo is killed by a hunter. Left utterly alone, Toja grows weary of a world that offers grief at every turn. He dreams instead of the Underwater Palace, imagining it as a distant, peaceful realm where suffering cannot reach him.

Elsewhere, Turtle has failed in the task of bringing the Dragon King a rabbit’s liver to cure his illness. Desperate to find another rabbit, Turtle performs a ritual to the Mountain Spirit and happens upon Toja and a young female rabbit, Tonyeo. Drawn by the promise of a better life beyond the hardships of the land, they follow Turtle beneath the water. Yet the palace proves nothing like Toja’s fantasy. The Dragon King remains ill, and the creatures of the Underwater Palace capture Toja and Tonyeo as the possible remedy. What Toja hoped would be sanctuary becomes another prison, ruled by fear, appetite, and the demands placed on the weak.

With help from Jjukkumi, the palace’s physician-general, Toja and Tonyeo attempt to devise a way back to land. Toja must confront danger, loss, manipulation, and the repeated temptation to believe that safety lies somewhere else. Through his trials, he gradually discovers that escape alone cannot solve the pain of being alive; every place contains its own perils, and home must be found rather than merely fled toward. Ultimately, Toja’s journey transforms his longing for an unreachable paradise into a clearer understanding of where—and how—he can live.

The musical explores hardship, displacement, and the human desire to abandon an imperfect present for an imagined elsewhere. Its central insight is that freedom and belonging emerge not from a flawless destination, but from facing one’s life and finding meaning in the place one truly inhabits.

madangnori chunpungs wife.en:
In Hanyang, Lee Chunpung lives extravagantly on the fortune left by his parents, neglecting his household and his devoted wife, Madam Kim. His days are spent in drinking houses, gambling dens, and the company of courtesans, until his wealth is gone and creditors close in. Ashamed but not truly changed, Chunpung hands the management of the household to Madam Kim and signs a pledge promising to behave himself. With discipline and commercial skill, she restores the family’s finances; yet Chunpung’s appetite for pleasure soon returns.

An opportunity then takes Chunpung to Pyongyang with a large sum of money, including public funds entrusted for an official purchase and money Madam Kim has painstakingly saved. Rather than complete his task, he falls under the spell of Yu Chuwol, a celebrated courtesan. He lavishes money and gifts on her until every last coin has vanished. Once he is penniless, Chuwol strips away her affection and reduces the once-proud gentleman to humiliating service in her household.

Back in Hanyang, Madam Kim learns of his disgrace. Instead of simply lamenting his betrayal, she takes decisive action. Disguised in male official dress, she travels to Pyongyang as part of the provincial governor’s retinue. There she confronts the social world in which Chunpung has been trapped and, without immediately revealing herself, puts him through a painful reckoning. Chunpung bows, pleads, and endures public humiliation before the stern official who holds power over him—only to discover that this formidable figure is his own wife.

Returned home, Chunpung can no longer hide behind swagger or excuses. His wife’s competence, courage, and mercy force him to recognize the ruin caused by his irresponsibility. He abandons his dissipated life, turns toward the care of his home, and the couple rebuilds a peaceful and prosperous household together.

The show’s themes are accountability, marital trust, and the reversal of conventional power between husband and wife. Its comic humiliations ultimately celebrate a resourceful woman’s ability to save both her family’s livelihood and her husband from his own folly.

kikis borderline personality disorder di.en:
Kiki’s Borderline Personality Disorder Diary unfolds as a candid talk-concert in which Kiki, appearing before an audience as the evening’s guest, tells the story of learning to live with borderline personality disorder. Looking back, Kiki describes a life shaped by overwhelming feelings, fear of abandonment, and relationships that become impossible to hold steady. After repeated breakups with a long-term partner, Kiki reaches a crisis and is admitted to a psychiatric hospital. There Kiki meets Ethan, a counselor who introduces dialectical behavior therapy and begins helping Kiki name emotions, endure distress without acting destructively, and recognize patterns that have governed life for years.

The narrative does not present treatment as a clean ascent from illness to cure. As Kiki works through therapy, attempts a new job, and enters a new romance, familiar impulses and old pain return. Learning the techniques is one thing; facing hurt rather than fleeing, lashing out, or clinging to another person remains painfully difficult. Kiki’s public account moves between recollection, confession, and the immediate effort to make sense of feelings that can change without warning.

After completing the formal course of therapy, Kiki comes to understand how much recognition, patience, and support from loved ones can matter. This realization leads Kiki to seek out Kiki’s mother. The encounter is fraught: Kiki’s mother cannot accept that Kiki has the disorder, and the hoped-for validation does not arrive easily. Instead, mother and child begin counseling together through tears, opening a difficult conversation rather than resolving their history at once.

Five years after beginning treatment, Kiki again stands before the audience. Kiki does not claim to be fully recovered, but can say that self-hatred no longer has the final word—and that learning self-acceptance remains an ongoing practice.

The musical is about living with, rather than triumphantly erasing, pain. It explores self-understanding, the fragile work of sustaining relationships, and the possibility that compassion—from others and from oneself—can make continued life feel possible.

2026 midnight actor musician the choice.en:
On New Year’s Eve, 1937, a nervous married couple wait inside their home in Azerbaijan, a Soviet republic gripped by the Great Terror. As midnight approaches, they try to sustain an appearance of ordinary domestic warmth, speaking cautiously about the future while dread presses in from outside: people are being taken away in the night, neighbours may be informers, and a careless word can destroy a life. Their affection is genuine, yet fear has made even the closest relationship uncertain. Each wonders what the other may know, believe, or be willing to do to survive.

Then comes the sound they have been anticipating—the knock at the door. The visitor who enters is not easily understood or dismissed. His arrival freezes the couple’s attempts at normality and turns their private room into a place of interrogation, accusation, and reckoning. With time seemingly suspended on the threshold of the new year, the stranger draws out memories, suspicions, compromises, and concealed cruelties. The husband and wife are forced to revisit the choices that brought them to this night: whom they trusted, whom they failed, what they accepted, and what they may have sacrificed in the hope of keeping themselves safe.

As the encounter intensifies, the question of who has power over whom becomes increasingly unstable. The visitor may represent the terrifying machinery of the state, but he also exposes the terror already lodged within the household. The couple’s loyalty is tested against self-preservation, and their love is strained by the possibility that either of them could betray—or already have betrayed—the other. Approaching midnight no longer offers the promise of renewal; it becomes a deadline by which the truth must surface. In the final confrontation, the characters must face what fear has made them capable of, while the distinction between victim, witness, accomplice, and judge begins to collapse.

The musical explores how authoritarian fear invades private life, turning intimacy into suspicion and survival into a moral bargain. It asks whether evil is imposed from above, created by ordinary human weakness, or both.

2026 wtof million loves.en:
Million Loves follows ordinary Koreans whose private hopes, romances, disappointments, and loyalties unfold against the sweeping changes of modern Korean history. Rather than centering on a single heroic figure, the musical moves through the lives of people who must keep rebuilding their relationships as the country around them changes—through departures and reunions, economic uncertainty and new opportunity, generational conflict, and the persistent wish for a more secure future. Familiar popular songs give emotional voice to moments that the characters cannot easily explain: the excitement of young love, the ache of separation, the compromises made for family, and the memories that return when a song from the past is heard again.

As years pass, youthful dreams encounter the practical demands of work, marriage, parenthood, and survival. Lovers discover that affection alone does not erase distance, pride, or social pressures; parents and children struggle to understand one another across changing values; friends who once imagined a shared future find their paths diverging. Yet the characters’ stories repeatedly reconnect. A chance meeting, an old melody, a remembered promise, or a small act of kindness reveals that even relationships strained by time have not necessarily disappeared. The musical treats history not as a distant sequence of public events but as something felt in kitchens, streets, workplaces, and family gatherings—where people decide whom to protect, what to sacrifice, and whether to begin again.

The central movement is therefore one of accumulation: individual moments of love, grief, resentment, and forgiveness gradually form a larger portrait of a society in motion. By the end, the characters’ separate lives suggest that personal happiness is fragile but renewable, sustained by the human capacity to remember, reconcile, and offer love without demanding certainty in return.

The show’s themes are endurance, memory, and the many forms love takes across a lifetime—romantic, familial, communal, and compassionate. It asks how ordinary people preserve connection while history changes the world they thought they knew.

阴天.en:
At four o’clock on the morning of 4 August 1926, the Kanpu ferry crosses the strait between Shimonoseki and Busan. On board are playwright Kim Woo-jin and soprano Yun Sim-deok, whose disappearance before daybreak frames the action. Their final hours unfold alongside memories of Tokyo in 1921, when the unnamed Man first insinuates himself into their lives. He approaches Woo-jin as a fellow student and encourages the restless young writer to create a new play, Death Song. He then brings Woo-jin into contact with Sim-deok, a gifted music student whose voice and independence immediately captivate him.

The Man does not remain a benign matchmaker. He hovers at the edge of their collaboration, directing conversations, provoking suspicions, and seeming to know each person’s unspoken fears. Woo-jin and Sim-deok become artistic partners and gradually fall in love, finding in one another a rare companion who understands the cost of making art in a constricting world. Yet their attachment cannot remain private. Woo-jin’s marriage, Sim-deok’s public reputation, and the social judgment surrounding them turn love into a source of exposure and danger. The Man exploits every fracture, revealing what has been concealed and driving the pair to question whether their feelings, their work, and even their choices have ever truly belonged to them.

As the ferry’s journey advances toward dawn, past and present close in on each other. The Man’s role grows ever more unsettling: narrator, instigator, witness, and possible architect of the tragedy. Woo-jin and Sim-deok struggle to preserve a future beyond disgrace and confinement, while the ship carries them through darkness toward an uncertain escape. Their disappearance at sea leaves no settled explanation, only the lingering possibility that the ending was both a desperate choice and the culmination of forces that had long been steering them there.

The musical explores love as both refuge and peril, and art as a fragile assertion of freedom. It sets personal desire against social control, asking where fate ends and individual responsibility begins.

treadmill.en:
At the premium hand car-wash Washing Zone, A spends each day polishing expensive cars while trying to repay the crushing debt left by his parents. His work is ruled by a humiliating system: customers watch from the lounge above and can press a red button to complain, with every press cutting ten percent from A’s weekly wages. Trapped in this routine, A begins to sense an inexplicable foul smell clinging to him—an outward sign of the shame, fear, and exhaustion he has learned to endure. His one private fixation is Lila, a wealthy customer whose glamorous world seems permanently beyond his reach.

Then B arrives: affluent, volatile, and carrying the same strange smell. B refuses A’s habits of submission and repeatedly provokes him to ask why he accepts a life designed to grind him down. When A discovers a scratch on Lila’s car, the accident threatens his job and his already precarious existence. It is then that B approaches him with a dangerous proposition: target people who appear powerful, wealthy, and morally disposable; use their secrets against them; take back the money that the world has withheld.

Initially appalled, A gradually accepts B’s logic. The pair return to Washing Zone and cross a succession of ethical boundaries—intimidating those who mistreat A, blackmailing chosen victims, and turning resentment into escalating violence. In the exhilaration of their escape from ordinary powerlessness, A tells B about the fire that killed his family. As B urges ever more ruthless revenge, A confronts what B truly represents. The apparent partnership fractures, and A’s account of their night proves unstable: B may be less an independent companion than the furious, destructive self A has created to survive an intolerable reality.

The musical examines economic humiliation, class resentment, and the seductive promise that violence can restore dignity. It asks whether escape from an unjust system is possible when rebellion itself may reproduce the destruction it seeks to defeat.

6點下班.en:
At the confectionery company Afternoon, Promotional Team 2 receives an ultimatum: unless it can revive the fading sales of the long-neglected Autumn Moon Bread, the team will be dissolved. The deadline is short, the budget is meagre, and every employee understands that the order threatens more than a project—it threatens their security, their routines, and the fragile lives they support outside the office. With conventional celebrity marketing beyond reach, the team lands on a risky alternative: they will become the campaign. They form an employee band, 6 PM Clock-Off, and use their rehearsals, performances, and a newly written promotional song to make Autumn Moon Bread visible again.

The group brings together people whose office identities initially conceal private ambitions and pressures. Choi Da-yeon is capable, organised, and determined to protect both her work and love life. Yoon Ji-seok, a sharp, sceptical perfectionist, keeps his feelings guarded but is drawn back toward music and the possibility of writing his own songs. Ahn Sung-joon shoulders the responsibilities of raising four-year-old twins; Seo Young-mi balances work with single motherhood; and long-serving manager Noh Joo-yeon carries the loneliness and compromises accumulated over two decades at the company. The younger employees, including timid contract worker Jang Bo-go, once an aspiring singer-songwriter, and enthusiastic intern Go Eun-ho, add their own uncertainty about work, opportunity, and the future.

As the team learns to play together, rehearsals create friction, comic mishaps, and unexpected solidarity. Their campaign begins to attract attention, growing from a desperate corporate assignment into a space where they can speak honestly through music. Yet success brings no simple escape from deadlines, employment insecurity, family demands, or the fear that pursuing a dream may be impractical. By facing those pressures collectively, the members find the nerve to reconsider the futures they had quietly postponed.

The musical is about ordinary workers recovering voice, companionship, and self-belief inside a system that often reduces them to results and deadlines. It celebrates music as a shared act that can turn workplace survival into a chance to remember what makes life feel alive.

小说.en:
In the editorial room where his serialized fiction takes shape, the acclaimed novelist Han Da-kui is found dead, having seemingly died exactly as the ending he had just written prescribed. His most talked-about work centres on a shadowy figure—a black shadow born on the page that appears to mirror its own author—and, disturbingly, the crimes the novel describes begin to occur in the real world. The public, half-terrified and half-enthralled, devours the unfolding story, no longer able to tell where fiction ends and reality begins.

The last person known to have been with Han is White, his devoted editor, who together with the unfinished manuscript becomes the final witness to the writer's death. When a detective arrives to reconstruct Han's last days, White must recount a relationship he has kept guarded: the charged intimacy of editing a genius whose pages seemed to anticipate reality, turning the people around him and his own private wounds into material. As White retraces remembered conversations and unpublished drafts, each disclosure shifts the meaning of that final meeting—an argument can sound like a confession, an act of care like a betrayal, a manuscript like either evidence or invention.

The closer the investigation comes, the more the line between the novel and the death dissolves. Was the black shadow a real killer, a mask that Han created, or a truth the people around him helped to write?
