White may never have merely edited Han's words; he may have helped shape the very story that now judges him. Han's death resists a single explanation not because there are no answers, but because every answer belongs to someone telling a story—and every storyteller has something to conceal.

Staged as an immersive mystery set inside the novel's editorial room, the piece explores authorship, obsession, and the dangerous intimacy between a creator and the person entrusted with his work, asking whether truth can survive when memory, guilt, and fiction keep rewriting one another.

apollonia.en:
In 1920s Manhattan, Richard and Oscar are a comic vaudeville duo at the Apollonia Inn & Bar: Richard is its dazzling Kid Show star, while Oscar is the singing waiter who shares his act. Their partnership is threatened when an unruly drunk provokes Oscar. Richard rushes to defend his friend, the quarrel turns into a brawl, and the two performers are thrown out of the Apollonia—the only stage that has ever felt like home. They drift between theatres, taking whatever work they can find, but the city offers little comfort and their prospects grow dim. Then a newsboy hands them an unsold paper carrying an announcement: Apollonia’s newly arrived star is seeking a singing-and-dancing chorus. Oscar presses the reluctant Richard to audition, and their chance to return reunites them with the place they thought they had lost.

Back at Apollonia, Richard prepares a special performance for Oscar’s birthday, trying to turn their renewed engagement into a celebration of their friendship and their shared life onstage. The night is interrupted by the arrival of a Mafia soldier, whose presence drags the performers into danger and forces them to confront what Apollonia means beyond its footlights. Amid songs, comic role-playing, and escalating tension, the musicians’ professional masks give way to their personal longings: Richard’s devotion to performance, Oscar’s need for belonging and recognition, and the fragile loyalty that has kept them together. The bar becomes both a haven and a battleground, where old resentments, ambitions, and fears must be aired before Richard and Oscar can decide whether their partnership is merely an act—or the family they have chosen.

At its heart, Apollonia explores friendship forged through artistic collaboration, and the way a stage can become a refuge for people with nowhere else to belong. It also asks whether dreams and loyalty can survive when power, violence, and changing circumstances intrude on a cherished world.

moon sorbet.en:
On a sweltering summer night, everyone in the apartment block huddles under the air conditioning to keep cool—while up in the sky, the moon begins to melt, drop by drop. The kind-hearted resident-committee granny is the first to hear that mysterious dripping and discover the astonishing change.

Unwilling to let it go to waste, she gathers the melted moon-water drop by drop and makes it into a cool sherbet, while the moon rabbits, their home now lost, drift down to Earth in search of a new one. Behind the cool fairy tale hides a quiet reminder about global warming and the environment.

Adapted from Korean picture-book author Baek Hee-na's Dalshabet, this licensed family musical from C MUSICAL runs a brisk sixty minutes, letting grown-ups and children alike, amid neighborly warmth, think about our relationship with this planet.

south pacific.en:
On a war-torn island in the South Pacific during World War II, U.S. Navy nurse Ensign Nellie Forbush falls in love with Emile de Becque, an older French plantation owner who has made the island his home. Emile, a widower, lives with his two young children, Ngana and Jerome, whose mother was Polynesian. Although Nellie is charmed by Emile’s warmth and the beauty of his estate, she recoils when she learns the children’s heritage, unable to overcome the racial prejudices ingrained in her upbringing. Heartbroken, Emile sends Nellie away, while the war presses closer to the island.

Meanwhile, Lieutenant Joseph Cable arrives with a dangerous intelligence assignment: he must work with the island’s inhabitants to locate a Japanese base. Cable meets Bloody Mary, a Tonkinese trader who hopes he will marry her educated, gentle daughter, Liat. Cable and Liat fall deeply in love, but Cable, like Nellie, cannot imagine bringing a mixed-race wife home to the United States. He leaves Liat despite their mutual devotion.

As the Allied forces prepare a reconnaissance mission, Emile offers to join Cable in sailing through dangerous waters to observe the Japanese installation. Their information is vital to an impending American attack. Before departing, Emile asks Nellie to care for his children. Spending time with Ngana and Jerome forces Nellie to confront the cruelty and emptiness of her prejudice. She realizes that she loves both the children and their father, and resolves to reject the fears she has inherited.

Cable is killed during the mission, devastating Liat and Bloody Mary. Emile survives, but Nellie initially does not know his fate. When he finally returns home after the successful operation, Nellie runs to him. She embraces Emile and joins him with Ngana and Jerome at the piano, accepting them as her family.

The musical examines how love can be obstructed by learned racism, social expectations, and the violence of war. It contrasts the longing for home and happiness with the moral choices demanded by intimacy, responsibility, and human connection.

德拉拉牙科診所.en:
When the clock strikes midnight, a very unusual dental clinic opens its doors. No one should be alarmed that its dentist, Delara, is a vampire—for at Delara Dental Clinic every patient is welcome, however strange their teeth or however great their fear of the dentist's chair. Alongside a nurse comically terrified of garlic, Delara greets each night visitor with reassuring magic, lively songs, and endless patience.

The night brings a parade of extraordinary patients. A grand old lady whose fangs have worn away needs a set of dentures; a zoo crocodile has tunnelled through the night to fix his crooked buck teeth; an ear of corn is unhappy about its yellow kernels; ghosts and spirits drift in with aches they are too shy to explain. Even a thief who climbs over the wall turns out to have a mouth full of cavities—and rather than turning him away, the clinic welcomes him too, treating his toothache like anyone else's. Each patient arrives frightened, but Delara and the garlic-fearing nurse listen, uncover what is really wrong, and turn a scary appointment into a warm, funny adventure.

As the treatments unfold—with plenty of comic mishaps and sing-along songs—the visitors discover that facing a toothache is far less frightening than hiding from it, and that a little courage (and a toothbrush) goes a long way. By dawn, the once-terrified patients leave with brighter, healthier smiles.

Adapted from Yoon Dam-yo's beloved Korean picture book, this family musical turns the dreaded trip to the dentist into a playful, reassuring celebration of courage, kindness, and the simple habit of caring for one's teeth. With performers stepping off the stage to sing and play with the audience, it invites even the most nervous young theatregoers to open wide and smile.

那個女人是誰.en:
In famine-stricken Moab, Ruth’s life is shattered when her husband dies, leaving her a young widow alongside her mother-in-law Naomi and sister-in-law Orpah. Naomi, stripped of her husband and both sons, resolves to return to Bethlehem, where she has heard that food has returned. She urges the two younger women to remain in Moab and rebuild their lives. Orpah reluctantly accepts the farewell, but Ruth refuses to abandon Naomi. Defiant, resourceful, and far from a passive heroine, she chooses the dangerous road to Bethlehem and vows to share Naomi’s future, whatever it may hold.

Their arrival brings no easy welcome. Naomi is consumed by grief and bitterness, insisting that the woman who left Bethlehem has not returned. Ruth, meanwhile, is marked as an outsider: a widowed Moabite with no secure place in the community and no means of support. To keep them alive, she enters the harvest fields to glean the leftovers behind the reapers. There she encounters Boaz, a prosperous landowner whose generosity is matched by attentiveness. He notices the stranger working relentlessly in the heat, learns of her devotion to Naomi, and orders his workers to protect her and leave extra grain within her reach.

Ruth’s labour gradually restores dignity and hope to the two women’s household. Naomi, recognizing a possible future for Ruth, urges her to seek Boaz’s protection directly at the threshing floor. Ruth takes the risk, and Boaz responds with honour rather than rejection. Yet another relative has a prior claim to redeem the family’s land and future. In a public settlement at the town gate, Boaz secures that right, choosing to take responsibility for Ruth and Naomi when another man declines. Ruth and Boaz marry, and the household once defined by bereavement is renewed with the birth of a son.

The musical traces how loss, displacement, and social exclusion can be transformed through courage, steadfast love, and practical compassion. It centres women who sustain one another across generations, while presenting hope not as an escape from hardship but as a future patiently built through loyalty and decisive action.

民王.en:
Prime Minister Taizan Muto has only just taken office when an impossible crisis overturns both his public life and his private one: he and his feckless university-student son, Sho Muto, suddenly exchange minds and bodies. With no explanation for the phenomenon and no time to reveal the truth, Sho must inhabit his father’s body and appear before the National Diet as Japan’s head of government, while Taizan is stranded in the life of the son he has scarcely understood.

For Sho, accustomed to spending his days idly rather than studying politics, the role is a spectacular ordeal. He cannot follow parliamentary debates or hostile questioning, and he repeatedly misreads even the kanji in official documents. His startlingly unstatesmanlike conduct shocks the public and leaves Taizan’s staff struggling to prevent a national embarrassment. Yet Sho’s new position also forces him to confront the human consequences hidden behind the formal language, discipline, and ritual of political power.

Taizan, meanwhile, must pass as Sho and attend the job interview intended for his son. He approaches it with the forceful, imperious instincts of a career politician, speaking his mind without restraint until the meeting collapses into a quarrel. Each man therefore fails at the other’s life in ways that expose the distance between them: the father’s authority proves useless in the uncertain world his son faces, while the son’s carefree habits become untenable beneath the weight of government.

To outsiders, the Prime Minister’s bewildering behavior invites outrage and criticism; no one imagines that father and son have traded bodies. Then a scandal erupts around Taizan, deepening the disorder and raising the stakes for both men. As they attempt to contain the political fallout, protect those around them, and survive their reversed lives, Taizan and Sho begin tracing the truth behind the swap itself.

At heart, the musical is about empathy earned through enforced perspective: a father and son must live one another’s burdens before they can truly see each other. Its political comedy also asks whether power can remain humane when those in charge are disconnected from ordinary lives.

白爪草.en:
At closing time, Ao Shirotsubaki remains in the small workroom behind the flower shop where she has built a modest, carefully ordered life. The flowers around her suggest gentleness and renewal, yet the room becomes a sealed arena when her identical twin, Beni Shirotsubaki, arrives. Beni has just been released after serving six years in prison for murdering their mother. Ao has spent those years trying to live beyond the crime and the stigma attached to it; nevertheless, urged by her counsellor, Kikyō-sensei, she agrees to face the sister she has kept at a distance.

Their reunion begins under the weight of shared childhood memories, sisterly devotion, fear, resentment, and the unbearable question neither woman can evade: what truly happened on the night their mother died? Beni does not simply ask for forgiveness or a place in Ao’s life. In the flower-filled back room, she begins to challenge the accepted story of the killing, drawing Ao back through the sisters’ intertwined past and exposing how much of their adult identities has been shaped by the tragedy. Her account makes the certainty of Beni’s guilt—and Ao’s innocence—feel increasingly unstable.

Then Beni makes her devastating proposal: they should exchange lives. Because the twins are indistinguishable, she argues, they can trade not only appearances but also the futures assigned to them: Beni can take Ao’s freedom and ordinary happiness, while Ao can inherit the punishment, isolation, and identity of the convicted sister. As the encounter intensifies, the question shifts from who committed the murder to who was truly meant to be harmed, and whether either sister can separate her own desires from the other’s. The suspense turns on each revelation, each remembered wound, and the terrible intimacy of two people who know exactly how to become one another.

The musical explores identity as both refuge and prison: the twins’ resemblance offers escape, but also makes an independent self difficult to claim. Beneath its murder mystery lies a story of guilt, survival, sisterly love, and the painful choices people make in pursuit of their own happiness.

ロボット イン ザ ガーデン 東京.en:
In a near-future England where sleek androids perform the work of everyday life, Ben lives in a country house with his capable lawyer wife, Amy. Since the death of his parents, he has drifted through life without purpose, leaving Amy increasingly isolated and resentful. One morning, Ben discovers an antiquated, battered robot in their garden: a small, box-shaped figure who can speak only haltingly and calls himself Tang. Unlike the efficient machines everyone else takes for granted, Tang is fragile, temperamental, and seemingly obsolete. Yet Ben is immediately drawn to him. He feeds Tang’s curious appetites, protects him from Amy’s impatience, and begins to treat the robot less as an appliance than as a companion in need of care.

Amy sees Tang as one more excuse for Ben to avoid responsibility. When Ben declares that he will repair the robot rather than dispose of him, the conflict in their marriage finally breaks open. Amy leaves, and Ben is left with both the pain of her departure and the urgent problem of Tang’s failing power cylinder. Clues on Tang’s body send Ben and Tang across the world—through America and beyond—in search of the robot’s maker and a way to save him.

As their journey unfolds, Ben discovers that Tang’s history is far more personal than he expected. Along the way, Tang’s childlike directness, mischief, and unwavering attachment force Ben to confront his own grief, cowardice, and dependence on others. Caring for Tang teaches him how to act decisively and to recognize what Amy’s love and patience have meant to him. When the truth about Tang’s creation emerges, Ben faces a choice between protecting the little robot who has become family and returning home prepared to repair the life he abandoned.

At heart, the musical explores how care creates connection, whether its recipient is human or machine. It follows Ben’s movement from emotional paralysis to responsibility, and shows love as something sustained through attention, courage, forgiveness, and the willingness to change.

rrr takarazuka rama.en:
In 1920, as British rule tightens its grip on India, unrest swells across the country. At a demonstration outside Delhi, A. Rama Raju—an Indian officer serving in the British police—single-handedly forces his way through a crowd and arrests its leader. His apparent loyalty to the colonial authorities masks a private purpose: Rama seeks promotion to Special Agent, granting him access to the police armoury. He intends to seize its weapons for the Indian people, fulfilling the mission inherited from his father. Leaving his beloved Sita behind, and supported uneasily by his uncle Venkateswarlu, Rama buries his feelings beneath disciplined service.

Far to the south, in the forests of Adilabad, the Gond community lives in peace until Viceroy Scott and Catherine encounter the young girl Malli. Treating her as something they can possess, they take her away to Delhi. Determined to bring her home, the Gond guardian Komaram Bheem enters the colonial capital in secret. The British authorities learn that he has come for Malli and promise advancement to the officer who captures him. Rama accepts the assignment, knowing that success may finally place the armoury within his reach.

Before either man knows the other’s identity, Rama and Bheem meet amid a blaze on a riverbank. A boy is trapped by fire and rising water; without exchanging more than a glance, the two men act together, risking their lives to save him. Their instinctive trust grows into an intense friendship. Rama finds in Bheem a fearless companion, while Bheem sees in Rama a man of extraordinary courage. Yet each is concealing the very cause that places him on the other’s path: Bheem must rescue Malli, and Rama must arrest the unknown Gond guardian.

When Rama discovers who Bheem is, friendship collides with duty. Their choices draw Sita, Malli, and those caught beneath colonial power into a conflict in which love, loyalty, and liberation demand a painful price.

The musical explores brotherhood forged across opposing obligations, and the cost of pursuing freedom under oppression. It asks whether devotion to a cause can coexist with personal love and human loyalty.

aoharu.en:
The musical unfolds as a lively, stop-start journey across Japan’s rail network, where every railway line appears in human form and speaks with the pride, fatigue, rivalries, and peculiar habits of the route it represents. Rather than following one hero toward a single destination, the show assembles a crowded timetable of encounters: the dependable but self-important Tokaido Shinkansen sweeps in at speed, while the Sanyo Shinkansen answers with equal confidence; the Tokaido Main Line carries the burden of long history, and the Keihin-Tohoku Line wrestles with the daily pressures of serving an overfull metropolitan corridor.

Each scene functions like a short connecting service. Lines compare their roles, complain about delays and disruptions, boast about prestige, negotiate transfers, and react to the practical realities that define their identities. The Utsunomiya Line, Tobu Tojo Line, Seibu Ikebukuro Line, Yurakucho Line, Rinkai Line, Saikyo Line, Takasaki Line, and others enter not as background geography but as personalities whose friendships and arguments are shaped by where they run, whom they connect with, and the passengers they must carry. A seemingly ordinary operational problem—congestion, a weak overhead line, an inconvenient connection, an overambitious expansion, or the demand to cover for another route—can become the spark for a comic confrontation or a song.

The omnibus structure allows the action to jump rapidly between city centres, suburban edges, long-distance corridors, Shinkansen routes, and private railways. One vignette may turn a historical grievance into melodrama; the next turns commuter inconvenience into a group number; another lets competing lines stage a flamboyant declaration of superiority. There is no final mystery to solve: momentum comes from the continual arrival of new personalities and the way individual complaints gradually reveal a shared system. Even when they clash, the lines must coexist, interchange, and keep Japan moving.

At heart, the show treats rail travel as a comic social world: a vast network made of personalities who are proud of their territories yet dependent on one another. Its themes are connection, rivalry, endurance, and the hidden labor behind an ordinary journey.

belle epoque.en:
In the early 1970s, only a few years after humanity’s first landing on the Moon, veteran astronaut Oscar trains relentlessly at the American space agency after being selected for the Apollo 18 crew. To him, the coming mission represents more than professional advancement: it is the chance to stand on the lunar surface and fulfil a dream that has guided his life. Oscar is respected among his fellow astronauts, men who have endured the demanding official path into the programme and take pride in the discipline, risk, and sacrifice that spaceflight requires.

Then the agency announces a new initiative to train women astronauts. Its first candidates are drawn from the prizewinners of a women pilots’ air race, led by the champion, Milana. The established astronauts react with anger, seeing the decision as a political intervention and an affront to the standards by which they earned their positions. Speaking for his colleagues, Oscar protests. Agency leaders dismiss his objections, arguing that the enormously expensive Apollo programme needs a new element capable of holding the public’s attention and sustaining national support.

Milana and the other women join the astronauts’ training. At first, Oscar and Milana meet as adversaries: he regards her arrival as a threat to the mission’s integrity, while she must prove that her skill, courage, and ambition are not merely a publicity device. Yet the rigours of preparation force them to confront one another as people rather than symbols. As they train together, Oscar comes to understand the depth of Milana’s longing for the Moon, and mutual respect gradually softens their hostility into a profound personal bond. Their growing closeness suggests that the lunar dream can belong to more people than the institution once allowed.

Just as that new trust begins to take hold, Milana is abruptly arrested on suspicion of espionage. Her detention throws the programme, Oscar’s loyalties, and the possibility of Apollo 18 into turmoil, placing their shared dream under the shadow of political fear and suspicion.

The musical explores the cost of reaching for an ideal when institutions demand conformity, spectacle, and certainty. It sets hope against prejudice and distrust, asking who is permitted to dream of the Moon—and what people must risk to make that dream real.

buena vista.en:
In the turbulent final years of the Tokugawa shogunate, when the growing presence of foreign powers exposes the fragility of Japan’s old order, Taketo Akane is born into a physician’s family on Hashirajima in the Chōshū domain. Determined to rise as a samurai and find a purposeful place in his country’s future, he travels to Hagi and seeks instruction at Yoshida Shōin’s Shōka Sonjuku academy. There he encounters Shinsaku Takasugi, the brilliant son of a high-ranking samurai house. The two young men are drawn into the same political awakening, but they could hardly be more different: Taketo believes that persuasion and language can unite people, while Shinsaku insists that a decaying age can be overturned only through decisive action, even at the risk of one’s life. Their arguments are fierce, yet their clashing convictions gradually deepen into respect, and then into an unbreakable comradeship.

After Shōin’s death, Shinsaku establishes the Kiheitai, a revolutionary force that rejects rigid class distinctions. Inspired by its promise of a new society, Taketo devotes himself to its cause. But Chōshū is increasingly divided by factional struggle, and when Shinsaku disappears from the political scene, Taketo unexpectedly inherits the heavy responsibility of commander of the Kiheitai. In Shimonoseki, he finds solace in the company of a geisha whose affection offers a fragile refuge from violence and uncertainty. As conflict tears the domain apart, Taketo refuses to abandon his hope that Chōshū can be reconciled from within rather than sacrificed to endless bloodshed. His pursuit of peace, however, breeds suspicion among former allies and drives a painful wedge between him and Shinsaku, forcing both men to confront what loyalty, courage, and revolution truly demand.

The musical portrays a young patriot whose ideals flicker like heat haze amid the violence of the Bakumatsu. It explores friendship tested by opposing convictions, the human cost of political change, and love’s brief consolation in an unstable world.

diamond impulse.en:
In the glittering world of Tokyo’s elite, the celebrated jewel collector Iwase has acquired the “Star of Egypt,” a diamond of extraordinary value—and immediately receives a challenge from the infamous phantom thief known as the Black Lizard. Determined to seize the jewel and fascinated by danger, she sets her sights not only on Iwase’s treasure but also on his beautiful daughter, Sanae, whom she sees as another rare possession to claim. Alarmed, Iwase calls upon the brilliant private detective Akechi Kogorō, whose calm intelligence and flair for disguise have made him the Black Lizard’s most formidable opponent.

The Black Lizard answers his protection with audacity. Using elaborate impersonations, secret passageways, hired criminals, and carefully staged deceptions, she abducts Sanae and draws Akechi into a succession of traps across Tokyo and its shadowy waterfront. Her hidden lair reveals the full extent of her obsession with beauty: she preserves exquisite objects, rare gems, and human beings as though they were works of art, arranging her captives within a private world governed by her own sensual and cruel aesthetic. Sanae becomes the centrepiece of her most dangerous scheme, while the Black Lizard plots to exchange the girl for the Star of Egypt and humiliate the detective who has repeatedly frustrated her.

Yet the contest between Akechi and the Black Lizard becomes more intimate than either expects. Akechi penetrates her disguises and turns her own theatrical tricks against her, but he is drawn to the intelligence, courage, and lonely grandeur beneath her criminal mask. The Black Lizard, accustomed to controlling everyone around her, finds herself increasingly unable to treat Akechi merely as an enemy. As the police close in and her plans begin to collapse, she must choose between escape, triumph, and the dangerous feeling that has grown from their pursuit.

The musical explores the allure of disguise, beauty, and forbidden desire. At its heart is a tragic contest in which hunter and hunted recognise themselves in one another, even as their opposing worlds make a shared future impossible.

魔法使いの約束.en:
In a world where humans and wizards live uneasily side by side, A young person is summoned from modern Japan to become the Sage: the person destined to unite twenty-one powerful wizards before the Great Calamity arrives. Each year, the enormous moon called the Great Calamity descends upon the world, bringing devastation that only the Sage and the Sage’s Wizards can resist. Thrust into this unfamiliar realm, Akira is introduced to wizards divided among the Central, Northern, Eastern, Western, and Southern Countries—companions whose rivalries, wounds, loyalties, and dangerous abilities make unity far from certain.

In the Central Country, Arthur seeks to become a king worthy of his people, guided by the formidable Oz and supported by Cain and Riquet. In the North, Snow and White conceal ancient wisdom beneath their playful manner, while Mithra, Owen, and Bradley embody the region’s harsher, more volatile power. The East carries the weight of grief and vengeance through Faust, Shino, Heathcliff, and Nero; the West is shaped by beauty, desire, memory, and illusion in the lives of Shylock, Murr, Chloe, and Rustica; and the South offers a gentler but no less complicated community around Figaro, Rutile, Lennox, and Mithile. Akira must learn their names, histories, and fears—not merely command them—because the Sage’s strength depends on forming a genuine bond with each wizard.

As preparations for the approaching moon expose old conflicts and hidden pain, the group faces threats that test whether wizards and humans can trust one another at all. The wizards train, quarrel, protect one another, and confront the consequences of their past choices, while Akira gradually understands that saving the world cannot be reduced to magical force. To oppose the Great Calamity, the scattered wizards must choose to stand together, answering the Sage’s call with a shared promise to protect the fragile world beneath the moon.

The musical is ultimately about connection across fear, prejudice, distance, and loss. It presents hope not as an easy miracle, but as something created when damaged people choose understanding and solidarity over isolation.

stage tsurugi.en:
In early summer 1941, Sakura Amamiya is dispatched to Kyoto under orders from Sumire Kanzaki to investigate an ominous threat capable of endangering all Japan. Her search takes her to Arashiyama, where the city’s mystical calm has been broken by a succession of “sword-hunting” crimes: celebrated blades are being stolen one after another. The thefts are more than ordinary robberies. In a city shaped by spiritual power, each missing sword suggests a deeper design—and the danger surrounding the case soon proves to be as real as it is uncanny.

While pursuing one of the stolen weapons, Sakura encounters Asagi Todo, the sole daughter of the secretive Todo family. Carrying two blue-glowing swords, Asagi is a living sword-wielding weapon who has devoted herself to destroying the demons concealed within Kyoto. Their meeting brings together Sakura’s mission to protect the country and Asagi’s intensely personal battle to defend her city, but it also draws them into the unresolved burdens attached to the Todo name and its future.

The investigation gathers an unlikely alliance around them: Shirahime Okita, the proud heiress of the ancient Okita family, accompanied by her fiercely loyal attendants Shizuka and Shiori; Hagane Hijikata, the abrasive but brilliant physician beloved by Arashiyama; Zuying He, an ageless-looking member of the Shanghai Combat Revue whose long experience gives her unusual insight; and Juri Sawada, an energetic newspaper reporter able to capture photographs that should be impossible to take. As clues emerge from stolen blades, mysterious images, and Kyoto’s hidden spiritual currents, their separate talents become essential to understanding the crisis.

Their opponents are the Wolves, led by the Death Gods Shungaku Harada and Izumi Sannan. As the Arashiyama Iroha Group and the Wolves move toward open conflict, the struggle forces Asagi and Sakura to confront not only armed enemies, but also the purpose of power, inheritance, and the sword each person chooses to wield.

At its heart, the show is about choosing one’s own duty rather than merely inheriting it. It frames friendship and trust as forces that can turn lonely resolve into a shared protection for a threatened city.

tiger and bunny.en:
In Stern Bild, professional heroes are public celebrities whose rescues and arrests are broadcast on Hero TV, with corporate sponsors rewarding success. Veteran hero Wild Tiger—Kotetsu T. Kaburagi—has built his career on rushing toward anyone in danger, even when the collateral damage and lost points frustrate his employers. When Apollon Media reorganizes its hero division, Kotetsu is ordered to partner with Barnaby Brooks Jr., the brilliant new hero known as Bunny. Barnaby possesses the same Hundred Power as Wild Tiger, but approaches hero work with cool precision, a concern for ratings, and an openly stated desire to find the person responsible for his parents’ murder.

Their partnership begins badly. Kotetsu’s impulsiveness clashes with Barnaby’s calculation, and their attempts to solve cases together become competitions over methods, publicity, and credit. Yet amid public missions, training, and the relentless spectacle surrounding Hero TV, the other heroes—Blue Rose, Rock Bison, Sky High, Dragon Kid, Origami Cyclone, and Fire Emblem—are drawn into a mounting crisis. A dangerous criminal plot threatens Stern Bild’s citizens and exposes how easily the city’s heroic image can be manipulated. As the danger escalates, Kotetsu and Barnaby must decide whether they will keep treating each other as obstacles or trust the strengths the other brings to the fight.

Barnaby’s personal investigation deepens the conflict. His memories and his longing for justice make him vulnerable to deception, while Kotetsu’s experience tells him that saving lives cannot wait for a clean, satisfying answer. Their allies confront the same question from different angles: are heroes performers competing for sponsors and public approval, or people who accept responsibility when no camera is watching? In the decisive confrontation, the team’s survival depends on cooperation rather than individual fame. Kotetsu and Barnaby finally fight in concert, protecting Stern Bild and proving that their mismatched partnership can become a genuine bond.

The show centres on trust forged through conflict, and on the difference between public image and real heroism. It argues that justice requires compassion, teamwork, and the willingness to protect others even when recognition is uncertain.

road to legend.en:
In a near-future Japan where hip-hop has become a national obsession, rappers wield Phantom Metal—accessories that react to their DNA and emotions to project dazzling, lifelike illusions during performance. But every show carries a private cost: the visions can awaken painful memories and trauma, turning the battle stage into a place where an artist’s past is as dangerous as any rival’s verse.

At the revived legendary venue, CLUB Paradox, the storied rap duo BURAIKAN announces a new Paradox Live tournament to find the next legend. Status, background, and reputation are declared irrelevant; only a performer’s power as a Phantom Rapper matters. Eight crews answer the call, bringing radically different identities and ambitions into the arena. BAE—Allen Sugasano, Hajun Yeon, and Anne Faulkner—arrive with youthful charisma and an unapologetically global outlook. The Cat’s Whiskers, led by Naoakira Saimon alongside Yohei Kanbayashi, Ryu Natsume, and Shiki Ando, pursue victory with disciplined poise while concealing emotional fractures. From the slums, the brothers Kanata and Nayuta Yatonokami of cozmez fight not simply for acclaim, but for a future beyond hardship. Akanyatsura— Iori Suiseki, Zen Gaho, Hokusai Masaki, Satsuki Ito, and Reo Maruyama—bring the fierce loyalty of a tightly bound outlaw family.

They are joined by the bright, idealistic VISTY; the unsettling paired force of AMPRULE; the enigmatic 1Nm8; and the hard-edged Goku Luck. As the tournament proceeds through direct eliminations and a second-chance repechage route, the crews collide in performances that expose rivalries, old wounds, convictions, and unexpected affinities. Each battle demands more than technical command of rhyme and rhythm: it asks whether the performers can face the emotional images their Phantom Metal makes real. At CLUB Paradox, spectacle becomes confession, and victory means earning the right to stand at the summit of a new rap era.

The musical is about music as identity, confrontation, and survival. Its competing crews seek recognition, yet their deeper struggle is to transform trauma, loyalty, and personal history into a voice strong enough to be heard.

pandorahearts.en:
At his coming-of-age ceremony, fifteen-year-old Oz Vessalius, heir to the Vessalius dukedom, is abruptly seized by the red-cloaked Baskervilles and condemned for a sin he cannot remember committing. Cast into the Abyss—an endless, nightmarish prison inhabited by monstrous Chains—Oz encounters Alice, an amnesiac girl feared as the Blood-Stained Black Rabbit. She offers him a way out: a contract binding their fates together. Oz accepts, and they escape the Abyss, only for him to find that ten years have elapsed in the ordinary world.

The people he knew have changed. Sharon Rainsworth and her servant Xerxes Break now act through Pandora, an organization that investigates the Abyss, Chains, and the disaster known as the Tragedy of Sablier, when an entire city vanished a century earlier. Oz is also reunited with Gilbert, the devoted servant who once accompanied him as a boy. Gilbert has grown into the guarded young man called Raven, and his altered appearance and secrets make Oz confront the distance time has placed between them.

Alice remembers neither her past nor why she was imprisoned in the Abyss. Determined to restore her lost memories, Oz, Alice, and Raven pursue the fragments connected to her identity. Their search leads them into the machinery of old noble houses, forbidden contracts, and the unresolved consequences of Sablier’s destruction. The mystery of Alice’s past becomes inseparable from Oz’s own unexplained condemnation: the closer he comes to understanding the girl beside him, the more he is forced to ask what he truly is, what sin has been assigned to him, and whether the past can be escaped at all. As memories, loyalties, and identities prove unstable, the group presses onward through a world whose fate has been turning for a hundred years.

The musical is a story of self-discovery shaped by memory, guilt, and the violence of inherited history. It asks whether people defined by loss and accusation can still choose trust, companionship, and hope over the despair seemingly ordained for them.

けものフレンズ.en:
In the bright, bustling wilderness of Japari Park, the animal-girl Friends live according to their own habits and talents, turning every encounter into a game, a song, or a shared discovery. Serval, endlessly energetic and curious, roams the park with Fennec and Raccoon when an unusual problem begins to unsettle their normally cheerful home: the balance of the park seems to be wavering, and the Friends must work together to understand what has happened. Their journey brings them from open grasslands to watery shores and gathering places where different Friends make their homes, revealing a park built not on rivalry but on the pleasures of meeting someone unlike oneself.

Along the way, the trio encounters the members of PPP, the penguin performance group—Royal Penguin, Emperor Penguin, Gentoo Penguin, Rockhopper Penguin, and Humboldt Penguin—whose ambition to put on a successful show gives the adventure both rhythm and urgency. Other Friends, including Okapi, Mammoth, Sheep, White Tiger, Saber Tiger, Greater Flamingo, Raccoon Dog, Black Panther, Cheetah, and Blue Whale, each contribute a particular skill, perspective, or burst of comic confusion. Some are shy, some proud, some impatient to prove what they can do; all gradually learn that their individual strengths become most useful when offered to the group.

As misunderstandings and setbacks threaten to scatter everyone, Serval refuses to let the Friends face their worries alone. Raccoon’s determination, Fennec’s calm observation, and the penguins’ willingness to perform even when things do not go as planned help draw the wider community together. What begins as a series of small, playful encounters becomes a collective effort to protect the warmth of Japari Park. By the time the Friends gather for a final celebration, the stage fills with the proof that cooperation can transform uncertainty into a new beginning.

The musical celebrates friendship across difference, curiosity about the world, and the confidence that comes from being accepted as oneself. Its Japari Park is a place where every Friend has something distinctive to offer, and where joy grows when no one is left to solve a problem alone.

えぶりでいホスト.en:
Sekiguchi has quit his job as a life-insurance salesman and drifted into a purposeless, self-destructive slump. Wandering the city with no idea where he belongs, he spots a recruitment notice for CLUB★ONE, a host club located away from the glamorous center of Shinjuku. He applies almost on impulse. At the interview, the club’s representative and No. 1 host, Koichi, sells him on the promise of a warm, family-like workplace; before Sekiguchi can properly reconsider, he has been accepted, renamed “Hajime,” and drawn into the neon-lit world of nightlife.

Hajime quickly discovers that CLUB★ONE is anything but ordinary. Koichi projects the approachable charm of a younger-brother type despite having spent more than two decades as a host. The club’s No. 2, Ryoichi, is a former idol who turns romantic allure into a sales strategy while carrying a colossal debt. Senichi brings an intimidating, aggressively macho energy and is obsessed with mobile games. Around them are further hosts, staff, and regulars whose incompatible temperaments turn every routine shift into a fresh crisis. For Hajime, even basic questions—how to welcome a customer, invent a persona, make a sale, or survive the club’s workplace dynamics—become comic ordeals.

At first, Hajime views the job as a reckless detour populated by people no sensible person would imitate. Yet the skills he developed in insurance sales—listening closely, reading people’s anxieties, and finding the right words to make a client feel understood—begin to serve him unexpectedly well. As he faces the club’s eccentric customs and the hosts’ wildly impractical schemes, he gradually earns a place among them. What begins as a desperate attempt to escape his old life becomes a succession of absurd nights in which Hajime learns to function, connect, and laugh again.

The musical is about searching for belonging after failure and finding unexpected value in work that initially seems alien. Beneath its heightened comic chaos, it celebrates companionship, reinvention, and the small daily acts through which people make a place feel like home.

the kings donkey ears.en:
In a kingdom ruled by a fierce and capricious King, no one dares speak an unfavourable word about their sovereign. The Black Detective arrests anyone who does, while the King’s courtiers—including Lord Roast Beef, Duchess Abraham Ham, General Boiled Egg, and the Poet Chicken—survive by praising him, flattering him, and hiding what they truly think. Yet the King himself carries a humiliating secret: because of his selfishness, his ears have become large, hairy donkey ears, which he keeps concealed from the world.

Every barber summoned to cut the King’s hair discovers the secret and blurts out the forbidden truth—“The King has donkey ears!”—only to be thrown into prison. At last, only one Barber remains in town. Called to the castle, he is horrified by what he sees. Lord Roast Beef offers him release on one condition: he must never reveal the King’s ears. To ensure obedience, the court keeps the Barber’s father imprisoned and threatens his life should the Barber speak.

Back in town, the Barber becomes silent, withdrawn, and miserable. The townspeople cannot understand why he has changed, and even those who are tired of the King’s tyranny hesitate to challenge it openly. Burdened by the secret and unable to tell another person, the Barber wanders into the forest. There he confides his pain to the trees. The Spirits of the Forest answer, assuring him that they stand with him: the forest is alive, and truth is alive too. Strengthened by their encouragement, the Barber resolves to find the courage to speak honestly.

The truth begins to travel beyond the forest, reaching the King and shaking the fearful order of the court. Faced with the people and with the consequences of trying to conceal reality, the King must finally confront both his donkey ears and the cruelty he has used to protect his pride.

The musical is about the courage to tell the truth when fear makes silence seem safer. It also shows that power built on intimidation and false praise cannot last, and that admitting one’s faults opens the way to change.

浅利演出事務所主催公演 夢から醒めた夢 東京.en:
Piko, a bright, inquisitive girl who longs for adventure, is led by the Dream Messenger into an amusement park after closing time. There she meets Mako, a gentle ghost of her own age. Mako died suddenly in a traffic accident and cannot bear to leave her mother, who has been consumed by grief. She wants only one day back in the living world: enough time to comfort her mother and say goodbye properly. Moved by Mako’s devotion, Piko agrees to exchange places with her for a day. Mako returns home in Piko’s body, while Piko sets off for the Spirit-World Airport.

The airport is a strange, bustling terminal between worlds, staffed by Angel, Devil, and other officials. Its passengers await Rocket 707, the annual flight to the Land of Light. Only those with pure white passports may board. Among the waiting souls are an old man who has spent twelve years awaiting his wife, children who died in disasters and war, and spirits burdened by regrets: Meso, who took his own life after bullying; the Manager, who worked himself to death while neglecting his family; bikers killed in a reckless accident; and a gangster murdered in a fight. Their grey passports show that they must work and wait until the stains of their past are cleansed.

Piko carries Mako’s white passport in a bag and entrusts it to Meso while she goes to see the rocket. When she returns, the passport has turned black—the mark of a soul bound for Hell. Horrified that Mako may be condemned, Piko collapses. The crisis exposes Meso’s desperate theft and forces the airport’s officials to weigh wrongdoing against remorse, generosity, and the chance to change. As the departure approaches, Piko must recover Mako’s passport and return to the living world before the day of their exchange ends. Back with Mako’s mother, both girls confront the agony of separation and the cost of letting go.

The musical treats death not as an ending alone, but as a test of compassion, responsibility, and forgiveness. At its heart are Piko and Mako’s friendship, a mother’s grief, and the courage to release someone one loves.

スクールアイドルミュージカル.en:
In Kansai, two prestigious girls’ schools stand on opposite sides of an old rivalry. Tsubakisakuhana Girls’ High School in Hyōgo prides itself on tradition, academic achievement, and the expectation that its students will follow dependable paths. Across the border in Osaka, Takizakura Girls’ Academy has built a glamorous public image around its entertainment course and successful school-idol club. Their chairwomen, Madoka Tsubaki and Kyoka Takizawa, have long treated the other school as an adversary—and their daughters have inherited the pressure to uphold that conflict.

Rurika Tsubaki, the serious daughter of Tsubakisakuhana’s chairwoman, has assumed that her future is already decided: study hard, preserve the school’s reputation, and one day succeed her mother. Yet she feels an unnamed dissatisfaction with the ordinary life mapped out for her. Takizakura’s Anzu Takizawa, a polished and gifted idol performer, appears to have everything Rurika lacks: confidence, a stage, and a shining future in entertainment. Their encounter through school-idol activity draws them together despite the hostility surrounding them. Rurika is captivated by Anzu’s radiance, while Anzu finds in Rurika an earnest friend who sees more than the image she is expected to project.

Inspired by Takizakura’s performers, Rurika and her friends—Yuzuha Sumeragi, Yukino Hojo, Hikaru Amakusa, and Maaya Mikasa—form the Tsubakisakuhana Idol Club. As they learn to sing, dance, and perform, each confronts the roles assigned to her by family, school, or self-doubt. Meanwhile, Anzu’s choice to follow her own feelings disrupts Takizakura’s established order and strains her bond with Misuzu Wakatsuki, Toa Kurusu, RENA Suzuka, and Sayaka Harukaze. Competition, gossip, and parental expectations threaten to turn a shared love of performance into another battlefield between the schools. Rurika and Anzu must decide whether loyalty means preserving an inherited promise or pursuing the dreams they can create together.

At heart, the musical is about finding a self beyond the future others have planned. It celebrates friendship, creative courage, and the way a shared dream can transform rivalry into connection.

london way ivresse vague.en:
The London Way unfolds in London during a time of change, a city alive with social change, restless ambition, and the private hopes of people whose paths cross in its streets. Against this shifting urban backdrop, men and women from differing walks of life pursue work, love, dignity, and a place to belong. Their lives form an interwoven portrait of London: a metropolis where chance meetings can alter a future, old certainties are fading, and every person carries struggles that are rarely visible at first glance.

As the characters move through the city’s cafés, workplaces, homes, and public spaces, individual wishes collide with the pressures of the age. Some are determined to rise beyond the limits imposed by class, circumstance, or disappointment; others try to protect the small happiness they have managed to build. Relationships are tested by conflicting loyalties, unspoken feelings, and the difficult choices demanded by survival. Amid the bustle, humour and warmth emerge alongside frustration and loss, allowing ordinary encounters to become decisive moments in the characters’ lives.

London itself is not merely a setting but the thread that binds the ensemble together. Its energy offers promise, yet it can also leave people isolated in a crowd. As new tensions begin to simmer among the city’s many intersecting lives, each character must confront what they owe to others and what they are willing to risk for their own future. The story follows no single hero alone; instead, it gathers a mosaic of people who stumble, endure, reach out, and continue forward while the world around them changes.

Ultimately, The London Way is a human-scale drama about resilience, connection, and the quiet courage required to keep living honestly through uncertain times. It finds hope not in easy answers, but in the compassion people discover when their separate lives meet.

spyfamily 2.en:
In Musical SPY×FAMILY 2, the Forger family’s fragile domestic routine is tested by two dangerous adventures. Loid Forger, secretly the master spy Twilight, is still maintaining the false family he created for his mission; Yor Forger continues to conceal her life as a professional assassin; and their daughter Anya keeps her telepathy to herself. When Anya declares that she wants a dog, the family visits an animal-rescue adoption event. What should be a cheerful family outing becomes a national-security emergency: terrorists are preparing to assassinate a visiting Westalis foreign minister, using dogs fitted with bombs. While Loid pursues the conspiracy and Yor is drawn into the physical danger, Anya encounters a large white dog named Bond, who can foresee fragments of the future. By reading minds and interpreting Bond’s visions, Anya learns that Loid is in mortal danger. Determined to save her papa, she and Bond race to change the future, helping the Forgers avert catastrophe. In the aftermath, Bond joins the household as Anya’s long-awaited pet.

The second act takes the family aboard the luxury cruise ship Princess Lorelei. Yor has accepted a covert assignment to protect Olka Gretcher, the surviving widow of a Mafia family, and Olka’s young son as they attempt to escape the assassins hunting them. Disguised as an ordinary City Hall worker, Yor must fend off a succession of killers while hiding the true nature of her work. By coincidence, Loid and Anya win cruise tickets in a shopping-centre lottery and board the same ship, unaware of Yor’s mission. Anya discovers the threat through the thoughts of those around her and tries to aid Yor without exposing her own abilities, while Loid is pulled between caring for Anya and responding to a bomb planted aboard the vessel. As Yor battles to keep Olka and her child alive, the family’s separate struggles collide in a crisis that threatens every passenger on the ship.

The musical is ultimately about a family assembled for practical reasons that gradually becomes emotionally real. Beneath the disguises, comic misunderstandings, and high-stakes action, Loid, Yor, Anya, and Bond repeatedly choose to protect one another—and strangers in need—because they have come to care.
